SPECIAL ACT ON THE ESTABLISHMENT OF THE JEONNAM-GWANGJU INTEGRATED SPECIAL CITY

PART I GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1 (Purpose)
The purpose of this Act is to establish the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City by integrating the former Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City, based on the spirit of Gwangju, characterized by democracy, human rights, justice and peace, and the spirit of community solidarity embodied in the May 18 Democratization Movement achieved together by Gwangju Metropolitan City and Jeollanam-do, which inherited Jeolla's thousand-year history, and thereby contribute to substantial local decentralization and balanced national growth through the harmonious development of global future-oriented high-tech industries, including artificial intelligence, energy and semiconductors, and agriculture and fisheries.

Article 2 (Definition)
For the purposes of this Act, "metropolitan living zone" means an area within the jurisdiction of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as the "Integrated Special City") that extends across two or more Sis, Guns or Gus (meaning autonomous Gus; hereinafter the same shall apply), is jointly used by residents in their daily lives and entails common administrative needs beyond the boundaries of administrative districts.

Article 3 (Scope of application)
This Act shall apply only within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City under Article 7 (1).

Article 4 (Responsibilities of the State)
① The State shall take legislative and administrative measures, including continuously improving relevant statutes, to enable the Integrated Special City to resolve the problems of the single-pole metropolitan concentration system and the crisis of local extinction and to grow into a capital of artificial intelligence, energy and culture.
② Through evaluations of the Integrated Special City's operational objectives and the degree to which they have been achieved, the State shall formulate measures and policies for realizing advanced local decentralization and developing the regional economy.
③ The State shall ensure that the Integrated Special City continues to enjoy the administrative and financial benefits previously enjoyed by Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City, which are abolished upon the enforcement of this Act.
④ The State shall promptly prepare necessary administrative and financial support measures, including those expanding financial stability and autonomy, to facilitate the successful establishment of the Integrated Special City and the achievement of the purposes of its establishment.
⑤ The State shall establish an institutional foundation for expanding substantive autonomous authority, including the transfer of powers of central administrative agencies, deregulation and fiscal decentralization, so that the Integrated Special City can become a model for alleviating concentration in the Seoul metropolitan area and innovating local administration.

Article 5 (Responsibilities of the Integrated Special City)
① The Integrated Special City shall actively cooperate in the formulation and implementation of national policies relating to the Integrated Special City.
② The Integrated Special City shall take measures to enact, amend or repeal ordinances of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as "Integrated Special City ordinances") in accordance with the purpose of this Act with respect to matters which this Act requires or permits to be prescribed by ordinance.
③ The Integrated Special City shall formulate and implement balanced development plans for each region to promote balanced development within its territory.
④ The Integrated Special City shall conclude an agreement with the Prime Minister concerning its performance objectives and evaluation (including matters concerning educational autonomy). In such cases, the Prime Minister shall consult in advance with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies concerning evaluation of whether the transfer of powers from central administrative agencies, deregulation and other measures contribute to the development and growth of the Integrated Special City and concerning institutional improvements based on evaluation results.
⑤ The Integrated Special City shall formulate and implement necessary policies to inherit and develop the historical value of the former Gwangju Metropolitan City area in contributing to the development of democracy in the Republic of Korea and its brand identity as a hub city of Asian culture.

Article 6 (Relationship with other Acts)
① This Act shall prevail over other Acts with respect to the organization and operation of the Integrated Special City, transfers of powers from central administrative agencies, deregulation, etc.: Provided, That where another Act has special provisions concerning the Integrated Special City, the other Act shall govern.
② Where this Act vests powers of the heads of central administrative agencies, etc. in the Mayor of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as the "Mayor of the Integrated Special City") and the Superintendent of Education of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as the "Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City") (including duties, principles, standards, procedures, etc. relating to the transferred powers; hereinafter the same shall apply), the relevant statutes shall apply by deeming the powers of the Mayor and Superintendent of Education to be those of the heads of the relevant central administrative agencies, etc. The same shall apply where matters concerning the heads of central administrative agencies, etc. are made applicable to the Mayor of the Integrated Special City and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City.

PART II ESTABLISHMENT AND OPERATION OF THE JEONNAM-GWANGJU INTEGRATED SPECIAL CITY

CHAPTER I ESTABLISHMENT OF THE JEONNAM-GWANGJU INTEGRATED SPECIAL CITY

Article 7 (Establishment of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City)
① Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City shall each be abolished, and the Integrated Special City shall be established under the direct jurisdiction of the Government as follows, with "Gwangju Special City" as its abbreviated name:

Name: Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City
Jurisdiction: The entire area of the former Jeollanam-do and the entire area of the former Gwangju Metropolitan City.

② The Integrated Special City shall have a status comparable to that of Seoul Special Metropolitan City within the scope prescribed by this Act.
③ The Integrated Special City shall make balanced use of and operate the former Jeonnam Eastern Office, Muan Office and Gwangju Office. Notwithstanding Article 94-3 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, standards for the floor area of its offices may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance in consideration of the numbers of residents and public officials, etc.

Article 8 (Special provisions on entrustment of affairs of the Integrated Special City)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City or the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may entrust another local government, the head thereof, or a superintendent of education with the performance of part of the affairs under his or her jurisdiction and affairs delegated under statutes.
② Except as otherwise provided in this Act, the provisions on entrustment of affairs under Article 168 of the Local Autonomy Act shall apply mutatis mutandis.

Article 9 (Special provisions on Sis, Guns, Gus, etc. within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City)
① The Integrated Special City may have Sis, Guns and Gus within its jurisdiction.
② The names and jurisdictions of the Sis, Guns and Gus within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City shall be the same as those of the Sis, Guns and Gus of Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City abolished pursuant to Article 7 (1).
③ The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may designate metropolitan living zones within its jurisdiction.

Article 10 (Special provisions on status and authority of Sis, Guns and Gus within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City)
① Notwithstanding the Local Autonomy Act and other relevant statutes, Sis and Guns within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City shall retain the affairs and authority previously exercised before integration. The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall not reduce their administrative or financial authority or impose disadvantages on them on the ground of integration.
② Where the Integrated Special City receives powers or financial resources transferred from central administrative agencies under this Act, it shall formulate and implement a transfer plan for allocating and supporting powers, affairs and finances to strengthen the autonomy and administrative functions of Sis, Guns and Gus. Necessary matters shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall establish and implement measures to strengthen autonomous authority that include the following matters to address disparities in self-governance capacity between autonomous Gus and Sis/Guns within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City:
1. Measures to expand and adjust the administrative and financial autonomous authority of autonomous Gus in the former Gwangju Metropolitan City area;
2. Measures to strengthen the autonomy of autonomous Gus in initiating urban plans, exercising taxation authority, and operating organizations.
④ In principle, the affairs of the Integrated Special City shall be allocated so that Sis, Guns and Gus can handle them first to promote residents' welfare and administrative efficiency. Unless there is a special reason, such as the need to respond to metropolitan administrative demands, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall endeavor to comprehensively transfer the powers and affairs of the Integrated Special City to Sis, Guns and Gus.
⑤ With respect to affairs transferred under paragraph ④, the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu shall be deemed the competent authority under the relevant statutes.

Article 11 (Special provisions on application of other statutes following establishment of the Integrated Special City)
① Where another statute refers to a local government, metropolitan city or Do, it shall be applied by deeming the reference to include the Integrated Special City, respectively.
② Where another statute refers to members of local councils or members of metropolitan city or Do councils, it shall be applied by deeming the reference to include members of the Council of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as the "Integrated Special City Council"), respectively.
③ Where another statute refers to the head of a local government or a Metropolitan Mayor or Do Governor, it shall be applied by deeming the reference to include the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, respectively.
④ Where another statute refers to a local council or a metropolitan city or Do council, it shall be applied by deeming the reference to include the Integrated Special City Council, respectively.
⑤ Where another statute refers to ordinances or rules of a local government or a metropolitan city or Do, it shall be applied by deeming the reference to include Integrated Special City ordinances and rules of the Integrated Special City, respectively.
⑥ Where another statute refers to a superintendent of education or a superintendent of education of a City or Do, it shall be applied by deeming the reference to include the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City, respectively.
⑦ Where another statute refers to a fire headquarters or the head of a fire headquarters, it shall be applied by deeming the reference to include the Fire Headquarters of the Integrated Special City or the head thereof, respectively.
⑧ For the categories of local taxes of the Integrated Special City, Article 8 of the Framework Act on Local Taxes that previously applied to Jeollanam-do and the Sis/Guns under its jurisdiction and Gwangju Metropolitan City and the autonomous Gus under its jurisdiction shall apply; and imposition and collection of the local taxes of the Integrated Special City shall be governed by local tax-related Acts under Article 2 (1) 4 of the same Act.
⑨ The financial adjustment grants of the Integrated Special City shall be funded, in the case of autonomous Gus, from the categories of ordinary taxes of the former Gwangju Metropolitan City (excluding local consumption tax amounts under Article 71 (3) 3 (a) and 4 (a) of the Local Tax Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) and, in the case of Sis/Guns, from the categories of ordinary taxes of the former Jeollanam-do.
⑩ Notwithstanding paragraphs ① through ⑨, where a particular statute has different provisions applicable to metropolitan cities and Dos, the provisions applicable to metropolitan cities shall apply to areas under the jurisdiction of autonomous Gus and those applicable to Dos shall apply to areas under the jurisdiction of Sis/Guns until the relevant statute is amended: Provided, That where applying a statute on the basis of jurisdiction is difficult, the head of the national agency responsible for that statute may determine which of the provisions applicable to metropolitan cities or Dos shall apply to the Integrated Special City after hearing the opinion of the Mayor of the Integrated Special City (or the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City for affairs within the Superintendent's jurisdiction).

CHAPTER II ESTABLISHMENT OF THE JEONNAM-GWANGJU INTEGRATED SPECIAL CITY SUPPORT COMMITTEE AND TRANSFER OF AUTHORITY

SECTION 1 ESTABLISHMENT OF THE JEONNAM-GWANGJU INTEGRATED SPECIAL CITY SUPPORT COMMITTEE

Article 12 (Establishment of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Support Committee)
① A Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Support Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Support Committee") shall be established under the Prime Minister to deliberate on the following matters relating to the performance objectives and evaluation of the Integrated Special City and the development of a capital of artificial intelligence, energy and culture, etc., so that the Integrated Special City can achieve the purposes of this Act:
1. Formulation and implementation of the basic plan of the Integrated Special City and measures for its development;
2. Enhancing the administrative and financial autonomy of the Integrated Special City and providing administrative and financial support under Article 4 (4);
3. Conclusion of agreements under Article 5 (4) and utilization of the results of their evaluation;
4. Promotion of deregulation under Article 14;
5. Examination of opinions concerning bills submitted under Article 15;
6. Phased transfer of powers of central administrative agencies under Article 16;
7. Transfer of affairs of special local administrative agencies and measures resulting therefrom;
8. Formulation and amendment of basic plans under Article 150;
9. Promotion of educational autonomy in the Integrated Special City;
10. Consultation and coordination between the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City, and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies concerning matters under subparagraphs 1 through 9;
11. Other matters submitted for deliberation by the chairperson of the Support Committee, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, or the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City as deemed necessary.
② The Support Committee shall consist of not fewer than 25 and not more than 40 members, including one chairperson.
③ The Prime Minister shall serve as chairperson of the Support Committee, and its members shall be:
1. The Mayor of the Integrated Special City;
2. The Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City;
3. Heads of relevant central administrative agencies prescribed by Presidential Decree;
4. Persons with extensive knowledge and experience in urban development, local autonomy, or educational autonomy, appointed or commissioned by the Prime Minister.
④ A working committee shall be established to examine agenda items for deliberation by the Support Committee and handle matters delegated by the Support Committee.
⑤ The working committee under paragraph ④ shall consist of up to 25 members, including one chairperson, and the Minister for Government Policy Coordination shall serve as its chairperson.
⑥ A working support group may be established to handle and support the affairs of the Support Committee.
⑦ Except as otherwise provided in this Act, matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Support Committee and working committee and the establishment and operation of the working support group shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
⑧ The Support Committee shall continue to exist for five years from the date this Act enters into force.

Article 13 (Measures following deliberation by the Support Committee)
The Support Committee shall notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies of the results of its deliberation on matters under the subparagraphs of Article 12 (1), and the notified heads of the agencies shall take necessary measures.

SECTION 2 PROMOTION OF DEREGULATION AND TRANSFER OF POWERS OF CENTRAL ADMINISTRATIVE AGENCIES

Article 14 (Promotion of deregulation)
① The heads of central administrative agencies shall endeavor to improve regulations under the relevant statutes that apply to the Integrated Special City on a priority basis to develop the Integrated Special City into a deregulated region leading national development.
② The Integrated Special City shall prescribe by Integrated Special City ordinance basic matters for improving regulations necessary to develop a capital of artificial intelligence, energy and culture and effect major transformations in marine tourism, agriculture, fisheries, etc.
③ The ordinance under paragraph ② shall include matters concerning registration and publication of regulations prescribed by autonomous legislation, examination of the enactment or strengthening of regulations, improvement of existing regulations, and establishment of a regulatory review body.
④ The Integrated Special City shall review regulations prescribed by its autonomous legislation within a period not exceeding five years, as set by Integrated Special City ordinance, and implement regulatory reform measures, including improvements to the substance of regulations and related procedures. In such cases, regulatory reform means prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance may be used.
⑤ The Mayor of the Integrated Special City and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City shall submit the results of reviews under paragraph ④ and regulatory reform measures to the Support Committee.
⑥ Where necessary in connection with the matters under paragraphs ② through ⑤, the Support Committee may, after completing deliberation, present opinions to the Mayor of the Integrated Special City and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City.

Article 15 (Submission of opinions on bills and incorporation into legislation)
① With the consent of at least two thirds of all incumbent members of the Integrated Special City Council, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may submit to the Support Committee opinions on matters relating to the Integrated Special City that need to be reflected in Acts.
② The Support Committee shall notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies of opinions submitted under paragraph ①.
③ The heads of relevant central administrative agencies shall examine the validity of the matters notified under paragraph ②. The examination period shall not exceed two months from the date of notification.
④ The heads of relevant central administrative agencies shall notify the Support Committee of the results of the examination under paragraph ③ within seven days from the expiration of the examination period. Where a head determines that an opinion is invalid, the head shall specify the reasons and details; where the head determines that an opinion is valid, the head shall actively cooperate so that the matter is reflected in relevant Acts.
⑤ The Support Committee shall deliberate on examination results notified under paragraph ④ and notify the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City, and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies of the results of its deliberation.

Article 16 (Phased transfer of powers of central administrative agencies)
① The Support Committee shall formulate a plan to transfer affairs to the Integrated Special City in phases (hereinafter referred to as a "transfer plan"), taking into account the Integrated Special City's regional circumstances, capacity and financial capability, excluding affairs essential to the existence of the State, such as foreign affairs, national defense and judicial affairs.
② A transfer plan shall include the following matters:
1. A comprehensive survey of affairs falling within the authority of central administrative agencies as prescribed by statutes;
2. Examination and selection of affairs within the authority of central administrative agencies that are to be transferred to the Integrated Special City;
3. Final determination of the powers of central administrative agencies to be transferred to the Integrated Special City and their follow-up management;
4. Other matters necessary for efficiently promoting transfers of authority of central administrative agencies to the Integrated Special City, including administrative and financial support.
③ The Support Committee shall report a transfer plan formulated under paragraph ① to the Prime Minister and notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City thereof. The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall inform the heads of Sis, Guns and Gus (meaning autonomous Gus; hereinafter the same shall apply) of the transfer plan notified by the Support Committee.

Article 17 (Special provisions on phased transfer of affairs of the Integrated Special City and strengthening of autonomy)
① To realize decentralization and expand the autonomy of Sis, Guns and Gus, the Integrated Special City shall transfer affairs of the Integrated Special City to Sis, Guns and Gus under its jurisdiction in accordance with the criteria for allocation of affairs under Article 14 of the Local Autonomy Act, except for the following affairs:
1. Formulating and coordinating supra-regional urban plans, metropolitan transportation systems and metropolitan infrastructure;
2. Fostering region-specific industries and formulating and implementing supra-regional economic area plans;
3. Managing large-scale disasters;
4. Other affairs prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance as necessary for efficient metropolitan administration.
② An independent Jeonnam-Gwangju Local Decentralization Deliberation Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee" in this Article) shall be established under the Mayor of the Integrated Special City to identify and deliberate on affairs to be transferred to Sis, Guns and Gus under paragraph ①. The Committee shall consist of up to 20 members, including a chairperson, and a majority of its members shall be private-sector experts and persons representing the positions of Sis, Guns and Gus.
③ The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall formulate an annual implementation plan for transferring affairs, reflecting the results of deliberation by the Committee, report it to the Integrated Special City Council, and publicly announce it. The plan shall include the affairs subject to transfer, the amount of budgetary support, personnel redeployment and support measures, etc.
④ Affairs determined to be transferred to Sis, Guns and Gus under paragraphs ① through ③ may be prescribed by this Act as affairs of the Sis, Guns and Gus belonging to the Integrated Special City, notwithstanding that the Local Autonomy Act or any other Act prescribes them as affairs of the Integrated Special City.
⑤ The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall provide concurrent administrative and financial support under the implementation plan referred to in paragraph ③ so that transfer of affairs does not impose excessive financial or personnel burdens on Sis, Guns and Gus. Where the handling of transferred affairs is deemed unlawful or seriously detrimental to residents' interests, the Mayor may take minimum follow-up management measures, including corrective orders.
⑥ Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Committee, procedures for formulating implementation plans for the transfer of affairs, follow-up measures, etc., other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ⑤, shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 18 (Submission of data)
① The heads of relevant central administrative agencies may request the Mayor of the Integrated Special City to submit data necessary for nationwide statistical management or policy formulation concerning powers transferred under this Act.
② The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies to provide data and technical support necessary to exercise powers transferred under this Act.

SECTION 3 TRANSFER OF AFFAIRS OF SPECIAL LOCAL ADMINISTRATIVE AGENCIES AND DESIGNATION OF METROPOLITAN LIVING ZONES

Article 19 (Criteria for transferring affairs of special local administrative agencies)
① The following affairs of special local administrative agencies under Article 3 of the Government Organization Act (hereinafter referred to as "special local administrative agencies") established in the former Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City may be transferred to the Integrated Special City following consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies:
1. Affairs intended for the convenience of residents that must be performed locally;
2. Affairs affecting the development of the regional economy or the quality of life of local residents.
② Transfer of the affairs of special local administrative agencies under paragraph ① shall be subject to the following principles:
1. Consideration of the administrative and financial circumstances and capacity of the Integrated Special City;
2. Consideration of the position of the Integrated Special City regarding the transfer of affairs.
③ Where affairs of special local administrative agencies are transferred to the Integrated Special City under paragraphs ① and ②, all related affairs and powers shall be transferred at the same time.
④ Matters necessary for the transfer of affairs of special local administrative agencies, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ③, shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 20 (Requests for transfer of affairs of special local administrative agencies)
① Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City deems it efficient for the Integrated Special City to perform affairs of a special local administrative agency, the Mayor may request the Support Committee to deliberate on transferring the relevant affairs of that agency to the Integrated Special City.
② Upon receiving a request under paragraph ①, the Support Committee shall hear the opinions of relevant central administrative agencies concerning the proposed transfer and publicly announce the details after completing its deliberation.

Article 21 (Measures following transfer of affairs)
① The head of a central administrative agency having jurisdiction over a special local administrative agency whose affairs are transferred under Article 19 shall take measures necessary for the transfer, including administrative and financial support, such as personnel transfers, to enable the Integrated Special City to perform the transferred affairs smoothly.
② When appointing as local public officials public officials whose status changes following the transfer of affairs of a special local administrative agency, the Integrated Special City shall appoint them to grades corresponding to their previous grades notwithstanding Article 27 (2) 7 and paragraph (6) of the Local Public Officials Act.
③ The Integrated Special City may provide public officials transferred under paragraph ② with administrative and financial support and support for improving their living environments, etc.
④ The head of a central administrative agency responsible for a special local administrative agency shall share relevant administrative systems with the Integrated Special City and continuously conduct personnel exchanges to prevent disruption of duties due to the transfer of affairs.
⑤ When providing financial support under paragraph ①, the head of a relevant central administrative agency shall prepare a support plan specifying the methods and scale of support and including the following matters, and obtain deliberation by the Support Committee. The Support Committee shall hear the opinion of the Mayor of the Integrated Special City in advance:
1. Scope and details of the transferred affairs and handling procedures for each unit of affairs transferred;
2. Expenses incurred for each unit of affairs and by source of funds over the preceding three years;
3. Scale, method and timing of financial support and measures for procuring the relevant funds;
4. Other matters relating to financial support.

Article 22 (Restrictions on establishment of special local administrative agencies)
① The head of a central administrative agency shall not newly establish within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City a special local administrative agency that has been transferred to the Integrated Special City.
② Notwithstanding paragraph ①, where it is necessary to perform affairs within the jurisdiction of a central administrative agency, its head may establish a special local administrative agency following consultation with the Mayor of the Integrated Special City or the head of a Si, Gun or Gu.
③ Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City or the head of a Si, Gun or Gu consults with the head of a central administrative agency under paragraph ②, the consent of the relevant local council shall be obtained in advance.

Article 23 (Designation of metropolitan living zones)
① To meet common administrative needs of two or more Sis, Guns and Gus within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may designate all or part of the relevant Sis, Guns and Gus as a metropolitan living zone or alter the designated zone.
② To designate or alter a metropolitan living zone, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall hear the opinions of the heads of Sis, Guns and Gus within the area and obtain deliberation by the Metropolitan Living Zone Committee.
③ The heads of Sis, Guns and Gus within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City may request the Mayor of the Integrated Special City to designate or alter a metropolitan living zone.
④ Upon designating or altering a metropolitan living zone, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall notify the relevant heads of Sis, Guns and Gus thereof without delay.
⑤ Matters necessary for the establishment, composition and operation of the Metropolitan Living Zone Committee, designation and alteration of metropolitan living zones, notification, etc. shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 24 (Operation of metropolitan living zones)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may recommend that the heads of Sis, Guns and Gus within a metropolitan living zone establish a special-purpose local government under Article 199 of the Local Autonomy Act to handle common affairs of the zone.
② The head of a special-purpose local government established under paragraph ① may perform the following affairs:
1. Establishing road networks and administering public transportation within the metropolitan living zone;
2. Installing and operating public facilities within the metropolitan living zone;
3. Other affairs transferred to the special-purpose local government by agreement among its constituent local governments.
③ Details of the affairs under paragraph ② shall be prescribed by agreement.
④ Where necessary for the public interest, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may, after deliberation by the Metropolitan Living Zone Committee under Article 23 (2), coordinate functions and affairs between the Integrated Special City and the special-purpose local government. In such cases, the Mayor may provide administrative and financial support.
⑤ Where the State delegates affairs to a special-purpose local government, the State shall bear the expenses necessary to perform those affairs.
⑥ Articles 202 through 211 of the Local Autonomy Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the agreement, composition of agencies, operation, etc. of special-purpose local governments under paragraph ①.

CHAPTER III LOCAL COUNCIL

Article 25 (Status and authority of the Integrated Special City Council)
The Integrated Special City shall have an Integrated Special City Council as the representative body of citizens and as an autonomous legislative body.

Article 26 (Duties of the chairperson of the Integrated Special City Council)
The chairperson of the Integrated Special City Council shall represent the Council, arrange its proceedings, maintain order, and supervise its affairs.

Article 27 (Special provisions on administrative organization of the Integrated Special City Council)
① Notwithstanding Articles 68 (3) (excluding matters concerning grades) and 103 (2) of the Local Autonomy Act, the number of expert advisers assigned to committees of the Integrated Special City Council and matters concerning appointment of Council staff and related procedures may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② In establishing the administrative organization of the Integrated Special City Council and managing personnel quotas, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall hear the opinion of the Council's chairperson.

Article 28 (Budget of the Integrated Special City Council)
① The budget of the Integrated Special City Council shall be separately entered in the Integrated Special City's budget.
② The chairperson of the Integrated Special City Council shall prepare a budget request for the Council, submit it for review to the committee responsible for affairs concerning operation of the Council, and then submit it to the Mayor of the Integrated Special City: Provided, That where the committee fails to complete its review of the Council's budget request by 30 days before the deadline for submitting the budget bill under Article 142 (1) of the Local Autonomy Act (hereinafter referred to in this Article as the "budget submission deadline"), the chairperson may directly submit the Council's budget request to the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
③ The budget of the Integrated Special City Council shall include reserve funds.
④ Reserve funds of the Integrated Special City Council shall be managed by the head of its administrative organization and expended with the consent of the committee responsible for Council operations and the approval of the Council chairperson: Provided, That during an adjournment they may be expended with the approval of the Council chairperson, who shall report such expenditures to the committee responsible for Council operations at the beginning of the next session.
⑤ In preparing the budget of the Integrated Special City Council, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall respect to the greatest possible extent the budget request submitted by the Council chairperson.
⑥ Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City intends to reduce the amount of expenditure requested in the budget of the Integrated Special City Council, the Mayor shall seek the Council chairperson's opinion and deliver a statement specifying the details and reasons for the reduction to the chairperson by 15 days before the budget submission deadline.
⑦ Upon receiving the statement under paragraph ⑥, the Council chairperson shall deliver an opinion on the reduction to the Mayor of the Integrated Special City by seven days before the budget submission deadline.
⑧ Where the chairperson submits an opinion under paragraph ⑦, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall attach that opinion to the budget bill submitted to the Integrated Special City Council.

Article 29 (Special provisions on professional personnel supporting policy work of the Integrated Special City Council)
Notwithstanding Article 41 of the Local Autonomy Act, the State shall endeavor to increase the number of professional personnel supporting policy work to at least one half of the prescribed number of Council members, in order to facilitate legislative activities of the Integrated Special City Council.

Article 30 (Special provisions on expenses for legislative activities)
① Notwithstanding Article 40 of the Local Autonomy Act, the types of expenses payable to members of the Integrated Special City Council and the payment standards shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② A Council Members' Remuneration Deliberation Committee shall be established under the Integrated Special City to deliberate and resolve on the types of expenses and payment standards under paragraph ①.
③ Matters necessary for composition and operation of the Council Members' Remuneration Deliberation Committee under paragraph ② shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 31 (Special provisions on audits and investigations of administrative affairs)
Notwithstanding Article 49 (7) of the Local Autonomy Act, matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under that paragraph may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 32 (Citizen monitoring)
① Citizens may monitor all activities relating to legislative processes of the Integrated Special City Council and the formulation, decisions and execution of policies by the Mayor or the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City to exercise oversight and scrutiny, as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Citizens may organize and operate a citizen monitoring group for the monitoring activities under paragraph ①.
③ Matters necessary for monitoring activities, composition and operation of citizen monitoring groups, etc. under paragraphs ① and ② shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 33 (Application mutatis mutandis of personnel affairs concerning public officials)
① Article 38 shall apply mutatis mutandis to ensuring fair treatment of public officials of the Integrated Special City Council to the extent not inconsistent with the nature of those affairs.
② Article 39 shall apply mutatis mutandis to special provisions concerning personnel management of the Integrated Special City Council to the extent not inconsistent with the nature of those affairs. In such cases, "the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City and the Mayor of the Integrated Special City" shall be construed as "the chairperson of the Integrated Special City Council".

Article 34 (Reporting on large-scale development projects)
Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City implements a large-scale development project prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance or grants approval, permission, authorization, etc. for such a project, the Mayor shall report the details of the development project plan to the Integrated Special City Council in advance.

CHAPTER IV AUTONOMOUS ADMINISTRATION

Article 35 (Special provisions concerning autonomous organizations)
① The Integrated Special City shall have four Vice Mayors, of whom two shall be state public officials in political service and two shall be local public officials in political service.
② Notwithstanding Article 123 (6) of the Local Autonomy Act, the titles, affairs, and powers of the Vice Mayors appointed under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ Notwithstanding Article 125 (2) of the Local Autonomy Act (excluding matters concerning personnel expenses and grade standards) and Articles 126 through 128 of that Act, the following matters may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance:
1. Standards for the establishment and operation of administrative organizations;
2. Standards for the prescribed number of local public officials (including staff assigned to the Integrated Special City Council);
3. Requirements for establishing agencies directly under the Integrated Special City, business offices and branch offices.
④ The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall establish and publicly notify standards for the establishment and operation of administrative organizations to ensure appropriate organizational scale and rational operation.

Article 36 (Special provisions concerning firefighting organization)
① Notwithstanding Articles 2 and 3 of the Framework Act on Firefighting Services, a Fire Headquarters of the Integrated Special City shall be established as an agency directly under the Mayor of the Integrated Special City to perform firefighting affairs of the Integrated Special City in an integrated manner.
② The Fire Headquarters of the Integrated Special City shall have two Deputy Heads to oversee firefighting affairs for different areas of the Integrated Special City.
③ The head of the Fire Headquarters of the Integrated Special City shall oversee firefighting affairs in the jurisdiction and direct and supervise subordinate public officials under the direction and supervision of the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
④ Matters necessary for the performance of firefighting affairs and operation of the Fire Headquarters of the Integrated Special City, other than those prescribed by relevant statutes, shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 37 (Personnel hearings)
① Notwithstanding relevant statutes, before appointing a Vice Mayor as a local public official in political service under Article 123 (2) of the Local Autonomy Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall request the Integrated Special City Council to conduct a personnel hearing.
② The Integrated Special City Council shall establish a special personnel hearing committee to conduct a personnel hearing for a person for whom the Mayor has requested a hearing under paragraph ①.
③ The Integrated Special City Council shall establish a special personnel hearing committee to examine a motion for consent to the appointment of the chairperson of the Audit Committee under Article 88 (2).
④ A special personnel hearing committee under paragraphs ② and ③ shall be deemed constituted when a motion for consent to appointment of a person requiring the consent of the Integrated Special City Council or a personnel hearing request submitted by the Mayor of the Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as a "motion for consent to appointment, etc.") is submitted to the Integrated Special City Council, and shall exist until the motion for consent to appointment, etc. is resolved at a plenary meeting of the Council or the progress of the personnel hearing is reported at such a plenary meeting.
⑤ A special personnel hearing committee shall hold a hearing on personnel affairs for the hearing or examination under paragraphs ② and ③.
⑥ Except as provided in paragraphs ① through ⑤, Articles 4 (2), 5 through 9, 10 (1) and (2), 11, 12 through 15, 15-2, and 16 through 18 of the Personnel Hearing Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to personnel hearings under paragraph ⑤. In such cases, "committee" shall be construed as "special personnel hearing committee"; "chairperson" as "chairperson of the special personnel hearing committee"; "National Assembly" as "Integrated Special City Council"; "appointing authority (including the President-elect) or nominating authority" and "President or Chief Justice of the Supreme Court" each as "Mayor of the Integrated Special City"; "Speaker" as "chairperson of the Integrated Special City Council"; "Justice of the Constitutional Court, etc." and "candidate for public office under Article 65-2 (2) of the National Assembly Act" each as "person subject to a personnel hearing"; and "state agency" as "local government".
⑦ Detailed matters necessary for the composition and operation of the special personnel hearing committee, conduct of personnel hearings, methods of obtaining answers and opinions from prospective appointees, etc., other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ⑥, shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 38 (Guarantee of fair treatment of public officials)
① Positions in excess of the prescribed number of public officials arising from the integration of the former Gwangju Metropolitan City and Jeollanam-do (including educational public officials and local public officials under the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article) shall be recognized as positions outside the prescribed quota, but the Integrated Special City shall actively endeavor to eliminate such excess promptly.
② The Integrated Special City shall accord equal treatment in personnel affairs to public officials belonging to the abolished Gwangju Metropolitan City and Jeollanam-do.
③ Public officials appointed before the establishment of the Integrated Special City shall be guaranteed the opportunity to work within the jurisdiction of the former Gwangju Metropolitan City or Jeollanam-do, respectively: Provided, That this shall not apply where the public official expressly consents otherwise.
④ Personnel management of local public officials under the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City shall be governed by the separate provisions of this Act.

Article 39 (Special provisions on personnel management of the Integrated Special City)
① The powers of the Minister of Education and the Minister of the Interior and Safety under Articles 30 (2) and 74 (2) of the Local Public Officials Act shall be vested in the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City and the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, respectively.
② Notwithstanding Articles 7 (2) and (11), 8, 9 (1) and (2), 10 (2), 11, 32, 37 (1) and (4), 38 (excluding the minimum years of service by grade required for promotion), and 39 (excluding paragraphs (4) and (7)) of the Local Public Officials Act, matters falling under the following subparagraphs may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance:
1. Composition of the Integrated Special City Personnel Committee (including the personnel committee under the chairperson of the Integrated Special City Council; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article) and the Integrated Special City Office of Education Personnel Committee, and selection of their vice chairpersons;
2. Staff of the Integrated Special City Personnel Committee and the Integrated Special City Office of Education Personnel Committee;
3. Agencies conducting examinations;
4. Methods for appointment and recommendation of newly recruited candidates;
5. Methods and order of promotion, preparation of promotion candidate lists, and examinations for promotion.
③ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under the main sentence of the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 7 (5); Articles 8 (3) and (4), 10 (4), 25-3, 27 (4), the proviso to Article 29-2, Article 30-3, the latter part of Article 30-5 (2), Article 34, Article 34-2 (2), the main sentence of Article 35 (1), the latter part of Article 35 (2), Article 36 (1) and (2), the main sentence of Article 36 (4), Article 36 (5), Article 39-2 (4), the proviso to Article 41-4 (2), the former part of Article 41-4 (3), the proviso to Article 46-3, the proviso to the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 63 (2), Articles 67-2 (6), 67-3 and 76 (3) of the Local Public Officials Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
④ Notwithstanding Article 25-2 of the Local Public Officials Act, matters concerning the fields, periods, and procedures for appointment of foreigners may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance: Provided, That this shall not include appointments in fields involving the exercise of public authority or national security and secrets.
⑤ Persons proficient in foreign languages may receive preferential treatment for promotion as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑥ Notwithstanding the Local Public Officials Act and relevant statutes thereunder, matters relating to the following may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance:
1. Conduct of examinations for public officials exempt from grade classifications under Article 4 (2) of the Local Public Officials Act;
2. Promotion under Article 39 (2) through (7) of the Local Public Officials Act;
3. Filling vacancies under Article 41 (2) of the Local Public Officials Act.

Article 40 (Special provisions on appointment of state public officials)
Among the powers of the relevant ministers or the heads of central administrative agencies under Articles 32 (1) through (3), 78 (1) and (4), and 82 of the State Public Officials Act concerning appointment, etc. of state public officials belonging to the Integrated Special City (including the Integrated Special City Council, but excluding public officials under the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City), the matters prescribed by Presidential Decree shall be exercised by the Mayor of the Integrated Special City (including the chairperson of the Integrated Special City Council; hereinafter the same shall apply in this Article). Notwithstanding Article 16 of the same Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall be the defendant in related administrative litigation.

Article 41 (Personnel exchanges between the State and the Integrated Special City)
① To enhance the capacity to perform autonomous administration and develop the capabilities of subordinate public officials, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City (including the chairperson of the Integrated Special City Council) and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may conduct personnel exchanges, within a limit not exceeding ten percent of the total number of general-service public officials in each grade, following consultation with the heads of other local governments, state agencies, public organizations, foreign administrative agencies, and other institutions.
② Criteria and methods for personnel exchanges under paragraph ①, support for persons subject to exchanges, etc. shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ Notwithstanding Article 30-4 (4) of the Local Public Officials Act, grounds, periods, and procedures for dispatch and matters concerning service during dispatch may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
④ The State shall actively cooperate in personnel exchanges with the Integrated Special City to ensure consistent operation of national policies and interconnection between the State and the Integrated Special City.

Article 42 (Special provisions on selection and recruitment of local talent)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City or the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may select local talent as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance, have selected persons serve as trainees for a period not exceeding three years, and appoint persons who are recognized as outstanding in performance and aptitude during training as public officials of Grade VII or below following deliberation by the Integrated Special City Personnel Committee or the Integrated Special City Office of Education Personnel Committee at least one month before the end of the training period.
② When appointing a trainee under paragraph ① as a public official of Grade VII or below, probationary appointment shall be waived notwithstanding the main sentence of Article 28 (1) of the Local Public Officials Act.

Article 43 (Support for public officials whose workplaces change)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City (including the chairperson of the Integrated Special City Council) and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may formulate and implement support measures, including relocation assistance, as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance, for public officials or employees ordered to work in distant areas due to establishment of the Integrated Special City or who change residence following relocation of the location of an office.
② Support measures under paragraph ① shall include the following matters:
1. For persons changing their residence:
(a) Temporary payment of relocation assistance;
(b) Temporary payment of housing assistance;
2. Temporary payment of transportation expenses at actual cost to persons commuting over long distances.

Article 44 (Strengthening expertise of residents' self-governance organizations and establishment of secretariats)
① To ensure the efficient performance of duties by residents' self-governance councils and enhance their expertise, a secretariat or dedicated administrative personnel may be established within each council.
② Specific matters, including the composition of secretariats, personnel management and scope of affairs, shall be prescribed by ordinance of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu in consideration of local conditions.
③ The Mayor of the Integrated Special City and the heads of Sis, Guns and Gus may provide administrative and financial support necessary for the stable operation of secretariats.

Article 45 (Special provisions concerning operation of metropolitan administration)
① Where the opinions of the heads of relevant central administrative agencies differ from those of the Mayor of the Integrated Special City in establishing or implementing plans relating to roads, transportation, the environment, etc. concerning the Integrated Special City, the Prime Minister shall coordinate the differences unless otherwise specially prescribed by another Act.
② Matters necessary for coordination by the Prime Minister under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 46 (Special provisions concerning awards and decorations)
Notwithstanding Article 5 (2) of the Awards and Decorations Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall recommend awards and decorations for public officials belonging to the Integrated Special City.

Article 47 (Special provisions concerning recommendations to declare special disaster areas)
Notwithstanding Article 60 (1) and (4) of the Framework Act on the Management of Disasters and Safety, where a disaster of a scale prescribed by Presidential Decree occurs and the Mayor of the Integrated Special City deems special measures necessary because it significantly affects the peace and maintenance of social order of the Integrated Special City or to effectively address the damage, the Mayor may recommend that the President declare the affected area a special disaster area following consultation with the head of the Central Disaster and Safety Countermeasure Headquarters.

Article 48 (Special provisions concerning expansion and operation of participatory budgeting)
① When operating the participatory budgeting system under Article 39 of the Local Finance Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall endeavor to encourage projects proposed by residents through resources increased by integration.
② Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City determines that projects proposed by residents' self-governance councils or other resident bodies contribute to balanced development among regions, the Mayor may give priority to reviewing and reflecting such projects in the budget compilation process.
③ Allocation of participatory budgets and detailed operational methods shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance reflecting the characteristics of individual regions and the opinions of residents.

Article 49 (Special provisions concerning residents' referenda)
Notwithstanding Article 9 (2) of the Residents' Referendum Act, a residents' referendum may be requested with signatures numbering at least the number prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance within a range of not less than one thirtieth and not more than one fifth of the total number of residents entitled to request a referendum.

Article 50 (Special provisions concerning classification of occupational groups and series)
① Notwithstanding Article 4 (1) and (4) of the Local Public Officials Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may integrate occupational groups and series of general-service local public officials in Grades II through IV as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance, and may integrate or newly establish some occupational groups and series of general-service local public officials in Grade V or below as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Where occupational groups or series are integrated or newly established under paragraph ①, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may, following deliberation by the Integrated Special City Personnel Committee or the Integrated Special City Office of Education Personnel Committee, alter the method of preparing the list of candidates for promotion as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. The alteration shall apply from the date one year after the alteration.

Article 51 (Special provisions concerning position classification systems)
① Notwithstanding Article 24 of the Local Public Officials Act, the Integrated Special City may implement a position classification system for general-service public officials at a time prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under Articles 22 (1), 22-2 (2) and 23 (1) and (2) of the Local Public Officials Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 52 (Special promotion of outstanding public officials)
Notwithstanding Article 39-3 (2) of the Local Public Officials Act, the requirements and other matters concerning special promotion of outstanding public officials may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. Such provisions shall include preferential treatment in special promotion for public officials who meet the grounds specified in Article 39-3 (1) 1 through 3 of the same Act.

Article 53 (Special provisions concerning open positions and publicly competed positions)
① Notwithstanding Article 29-4 of the Local Public Officials Act (excluding paragraph (3)), detailed operational matters concerning the designation of open positions, appointment requirements and procedures, etc. (excluding matters concerning the conduct of examinations) may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Notwithstanding Article 29-5 (3) of the Local Public Officials Act, matters necessary for designating and operating publicly competed positions may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

CHAPTER V AUTONOMOUS FINANCES

Article 54 (Administrative and financial support from the State)
① The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for the successful establishment and operation of the Integrated Special City.
② In implementing various policy projects, the heads of central administrative agencies may provide priority support to the Integrated Special City and its Sis, Guns and Gus as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ Notwithstanding Article 22 (1) of the Local Finance Act, the State may separately determine ratios for sharing expenses between the Integrated Special City and its Sis, Guns and Gus.

Article 55 (Principle of no disadvantages)
Integration of Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City shall not result in the loss of administrative or financial benefits previously enjoyed by Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City or impose additional burdens on residents of those areas.

Article 56 (Budgetary support and special provisions)
① The State may provide support equivalent to part of the operating expenses and other costs saved by integration of Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City (limited to expenses funded from the State budget).
② The budget for the fiscal year in which the Integrated Special City is established shall consist of the budgets separately prepared, resolved upon and established by the former Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City, combined by account and budget item.
③ The State shall guarantee that financial support to the Integrated Special City is at least equal to the level of support provided before its establishment.
④ The State may provide special financial support to the Integrated Special City, including grants, financial investment and loans, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 57 (Establishment and operation of balanced development fund)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall establish and operate a balanced development fund under this Act to reduce disparities among regions of the Integrated Special City, eliminate inefficiency resulting from competitive and overlapping investment within the same living areas and among regions, and expand mutual cooperation and linkage among local governments within the Integrated Special City.
② Sources and uses of the balanced development fund and other matters concerning its operation shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 58 (Special provisions on issuance of local bonds)
Notwithstanding Article 11 (3) of the Local Finance Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may issue local bonds exceeding the prescribed ceiling on local bond issuance following a resolution by the Integrated Special City Council; in such cases, a majority of incumbent Council members shall attend and at least two thirds of those present shall vote in favor: Provided, That in cases falling under the proviso to Article 11 (3) of the same Act, the Mayor shall first obtain approval from the Minister of the Interior and Safety and then obtain a resolution of the Integrated Special City Council.

Article 59 (Special provisions concerning management of local public enterprises)
Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under Article 7 (2), the proviso to the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 14 (1), Article 17 (3), Article 33 (4), Article 43 and Article 71 (2) of the Local Public Enterprises Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 60 (Special provisions concerning management of public property)
Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under Article 20 (2) 1, the proviso to Article 29 (1), Article 29 (2), Article 34 (1) 2, Article 34 (2) and the main sentence and proviso to Article 37 (1) of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 61 (Special provisions on adjustment of tax rates)
Notwithstanding tax rates (including standard tax rates and surtax base rates; hereinafter the same shall apply) under the Local Tax Act, the tax rates of Integrated Special City taxes may be increased or decreased by up to 100 percent of the applicable tax rate as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance: Provided, That tax rates under Articles 13, 13-2, 15, 34, and 146 (2) 2 and 3 of the Local Tax Act shall not be adjusted.

CHAPTER VI EDUCATIONAL AUTONOMY

Article 62 (Special provisions on election of the Superintendent of Education)
① The State shall establish the office of Superintendent of Education in the Integrated Special City to promote the autonomy and professionalism of education and the distinct characteristics of local education.
② The Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City shall be elected by universal, equal, direct and secret ballot of residents in accordance with the Local Education Autonomy Act, Public Official Election Act, Local Autonomy Act, Framework Act on Education and other relevant Acts.

Article 63 (Special provisions on establishment and operation of school foundations)
① The authority of the Minister of Education under the latter part of Article 20 (2) and Article 45 (2) through (4) of the Private School Act shall be vested in the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City regarding school foundations establishing and operating schools under Article 4 (1) 1 of that Act, and in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City regarding school foundations establishing and operating private schools under Article 4 (3) 1 of that Act: Provided, That the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall exercise such authority regarding school foundations that concurrently establish and operate schools under Article 4 (3) 1 and other private schools.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under Articles 10-2 (2), the proviso to 18-2 (4), 18-2 (5) and the proviso to 21 (1) of the Private School Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ When applying Article 40 of the Private School Act mutatis mutandis to the Integrated Special City, "Minister of Education" shall be construed as "Minister of Education or Mayor of the Integrated Special City".
④ Where necessary for regional development, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may grant permission under Article 10 (1) of the Private School Act regarding school foundations under Article 4 (3) 2 and 3 of that Act with the prior consent of the Minister of Education.
⑤ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under the former and latter parts of the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 10 (1) of the Private School Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance with the prior consent of the Minister of Education.

Article 64 (Special provisions concerning early childhood education and childcare)
① The authority of the Minister of Education under Article 13 (4) of the Early Childhood Education Act shall be vested in the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Education under Articles 5 (3), 6 (2), 8 (1), the main sentence of the portion other than the subparagraphs of 8 (4), 10 (2), 12 (3), 16 (2), 17 (4), 19 (4) (limited to evaluations under Article 19 (1)), 23 (2), 24 (1), 24 (5) (limited to methods of support under Article 24 (2)), the former part of the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 25 (1), 25 (2) and (5), 26 (3), 27 and 30 (2) of the Early Childhood Education Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Education under Articles 6 (4), 7 (5), 11 (3), 13 (4), 14 (3), the main sentence of 15, 17 (5), 19 (2), 23 (5), 24 (1) and (4), the proviso to 25 (1), 25 (6), 28 (1) 8, 29 (5), 37 and 43 (1) and (2) of the Child Care Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 65 (Special provisions concerning elementary and secondary education)
① Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Education under Articles 4 (1), 13 (4), 14 (2), 18-2 (4), 18-3 (2), 27 (3), 30 (3) (excluding matters concerning standards for teacher placement), 31 (3), 33 (2), 34 (1) and (2), 34-2 (4), 43 (2), 47 (2), 60 (3), 60-2 (3), 60-3 (5), 63 (3) and the latter part of 63 (5) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Notwithstanding Articles 43 and 47 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, eligibility for admission to foreign schools under Article 60-2 of that Act may be differently prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or determined by the Minister of Education under the portions other than the subparagraphs of Articles 6 (1) and 7 (1) of the Framework Act on the Promotion of Digital-Based Distance Education may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 66 (Special provisions on operation of schools and curricula)
① National, public and private elementary, middle, high and special schools situated in the Integrated Special City may, upon designation by the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City, operate schools or curricula to which Articles 8, 19 (4), 21 (1), 22 (2), 23 (3), 24, 26 (1), 29, 31, 39, 42 and 46 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act do not apply (hereinafter referred to as "autonomous schools").
② The head of a national or public autonomous school may request the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City or the head of the education office to appoint teachers necessary for operating the autonomous school or defer transfer of teachers belonging to the school.
③ Where necessary, the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may establish and operate autonomous schools to foster talent suited to regional characteristics.
④ Matters to which paragraph ① does not apply and matters necessary for operation of autonomous schools under paragraph ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
⑤ A person who completes the full curriculum at an autonomous school equivalent to an elementary, middle or high school under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act shall be deemed to have academic qualifications equivalent to graduation from an elementary, middle or high school, respectively.
⑥ Teachers and students of autonomous schools shall not suffer disadvantages because of their service or studies at such schools.

Article 67 (Special provisions concerning designation, establishment and operation of schools for gifted students)
① Notwithstanding Article 6 of the Gifted Education Promotion Act, the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may designate or establish and operate schools for gifted students with the prior consent of the Minister of Education. In such cases, the Minister shall determine whether to grant consent following deliberation by the Central Gifted Education Promotion Committee under Article 4 of the same Act.
② Where a school for gifted students under paragraph ① violates statutes or school regulations or is deemed incapable of achieving its purpose of establishment, the Superintendent of Education may revoke its designation with the prior consent of the Minister of Education. The Minister shall determine consent following deliberation by the Central Gifted Education Promotion Committee under Article 4 of the Gifted Education Promotion Act.
③ Articles 9, 19, 19-2, 24, 26, 29, 31 and 46 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act may be disapplied to schools for gifted students: Provided, That the scope and limits of such disapplication shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
④ Notwithstanding Article 47 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, the head of a school for gifted students may permit admission (including readmission, transfer and admission by transfer) of foreigners recognized as having the ability to receive gifted education.
⑤ Where necessary to provide foreign language instruction at a school for gifted students, foreigners satisfying qualification requirements prescribed by Presidential Decree may be appointed as fixed-term teachers or instructors notwithstanding Article 21 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, Articles 6 and 32 (1) of the Educational Public Officials Act, and Articles 52 and 54-4 (1) and (3) of the Private School Act.
⑥ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under Article 5 (3) of the Gifted Education Promotion Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑦ Curricula at schools for gifted students shall be organized and operated mainly around individualized education suited to each student's capabilities and aptitude; the head of the school shall determine specific details with approval from the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City.
⑧ The Superintendent of Education shall periodically evaluate and disclose operational performance of schools for gifted students. Specific matters concerning evaluation methods, etc. shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
⑨ Students at schools for gifted students may advance or graduate early and become eligible for early admission to schools of a higher level according to their abilities and aptitudes. Specific matters shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑩ The Superintendent of Education shall take necessary management and supervisory measures to ensure that establishing and operating schools for gifted students does not become privileged education for particular social groups or excessively elitist education or intensify educational disparities among regions and social groups.

Article 68 (Special provisions on operation of specialized purpose high schools)
① Articles 19, 19-2, 24, 26, 29 and 46 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act may be disapplied to high schools under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the same Act situated in the Integrated Special City that provide specialized education in fields prescribed by Presidential Decree (hereinafter referred to as "specialized purpose high schools"): Provided, That the scope and limits of such disapplication shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Notwithstanding Article 47 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, the head of a specialized purpose high school may permit admission (including readmission, transfer and admission by transfer) of foreigners recognized as capable of studying at the high school level; details shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ Where necessary for foreign language instruction, specialized purpose high schools may appoint foreigners meeting the qualification requirements prescribed by Presidential Decree as fixed-term teachers or instructors notwithstanding Article 21 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, Articles 6 and 32 (1) of the Educational Public Officials Act, and Articles 52 and 54-4 (1) and (3) of the Private School Act.
④ The Superintendent of Education shall take necessary management and supervisory measures to prevent the establishment and operation of specialized purpose high schools from becoming privileged education for particular groups or excessive elitist education or intensifying educational disparities among regions and social groups.

Article 69 (Special provisions concerning integrated operation of schools)
① Notwithstanding Articles 26, 30 and 61 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may autonomously organize grade systems for the integrated operation of schools not exceeding the size prescribed by Presidential Decree (limited to schools under Article 2 of the same Act).
② In elementary, middle and high schools autonomously operating grade systems under paragraph ①, the Superintendent of Education may permit cross-level teaching by teachers (meaning teaching students of another school level) as determined by the Minister of Education.
③ The Superintendent of Education may provide administrative and financial support for cross-level teaching under paragraph ② and necessary training for participating teachers.
④ Matters necessary for teacher training and education, etc. other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ③ shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 70 (Support for students with migration backgrounds, etc.)
① The head of a school situated in the Integrated Special City (limited to schools under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act) may autonomously operate curricula for students with migration backgrounds, etc. under Article 28-2 (1) of that Act, regionally specialized curricula, etc. in accordance with the curriculum under Article 23 (2) of the same Act: Provided, That the Superintendent of Education may determine matters necessary for operating school curricula. <Amended on 2026.5.19>
② Notwithstanding Articles 13 (4) and 43 (2) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, the Superintendent of Education may refrain from designating attendance districts for elementary schools operating distinctive curricula under paragraph ① and may conduct middle school admission procedures as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ Notwithstanding Articles 13 (4), 14 (2), 43 (2) and 47 (2) of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, the Superintendent of Education may permit transfers to and admission to schools in agricultural and fishing villages.
④ Notwithstanding Article 5 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, to guarantee learning rights of persons eligible for special education under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Act on Special Education for Persons with Disabilities, etc., the Superintendent of Education may establish elementary, middle, high and special schools together in accordance with regional conditions: Provided, That where a special school is established together with other schools, requirements prescribed by Presidential Decree concerning school size, facilities and equipment standards, etc. shall be met.

Article 71 (Special restrictions on transfer of teachers recruited for particular regions)
Notwithstanding the latter part of Article 11 (2) of the Educational Public Officials Act, the period during which teachers newly recruited under the former part of that paragraph may be restricted from transferring to another region or school may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 72 (Special provisions on recruitment of teachers)
Notwithstanding the former part of Article 11 (1) of the Educational Public Officials Act, where the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City deems it necessary for balanced regional development under the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth and for the stable recruitment of outstanding local talent, the Superintendent may conduct open competitive examinations for newly recruited teachers from among graduates (including prospective graduates) of universities situated in the region or residents thereof, etc., for a number not exceeding ten percent of the planned recruitment of new teachers, as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. <Amended on 2026.6.2>

Article 73 (Special provisions concerning establishment and operation of foreign educational institutions)
① A foreign school corporation (meaning a national or local government or nonprofit corporation that establishes and operates early childhood, elementary, secondary or higher educational institutions abroad pursuant to foreign law; hereinafter the same shall apply) may establish a foreign educational institution (meaning a foreign educational institution under Article 2, subparagraph 5 of the Special Act on Designation and Management of Free Economic Zones; hereinafter the same shall apply) in an area of the Integrated Special City prescribed by Presidential Decree.
