② Where a foreign educational institution is established under paragraph ①, establishment of an institution equivalent to a school at the high school level or below shall require approval from the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City, and establishment of an institution equivalent to a school under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act (hereinafter referred to as a "foreign higher education institution") shall require approval from the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
③ The Superintendent of Education or the Mayor shall obtain deliberation and resolution by the Foreign Educational Institution Establishment and Operation Deliberation Committee under paragraph ⑤ (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee" in this Article) before approving the establishment of a foreign educational institution under paragraph ②.
④ Standards and procedures for approval of establishment, and other matters necessary for establishment and operation of foreign educational institutions shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance: Provided, That the Minister of Education shall be consulted in advance when prescribing standards for establishment of foreign higher education institutions.
⑤ The Superintendent of Education and the Mayor shall each establish a Committee under their respective offices to deliberate on the establishment and operation of foreign educational institutions.
⑥ Functions, composition and operation of the Committees shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑦ Except as prescribed by this Act, the Special Act on Establishment and Operation of Foreign Educational Institutions in Free Economic Zones and Jeju Free International City (including its penal provisions and administrative fines) shall apply mutatis mutandis to the establishment and operation of foreign educational institutions. In such cases, "Minister of Education" shall be construed as "Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City" for institutions equivalent to schools at the high school level or below and as "Mayor of the Integrated Special City" for foreign higher education institutions; and matters otherwise to be prescribed by Presidential Decree (excluding the main sentence of Article 10 (1) and Article 11 (1) and (3) of that Act) that this Act permits the Integrated Special City to regulate differently may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑧ The State or the Integrated Special City may provide funding necessary for purchasing sites, constructing facilities or operating foreign educational institutions, or may provide sites, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
⑨ For a foreign educational institution established under paragraph ① that is equivalent to a school at the high school level or below, the number of Korean nationals admitted shall be determined by the head of the institution within the ratio prescribed by Presidential Decree.
⑩ The Superintendent of Education shall take necessary management and supervisory measures to prevent foreign educational institutions at the high school level or below from becoming privileged education for particular groups or excessively elitist education or intensifying educational disparities among regions and social groups.

Article 74 (Special support for early childhood education and childcare in population-declining areas)
① Where necessary for early childhood education or childcare, the head of a kindergarten situated in an area with a declining population under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Special Act on Support for Areas with Declining Populations (limited to areas without childcare centers, with specific areas prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance) may permit children under three years of age to enroll, notwithstanding Article 11 (1) of the Early Childhood Education Act.
② Expenses incurred under paragraph ① may be supported by local education subsidies under the Local Education Subsidy Act.

Article 75 (Special provisions on training personnel for regional development)
① The State and the Integrated Special City shall establish policies, including administrative and financial support, to develop outstanding human resources linked to local industries and encourage them to settle in the region.
② The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall give priority to policies establishing settlement conditions, including housing, educational and cultural facilities, to attract and retain outstanding human resources.
③ Specific beneficiaries, methods and procedures for support under paragraphs ① and ② shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 76 (Special provisions on status and powers of the Superintendent of Education)
Notwithstanding any other Part of this Act, the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City shall have independent status and authority over educational and academic affairs of the Integrated Special City, including organizational, personnel, financial and audit matters, under the Local Education Autonomy Act.

Article 77 (Special provisions concerning authority to organize educational autonomy)
① Notwithstanding Article 30 (1) (limited to matters concerning numbers) and (4) of the Local Education Autonomy Act, the Integrated Special City shall have two Deputy Superintendents of Education, with their division of affairs prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Notwithstanding Articles 30 (5) and 33 of the Local Education Autonomy Act, the following matters shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance by applying mutatis mutandis the relevant statutes applicable to Seoul Special Metropolitan City:
1. Standards for the establishment and operation of administrative organizations;
2. Standards for the prescribed number of local public officials, etc.
③ The Superintendent of Education shall actively support the following matters to eliminate educational disparities among regions and promote balanced development at the Si, Gun and Gu levels:
1. Securing autonomy and flexibility in the organization, personnel and financial operations of local offices of education;
2. Promoting educational cooperation projects between local offices of education and local governments;
3. Other matters necessary for balanced development of education in the Integrated Special City.
④ A head of a local office of education shall establish and operate a Local Education Development Committee to deliberate on educational development in the jurisdiction, jointly chaired by the head of the education office and the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu, with school operating committee members, local educational and industrial experts, residents, etc. as members. Matters necessary for its composition and operation shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑤ Following consultation with the Local Education Development Committee, the head of the education office shall formulate and implement a regional educational development plan for educational policies requiring cooperation with heads of Sis, Guns and Gus.
⑥ Notwithstanding Article 34 (4) of the Local Education Autonomy Act, matters concerning appointment of heads of local offices of education may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. In such cases, the Superintendent of Education may introduce an appointment method guaranteeing participation by local residents and educational stakeholders to strengthen local educational autonomy and reflect residents' opinions.
⑦ Notwithstanding Article 20 of the Local Education Autonomy Act, the Superintendent of Education may delegate some affairs, including preparation of draft budgets and personnel management, as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance, to heads of education offices appointed through open recruitment with the participation of local residents under paragraph ⑥.

Article 78 (Special provisions on personnel management following integration of Jeonnam and Gwangju)
① In principle, public officials (including educational public officials and local public officials) under the Superintendent of Education who were appointed or selected before the establishment of the Integrated Special City shall work within the jurisdiction of the former Gwangju Metropolitan City or Jeollanam-do. Where personnel are exchanged across former jurisdictions due to educational administrative necessity, the consent of the person concerned shall be obtained.
② Article 38 (3) shall not apply to public officials under the Superintendent of Education.
③ When preparing lists of candidates for promotion among educational public officials appointed before the Integrated Special City was established, the Superintendent of Education shall prepare separate lists for each former jurisdiction in consideration of the former personnel systems and the characteristics of teacher supply and demand.
④ In preparing lists of candidates for promotion under paragraph ③, the Superintendent of Education may prescribe different types, scopes and criteria of optional additional points for the former jurisdictions of Gwangju Metropolitan City and Jeollanam-do.
⑤ The scope, procedures, and other necessary matters for the application of special personnel management provisions shall be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Education.

Article 79 (Special provisions on establishment and operation of public alternative schools)
① To meet diverse educational needs, the Superintendent of Education may establish and operate alternative schools under Article 60-3 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act (hereinafter referred to as "public alternative schools").
② Article 60-3 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to standards for establishment, facilities and equipment, curricula and operation of public alternative schools. In such cases, "Superintendent of Education" shall be construed as "Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City".

Article 80 (Special provisions on support for rural and small schools and rural study programs)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City and the Superintendent of Education shall formulate and implement policies necessary to improve educational conditions and ensure the sustainable operation of schools in farming and fishing villages (including attached kindergartens; hereinafter the same shall apply) and small schools (including attached kindergartens; hereinafter the same shall apply) facing poor educational conditions due to a declining school-age population and regional circumstances.
② The Mayor, Superintendent of Education, and heads of Sis, Guns and Gus may provide administrative and financial support for operation of curricula, attracting students, improving living and childcare environments, and promoting education linked to the region at rural and small schools.
③ The Mayor and Superintendent of Education may operate and support rural schools, small schools and rural study programs and shall thereby promote support for rural and small schools, educational exchanges between urban and rural areas, and improved conditions for local settlement.
④ Matters necessary for operating and supporting rural and small schools and rural study programs under paragraphs ① through ③ shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 81 (Special provisions on linking elementary and secondary education with higher education)
① To link higher education with elementary and secondary education, the Superintendent of Education may participate in planning, coordinating and implementing the following higher education projects following consultation with the Mayor of the Integrated Special City:
1. Development and operation of curricula and joint curricula linking elementary, middle and high schools with universities;
2. Operation of university-level education programs for high school students, early completion and credit recognition systems;
3. University-linked programs for teacher professional development, training and practical experience for prospective and incumbent teachers;
4. Programs linking career guidance, university admission and employment to develop local talent;
5. Other projects deemed necessary to link elementary and secondary education with higher education.
② Procedures, division of roles, financial contributions, and other matters necessary for projects under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 82 (Special provisions concerning operation of schools and curricula in regional strategic industries)
① Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City deem it necessary to apply standards under relevant statutes differently in designating industry-tailored high schools or operating specialized high schools within their jurisdiction in order to train specialized personnel in fields characteristic of the region, such as aerospace, artificial intelligence and future mobility, and strengthen cooperation among industry, academia and research, they may request the Minister of Education to apply special provisions concerning the designation or operation of such schools, notwithstanding the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, the Industrial Education Enhancement and Industry-Academia-Research Cooperation Promotion Act, and other relevant statutes.
② Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City intends to designate or cancel the designation of an industry-tailored high school under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall consult in advance with the Superintendent of Education.
③ Where the Mayor or the Superintendent of Education deems it necessary to apply standards under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, the Industrial Education Enhancement and Industry-Academia-Research Cooperation Promotion Act, etc. differently in operating industry-tailored high schools and specialized high schools under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act, the Mayor or Superintendent may request the Minister of Education to apply special provisions concerning the operation of such schools to train specialized personnel and strengthen industry-academia-research cooperation in regional specialized fields. Where the necessity of specialized education in regional strategic industries is recognized, the Minister may approve operation of industry-tailored high schools or specialized high schools by the Superintendent of Education in accordance with the standards prescribed by relevant statutes.
④ The Mayor and the Superintendent of Education may establish and operate integrated education and research facilities and campuses where universities, research institutions, enterprises, etc. may be jointly located within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City to train talent for regional strategic industries and promote industry-academia-research cooperation (hereinafter referred to as "regional industrial innovation campuses").
⑤ The Mayor and the Superintendent of Education may provide administrative and financial support for establishing and operating regional industrial innovation campuses, operating linked curricula among industry-tailored or specialized high schools, universities and industries, and specialized personnel training programs.
⑥ Matters concerning requests for special provisions on operation of schools under paragraph ③, linked curricula among universities and industries under paragraphs ③ through ⑤, and division of roles among relevant institutions shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 83 (Special provisions concerning student admission quotas)
① When determining admission quotas for high schools within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City, the Superintendent of Education may operate quotas flexibly as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance, taking into account changes in population, industrial demand and educational conditions.
② The Superintendent of Education shall conduct an annual survey of student demand to flexibly operate admission quotas under paragraph ①.
③ Detailed matters necessary for flexible operation of admission quotas under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by the education regulations of the Integrated Special City.

Article 84 (Special provisions concerning operation of schools attached to national universities)
① Where necessary, the Superintendent of Education may convert schools attached to national universities (excluding schools established and operated by national university corporations) within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City under Article 3, subparagraph 1 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act and Article 45 of the Higher Education Act into public schools following consultation with the Ministry of Education and university presidents.
② University presidents may present opinions concerning operation of curricula and transfer and promotion of teachers (including principals) at schools converted to public schools under paragraph ①, and the Superintendent of Education shall reflect those opinions to the greatest possible extent when operating the schools.
③ Heads of schools converted to public schools shall actively cooperate in field practice and research by students at colleges of education and teachers' colleges.
④ Matters necessary for designation and operation of attached schools, including curricula and field practice, shall be determined by agreement between the university president and the Superintendent of Education.

Article 85 (Support for structural improvement of private schools)
① To improve local educational conditions in response to declining school-age populations, the Superintendent of Education may order structural improvement of school foundations (limited to those establishing and operating schools under Article 4 (1) 1 of the Private School Act) and private schools established and operated by such foundations. Specific matters concerning orders for structural improvement shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② The Superintendent of Education may provide administrative and financial support where necessary to implement an order for structural improvement by a school foundation.

Article 86 (Special provisions concerning establishment, guidance and supervision of universities)
① The powers of the Minister of Education under Articles 50-2 (2) and 61 (1) and (3) of the Higher Education Act shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
② Where necessary for regional development, the Mayor may grant authorization under Article 4 (2) of the Higher Education Act with the prior consent of the Minister of Education.
③ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under Article 4 (1) of the Higher Education Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance with the prior consent of the Minister of Education.

CHAPTER VII AUTONOMOUS POLICING

Article 87 (Special provisions concerning the autonomous police system)
① To strengthen linkage between local administration and public security administration within its jurisdiction, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may formulate measures to improve the organization and affairs of autonomous policing through the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Autonomous Police Committee under Article 18 of the Act on the Organization and Operation of National Police and Autonomous Police.
② The State may actively cooperate in such institutional improvements and provide necessary budgetary support.

CHAPTER VIII AUTONOMOUS AUDITING

Article 88 (Establishment and duties of the Audit Committee)
① Notwithstanding Article 190 of the Local Autonomy Act and Article 81 of the Local Public Officials Act, an Audit Committee shall be established under the Mayor of the Integrated Special City to investigate, examine, verify, analyze and review (hereinafter referred to as "autonomous auditing") all affairs and activities of the Integrated Special City, its agencies and other agencies prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance (hereinafter referred to as "entities subject to auditing"), and persons belonging thereto, and to handle results under Article 92: Provided, That audits of affairs and entities in education and academic fields and persons belonging thereto shall be conducted by the head of the audit organization of the Integrated Special City Office of Education appointed by the Superintendent of Education.
② The Audit Committee shall consist of not more than seven auditors, including one chairperson (hereinafter referred to as the "Chairperson of the Audit Committee"), taking account of gender.
③ The Mayor shall appoint or commission auditors from among persons satisfying qualifications prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance; two auditors shall be persons recommended by the Integrated Special City Council and one shall be a person recommended by civil society as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
④ In selecting or recommending auditors, the Mayor and the Integrated Special City Council shall undergo deliberation by the Auditor Selection and Recommendation Committee.
⑤ The term of office of auditors who are not public officials of the Integrated Special City shall be three years.
⑥ Detailed methods and scope of autonomous auditing and standards for auditing activities shall be determined by the Chairperson of the Audit Committee following resolution by the Audit Committee.
⑦ The Audit Committee shall have independent status in performing its duties, and its independence shall be respected to the greatest possible extent in preparing budgets necessary for its organization, personnel and auditing activities.
⑧ Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Audit Committee and Auditor Selection and Recommendation Committee under paragraph ④, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ⑦, shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 89 (Chairperson of the Audit Committee)
① The Chairperson of the Audit Committee shall be appointed by the Mayor of the Integrated Special City with the consent of the Integrated Special City Council under Article 37 (3).
② The Chairperson shall represent the Audit Committee and have general control over its affairs.
③ The term of office of the Chairperson shall be three years.
④ Where the Chairperson is unable to perform duties due to unavoidable circumstances, an auditor selected as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance shall act on the Chairperson's behalf.

Article 90 (Secretariat of the Audit Committee)
① A secretariat shall be established within the Audit Committee to support autonomous auditing activities and handle administrative affairs, and secretariat staff shall be appointed by the Mayor upon recommendation of the Chairperson of the Audit Committee.
② Secretariat staff under paragraph ① shall be local public officials or firefighting officials appointed by the Mayor of the Integrated Special City under delegated appointing authority pursuant to Article 6 of the Firefighting Officials Act.
③ Matters necessary for the organization, duties and operation of the secretariat under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 91 (Autonomous audit plans)
① The Audit Committee shall establish an autonomous audit plan specifying the objectives, subjects, agencies and scope of each audit before conducting the audit to ensure systematic and effective autonomous auditing: Provided, That an autonomous audit plan may be amended while the audit is being conducted where necessary.
② The Audit Committee shall notify the head of an agency subject to an autonomous audit of the principal details of the autonomous audit plan under paragraph ① and any amended plan at least 30 days before the scheduled audit date: Provided, That this shall not apply where urgent circumstances require a prompt audit or where non-notification is unavoidable to ensure the effectiveness of the audit.
③ The Audit Committee shall notify the Board of Audit and Inspection, the Minister of the Interior and Safety, and the Mayor of the Integrated Special City of the autonomous audit plan under paragraph ① (including any amended plan) within two weeks from the date on which the plan is established.
④ Where necessary for an autonomous audit, the Audit Committee may require the following measures, limited to the minimum necessary for the audit. A person required to take such measures shall comply unless there is a justifiable reason not to do so:
1. From agencies subject to audit or persons belonging thereto: Attendance or answers, submission of relevant data, sealing of goods, examination of data entered into computerized information systems, etc.;
2. From other persons considered relevant to the matters to be audited: Cooperation in attending, answering questions and submitting relevant materials.
⑤ When auditing matters requiring specialized knowledge or practical experience, the Audit Committee may have audit officials of central administrative agencies, employees of the Integrated Special City, external professional institutions such as accounting corporations or research institutes, or specialists investigate, verify and analyze relevant matters.

Article 92 (Handling of results of autonomous audits)
① Unless there are special circumstances, the Audit Committee shall report the results of an autonomous audit to the Mayor of the Integrated Special City within 60 days after completing it.
② The results of an autonomous audit under paragraph ① shall include measures such as orders for reimbursement, disciplinary action or reprimand, correction, caution, improvement, recommendations and accusations.
③ Where measures to be taken according to the autonomous audit results reported under paragraph ① fall within the authority of the head of another agency, the Mayor shall notify the head of that agency of the relevant facts.

Article 93 (Suspension of limitation periods for disciplinary action or reprimand)
① The Audit Committee shall notify the Mayor of the Integrated Special City and the head of the agency or department subject to audit of the commencement and termination of an investigation into a specific case within ten days of each occurrence.
② From the date on which the Mayor receives notification from the Audit Committee of commencement of an investigation into a particular case under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall not proceed with disciplinary or reprimand procedures concerning that case.
③ Where disciplinary or reprimand procedures cannot proceed under paragraph ② and the limitation period for the grounds of disciplinary action or reprimand expires or has less than one month remaining, the limitation period shall be deemed to expire one month after the date of notification that the investigation has ended under paragraph ①.

Article 94 (Confidentiality and protection of status)
① Auditors who are not public officials and persons who are not public officials among those participating in audits under Article 91 (5) shall not disclose secrets acquired in the course of their duties either while in office or after leaving office.
② No auditor shall be dismissed or released from appointment against his or her will during the term of office except in any of the following cases:
1. Where the auditor becomes unable to perform duties due to a physical or mental disability;
2. Where the auditor falls under any of the subparagraphs of Article 31 of the Local Public Officials Act;
3. Where the auditor is elected as a member of the National Assembly, a head of a local government or a member of a local council;
4. Where the auditor is appointed as a public official, executive or employee of an agency subject to audit by the Audit Committee;
5. Where the auditor violates the prohibition on political activities under Article 95.
③ Where an auditor falls under paragraph ② 1, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall dismiss or release the auditor following a resolution supported by at least two thirds of the incumbent Audit Committee members: Provided, That in the case of the Chairperson of the Audit Committee, the consent of the Integrated Special City Council shall be obtained.

Article 95 (Prohibition of political activities)
An auditor who is not a public official shall not engage in political activities prescribed by Article 57 of the Local Public Officials Act and shall be deemed a public official for the purposes of applying Article 82 of that Act.

② Where an integrated spatial plan for the Integrated Special City is formulated and publicly notified, development, improvement and infrastructure projects implemented within its jurisdiction shall conform to the plan unless special circumstances exist.
③ Spatial and urban plans previously established by local governments before integration shall remain effective until the integrated spatial plan is established; following public notification of that plan, they shall be progressively revised after consistency reviews within a period prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 103 (Special provisions concerning deliberation on spatial restructuring plans)
Notwithstanding Article 35-6 (2) of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act, matters prescribed by Presidential Decree, including changes to spatial restructuring plans determined by the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, shall undergo deliberation by the local urban planning committee under Article 113 of the same Act.

Article 104 (Special provisions concerning development of housing sites)
① Notwithstanding Article 3 of the Housing Site Development Promotion Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may designate, alter or cancel designation of housing site development districts after consulting with the heads of relevant administrative agencies.
② Notwithstanding Article 3 (2) of the Housing Site Development Promotion Act, the Mayor may designate a housing site development district after consulting with the heads of relevant administrative agencies and obtaining deliberation by the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Housing Policy Deliberation Committee under Article 9 of the Framework Act on Residence.
③ Authority under Articles 8, 9 and 16 of the Housing Site Development Promotion Act concerning housing site development districts designated by the Mayor under paragraphs ① and ② shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.

Article 105 (Special provisions concerning housing construction projects)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may also exercise authority of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport under Articles 8 (1), 10 (1) and (2), 14 (1), 93 (1), and 96 of the Housing Act, limited to the Integrated Special City.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport under the proviso to Article 15 (4), the proviso to the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 16 (1), Article 16 (2), Article 19 (5), Article 31 (1), the main sentence and proviso to Article 31 (3), and Article 92 of the Housing Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. The Mayor shall obtain the prior consent of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 106 (Special provisions concerning designation of public housing districts)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may be delegated part of the authority of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport under the Special Act on Public Housing pursuant to Article 53 of the same Act. The scope and procedures of delegation shall be governed, mutatis mutandis, by Article 53.
② Notwithstanding paragraph ①, for public housing district development projects with an area of at least 300,000 square meters, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may expand the scope of authority delegated to the Mayor as prescribed by Presidential Decree, limited to projects implemented by public housing business operators under Article 4 (1) 3 of the Special Act on Public Housing.
③ When approving a public housing district development project under authority delegated pursuant to paragraph ②, the Mayor shall consult in advance with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the heads of relevant central administrative agencies as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 107 (Special provisions concerning specialized public rental housing)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may supply public rental housing designed to contribute to improving residents' quality of life and supporting independence by providing customized spaces and integrated services according to the characteristics and housing needs of single-person households, persons eligible for national veterans' benefits, young people, persons with disabilities and older persons (hereinafter referred to as "specialized public rental housing"), in the form of publicly constructed rental housing or publicly purchased rental housing under Article 2 of the Special Act on Public Housing.
② The Mayor may entrust the operation and management of specialized public rental housing, as prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport, to social enterprises under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Social Enterprise Promotion Act, social cooperatives under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Framework Act on Cooperatives, or nonprofit corporations established under the Civil Act or other Acts, etc., that have expertise and capacity in the relevant field. The State may provide necessary support to promote citizen welfare and balanced development of the Integrated Special City.
③ Eligibility for residence, rental conditions, quality standards of services provided, selection, evaluation and management of operating institutions, and other matters necessary for specialized public rental housing may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. The Mayor shall obtain the prior consent of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 108 (Special provisions concerning supply for home childcare centers)
① Notwithstanding Article 49-9 of the Special Act on Public Housing, the establishment and operation of home childcare centers in public rental housing shall fall under the authority of the Mayor of the Integrated Special City. The Mayor may establish a rental period of up to nine years for such centers.
② Where the Mayor intends to lease some public rental housing units to persons wishing to establish or operate home childcare centers under paragraph ①, the Mayor may request from the heads of Sis, Guns and Gus having jurisdiction data necessary to assess childcare demand in the public rental housing.
③ Notwithstanding paragraph ①, eligibility for occupancy, selection methods and rental conditions for persons seeking to establish and operate home childcare centers shall be governed by the Special Act on Public Housing.
④ Notwithstanding Article 57-2 (1) of the Housing Act, a person who rents public rental housing under paragraph ① to establish and operate a home childcare center need not reside in that housing.

Article 109 (Requests for designation of areas subject to a price ceiling on the sale of housing)
Where an area has a rate of increase in housing prices substantially higher than the rate of inflation under Article 57 (1) 2 of the Housing Act, and housing prices have risen sharply or are likely to rise sharply in view of local housing prices, transactions and housing market conditions, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may designate the area and request the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to designate it as subject to the price ceiling on the sale of housing.

Article 110 (Requests for designation of adjustment target areas)
The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may identify an area falling under either of the following subparagraphs pursuant to Article 63-2 (1) of the Housing Act and request the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to designate it as an adjustment target area:
1. An area where housing sales, etc. are overheated or likely to become overheated, considering housing prices, subscription competition rates, volumes of resale of rights to purchase housing and housing supply rates, etc.;
2. An area where transactions involving sales of newly supplied housing, housing purchases, etc. are depressed or likely to become depressed, considering housing prices, transaction volumes, unsold housing and housing supply rates, etc.

Article 112 (Special provisions concerning public notification of geographical names)
The authority of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to publicly notify geographical names under Articles 91-2 (5) and 91-3 (6) of the Act on the Establishment and Management of Spatial Data shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, except with respect to names covering two or more Cities or Dos (including the Integrated Special City).

Article 113 (Special provisions concerning installation of works of art in buildings)
Notwithstanding Article 9 (1) of the Culture and Arts Promotion Act, the scale criteria for each type of building within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City required to spend a certain amount on installing works of art may be differently prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 114 (Special provisions concerning the Protection of Military Bases and Installations Act)
① Notwithstanding Article 4 of the Protection of Military Bases and Installations Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City or the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu may recommend to the commander of the unit having jurisdiction the designation, alteration or cancellation of a protected area.
② Where a recommendation made under paragraph ① is not reflected, the commander of the unit having jurisdiction shall explain the reasons.
③ Where deemed necessary, the Minister of National Defense may commission, as a member of the Ministry of National Defense Deliberation Committee on Protection of Military Bases and Installations under Article 15 (1) of the Protection of Military Bases and Installations Act, a person recommended by the Mayor of the Integrated Special City who falls under any of the following subparagraphs:
1. A public official of a relevant local government;
2. An officer or employee of a public institution under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
3. An officer or employee of a local public enterprise established by the Integrated Special City or a Si, Gun or Gu under the Local Public Enterprises Act;
4. An officer or researcher of a research institute funded by a local government and established by the Integrated Special City under the Act on the Establishment and Operation of Research Institutes Funded by Local Governments.
④ Methods and procedures for designation, alteration or cancellation of protected areas under paragraph ① shall be governed by the Protection of Military Bases and Installations Act.
⑤ When establishing a master plan for management of protected areas, etc. under Article 16 of the Protection of Military Bases and Installations Act, the Minister of National Defense shall hear the opinion of the Mayor of the Integrated Special City in advance.

Article 115 (Provision of information on unused military sites)
① At the request of the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, the Minister of National Defense shall provide the Mayor with information concerning land within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City that is not used as a military unit site (meaning a military unit site under Article 2, subparagraph 5 of the Act on National Defense and Military Installations Projects) following consolidation, abolition or relocation of military units under the Defense Reform Master Plan pursuant to Article 5 of the Defense Reform Act (hereinafter referred to as "unused military sites").
② The Mayor of the Integrated Special City or the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu may submit opinions to the Minister of National Defense concerning the disposal of unused military sites.

Article 116 (Methods of disposal of unused military sites)
① Before releasing requisition of, transferring, selling or otherwise disposing of an unused military site, the Minister of National Defense shall remove above-ground structures, underground buried objects, hazardous substances, soil contamination, etc.: Provided, That this shall not apply in any of the following cases:
1. Where the Minister of National Defense intends to sell or otherwise dispose of above-ground structures: Provided, That above-ground structures other than those intended for disposal, underground buried objects, hazardous substances, soil contamination, etc. shall be removed;
2. Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City or the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu intends to continue using above-ground structures or underground buried objects: Provided, That above-ground structures or underground buried objects other than those to be used, hazardous substances, soil contamination, etc. shall be removed;
3. Where the Mayor or the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu agrees to remove above-ground structures, underground buried objects, hazardous substances, soil contamination, etc. and the Minister of National Defense agrees to bear the relevant expenses;
4. Where the Mayor or the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu removes above-ground structures, underground buried objects, hazardous substances, soil contamination, etc. at its own expense.
② Soil contamination removal under paragraph ① shall comply with the purification standards and methods under Article 15-3 of the Soil Environment Conservation Act.
③ Where unused military land is sold to a person who has removed or improved above-ground structures, underground buried objects, hazardous substances, soil contamination, etc. under paragraph ①, the sale price shall be the value of the land in its condition after removal and improvement at the time of sale less the amount equivalent to the expenses of removal and improvement.

Article 117 (Special provisions on disposal of unused military sites)
① Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City or the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu intends to use unused military sites to implement public works under Article 4 of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects (hereinafter referred to as "public works" in this Article), the Minister of National Defense shall actively cooperate.
② Where the Mayor or the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu requests release of requisition of an unused military site under Article 15 (1) of the Requisition Act or cancellation of designation as a protected area for military bases and installations under Article 4 (1) and (2) of the Protection of Military Bases and Installations Act to implement public works thereon, the Minister of National Defense shall give priority to examining such requests.
③ Public works implemented on unused military sites shall be deemed public projects under Article 20-2 (2) of the Special Measures Act on the Adjustment of Requisitioned Property and Article 4 (2) of the Special Measures Act on the Adjustment of Land Expropriated or Used under the Special Measures Decree on Expropriation and Use of Land in Areas Subject to Mobilization pursuant to Article 5 (4) of the Act on Special Measures for National Security.
④ Where the Mayor or the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu intends to purchase unused military sites or continue using above-ground structures, etc. thereon, the Minister of National Defense may exchange such sites or structures for public property belonging to the Integrated Special City or relevant Si, Gun or Gu that is currently used by a military unit and is planned for continued military use.
⑤ Where the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu deems that a building on an unused military site has no defects impeding its use in terms of structural safety, sanitation, fire prevention, etc., the building may be entered in the building register notwithstanding Article 38 (1) of the Building Act.

Article 118 (Special provisions on metropolitan transportation improvement projects)
① Notwithstanding Article 2, subparagraph 2 (a) and (b) of the Special Act on the Management of Metropolitan Transportation in Metropolitan Areas, roads extending across the former Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City shall be deemed included in the scope of metropolitan roads under item (a), and urban railways and railways operating across the former Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City shall be deemed included in the scope of metropolitan railways under item (b).
② The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall establish the master plan and implementation plan for metropolitan transportation with respect to the Integrated Special City under paragraph ①, and the State may provide support under Article 10 (1) of the Special Act on the Management of Metropolitan Transportation in Metropolitan Areas to prevent disadvantages arising from integration; financial support therefor may be borne by the State under Article 10 (2) of the same Act.
③ The State may bear expenses incurred in operating metropolitan transportation facilities (excluding metropolitan railways) to facilitate the early establishment of the Integrated Special City.
④ Paragraphs ① through ③ shall also apply to projects for constructing or improving metropolitan transportation facilities whose implementation procedures are ongoing pursuant to relevant statutes when this Act enters into force.

Article 119 (Special provisions concerning road projects of the Integrated Special City)
① Notwithstanding Article 85 of the Road Act, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may provide financial support for the following road projects requested by the Mayor of the Integrated Special City as necessary to achieve the objectives of this Act, including balanced national development and establishment of economic hubs:
1. Roads within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City (including local roads of Jeollanam-do before the establishment of the Integrated Special City) connecting to investment promotion districts under Article 164 (1), forest use promotion districts under Article 380 (1), etc.: Provided, That this shall be limited to roads designated under Articles 11, 12 and 15 (2) of the Road Act;
2. Metropolitan roads under Article 2, subparagraph 2 (a) of the Special Act on the Management of Metropolitan Transportation in Metropolitan Areas;
3. Traffic-congestion roads under Article 8 of the Road Act;
4. Express national highways designated under Article 11 of the Road Act;
5. Local roads supported by the State and designated under Article 15 of the Road Act;
6. Other roads prescribed by Presidential Decree.
② Paragraph ① shall also apply to ongoing projects for constructing or improving express national highways or metropolitan roads whose implementation procedures were underway under relevant statutes when this Act entered into force.

Article 120 (Special provisions concerning transportation networks for balanced development)
Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City requests the establishment of transportation networks to strengthen connections between metropolitan living zones under Article 23, economic zones such as industrial complexes, and surrounding cities and to promote balanced development within the Integrated Special City, the State may, where deemed necessary, reflect the requests in the following plans:
1. The national railway network development plan under Article 4 of the Act on the Construction and Maintenance of Railways and Railroad Facilities;
2. The comprehensive national road network plan under Article 5 of the Road Act.

Article 121 (Special provisions concerning urban railway projects of the Integrated Special City)
① Even where the jurisdictional urban transportation area changes upon establishment of the Integrated Special City, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall deem the urban railway to constitute the transportation facilities and means of the urban transportation area under the former jurisdiction of Gwangju Metropolitan City.
② The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may bear part of the financial support for urban railway construction under Articles 18 and 22 of the Urban Railroad Act.

Article 122 (Special financial provisions for supra-regional transportation projects)
① Where an extension or expansion of supra-regional transportation projects, including metropolitan express railways, planned and determined by the State is reflected in the national railway network development plan under Article 4 of the Act on the Construction and Maintenance of Railways and Railroad Facilities, part of the additional project costs may be supported from national funds.
② Where local funding is required for the project costs under paragraph ①, the Integrated Special City shall bear such costs.

Article 123 (Support for private investment projects)
① The State and the Integrated Special City may provide the following support to project implementers carrying out private investment projects for infrastructure projects under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Act on Public-Private Partnerships in Infrastructure:
1. Permission to occupy public facilities;
2. Acting on behalf of the implementer in purchasing land, facilities, etc. necessary for projects;
3. Implementing ancillary projects under Article 21 of the Act on Public-Private Partnerships in Infrastructure;
4. Expenses incurred in installing, improving or reinforcing traffic safety facilities mandatorily required due to enactment or amendment of relevant statutes;
5. Permission to use State or public property needed for ancillary projects;
6. Expenses of toll reductions or exemptions implemented to achieve carbon neutrality or guarantee human rights of persons with disabilities under the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth for Coping with Climate Crisis and the Toll Road Act;
7. Acting on behalf of the implementer in purchasing land, facilities, etc. necessary for ancillary projects;
8. Other matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.
② Where another authority is responsible for permitting occupation of public facilities under paragraph ① 1, the State and the Integrated Special City may request the authority to grant such permission, and the authority shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 124 (Reduction or exemption of charges for private investment)
Where necessary to facilitate private investment in areas facing the risk of regional extinction, the State and the Integrated Special City may reduce, exempt or refrain from imposing development charges, expenses for alternative forest resource creation, river occupation and use fees, traffic inducement charges, ecosystem conservation charges, public waters occupation and use fees, environmental improvement charges, infrastructure installation expenses and metropolitan transportation facility charges as prescribed by the Restitution of Development Gains Act, Mountainous Districts Management Act, River Act, Urban Traffic Improvement Promotion Act, Natural Environment Conservation Act, Public Waters Management and Reclamation Act, Environmental Improvement Cost Allocation Act, National Land Planning and Utilization Act, and Special Act on the Management of Metropolitan Transportation in Metropolitan Areas.

Article 125 (Special provisions concerning metropolitan traffic-congestion road improvement projects)
① Notwithstanding Article 8 of the Road Act, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall recognize that criteria for selecting metropolitan traffic-congestion road improvement projects in the Integrated Special City include both of the following and shall ensure that integration causes no disadvantage in national funding or otherwise:
1. Improvement of metropolitan traffic-congestion roads in Dong areas of the former Gwangju Metropolitan City before establishment of the Integrated Special City;
2. Improvement of metropolitan traffic-congestion roads in Dong areas of Jeollanam-do after establishment of the Integrated Special City.
② Notwithstanding the main sentence of Article 86 (2) of the Road Act, at least 50 percent of the total project costs (including survey and design expenses) incurred when the Mayor implements a detailed project plan for improving metropolitan traffic-congestion roads may be subsidized by the State.

Article 126 (Special provisions concerning bus rapid transit systems)
① Where regulatory special provisions are granted under Article 12 of the Act on the Promotion of and Support for Mobility Innovation to exclusive-use vehicles under Article 2, subparagraph 4 of the Special Act on the Construction and Operation of Bus Rapid Transit Systems operating in the Integrated Special City, Article 29 (4) of the Motor Vehicle Management Act may be disapplied during the relevant period.
② To resolve transportation problems between the former Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City within the Integrated Special City, the State shall support expenses necessary for introducing environmentally friendly exclusive-use vehicles under Article 32 (3) of the Special Act on the Construction and Operation of Bus Rapid Transit Systems, thereby ensuring that no disadvantage results from integration.
③ The State shall ensure that no disadvantage results from integration through financial support under Article 32 (1) of the Special Act on the Construction and Operation of Bus Rapid Transit Systems.

Article 127 (Special provisions concerning advertisements using means of transportation)
Notwithstanding Article 3 (3) of the Act on the Management of Outdoor Advertisements, etc. and Promotion of Outdoor Advertisement Industry, the methods of displaying advertisements on exclusive-use vehicles under Article 2, subparagraph 4 of the Special Act on the Construction and Operation of Bus Rapid Transit Systems operating within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City may be differently prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 128 (Special provisions concerning types of passenger transport businesses)
The authority of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport (excluding authority over passenger transport businesses for which licenses under Article 4 of the Passenger Transport Service Act have not been delegated to the Chairperson of the Metropolitan Transport Commission or Mayors/Do Governors under Article 75 of that Act and authority to determine standards and rates of fares and charges under Article 8 of that Act that has not been delegated under Article 75) and the authority of Mayors/Do Governors under Articles 4, 8 through 10, 13 through 16, 20 and 23 of that Act shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City. Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport under the main sentence and proviso to Article 4 (1), Article 4 (3), the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 4 (4), Article 4 (4) 4, the former and latter parts of Article 4 (5), the former part of Article 8 (2), Article 8 (3) and (5), Article 9 (4), the former part of Article 11, the former and latter parts of Article 14 (1) and (2), the main sentence of Article 15 (4), Article 16 (2) and (3), Article 18 (1) and (2), Article 20 (2), (3) and (5), the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 21 (1), the latter part of Article 21 (7), Article 21 (8), the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 21 (9), the latter part of Article 21 (11), the former part of Article 21 (12), Article 21 (13), Article 23 (3), the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 24 (4), Article 24-2 (1) through (3), Article 26 (1) 1, 2, 7 and 9, the latter part of Article 26 (3), Article 27 (2), the main sentence and proviso to Article 27-2 (1), and the main sentence of Article 27-3 (1), Article 27-3 (2) and (8) of the Passenger Transport Service Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. Where an ordinance is intended to prescribe standards different from those under the relevant statutes, the Mayor shall obtain the prior consent of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 129 (Special provisions concerning passenger transport platform businesses)
① The powers of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport under Articles 49-3, 49-5 through 49-7, 49-13 through 49-15, 49-18 and 49-19 of the Passenger Transport Service Act with respect to passenger transport platform businesses whose service areas are limited to the Integrated Special City shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
② Article 49-9 of the Passenger Transport Service Act shall apply to matters necessary for passenger transport platform businesses other than those prescribed in paragraph ①.

Article 130 (Special financial support for passenger transport platform business operators)
① Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City deems financial support necessary for a passenger transport platform business operator undertaking any of the following projects, the Mayor may subsidize or lend part of the funds necessary for that operator as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance:
1. Installing or improving facilities and equipment necessary for passenger transport platform businesses;
2. Expanding and improving facilities and equipment supporting economical, environmentally friendly and safe driving and management;
3. Other matters prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance to promote passenger transport platform businesses.
② At the request of the Mayor of the Integrated Special City on any of the following grounds, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may subsidize or lend part of the funds necessary for the operator. Matters concerning eligible recipients, methods and repayment of subsidies or loans shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. Where a passenger transport platform business operator undertakes a project under any subparagraph of paragraph ①;
2. Where it is necessary to expand traffic safety facilities for passenger safety.
③ A business operator receiving a subsidy or loan under paragraphs ① and ② shall not use such funds for purposes other than those for which they were granted or lent.
④ The Mayor shall supervise business operators receiving subsidies or loans under paragraphs ① and ② to ensure proper use of the funds.
⑤ Where a business operator obtains a subsidy or loan under paragraphs ① and ② by false or other improper means, the Mayor shall order the operator to return it and, if the operator fails to comply, may recover the funds in accordance with the procedures for disposition of delinquent national or local taxes.

Article 131 (Special provisions concerning standards and rates of fares and charges)
Notwithstanding Article 75 (1) of the Passenger Transport Service Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall be deemed delegated authority over fares and charges for passenger transport platform businesses within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City.

Article 132 (Duties of persons engaging in passenger transport platform services)
① Persons engaging in passenger transport platform services whose service areas are the Integrated Special City shall not engage in acts liable to impair service quality and shall be subject to Article 16 of the Act on the Development of Taxi Transportation Business concerning prohibited conduct of taxi transport employees.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport under Article 16 (3) of the Act on the Development of Taxi Transportation Business may be differently prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. Where the ordinance is intended to prescribe standards different from those under the relevant statutes, the Mayor shall obtain the prior consent of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.

Article 133 (Special provisions concerning taxi business areas)
① The authority of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport over designation and alteration of business areas within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City under Articles 5 (1), 5 (2) 3 and 19-2 (1) of the Act on the Development of Taxi Transportation Business shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City: Provided, That where the Mayor designates or alters a business area including facilities such as high-speed railway stations, airports (limited to airports operating scheduled international flights under the Aviation Business Act), ports (limited to trading ports equipped with passenger facilities under the Harbor Act), or multimodal transfer centers under Article 2, subparagraph 15 of the National Transport System Efficiency Act, the Mayor shall consult in advance with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and reflect the results in the designation or alteration.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under Article 5 (6) of the Act on the Development of Taxi Transportation Business may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 134 (Support for operation of public transportation)
① To promote citizen welfare and balanced development of the Integrated Special City, the State may support part of the losses incurred from operating public transportation routes serving remote areas between the former Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support for public transportation projects requested by the Mayor of the Integrated Special City to achieve the purposes of this Act.
③ Notwithstanding Article 32 (1) of the Framework Act on the Development of Railroad Industry, the obligation of the person causing costs to bear the following costs incurred through a railroad operator's provision of public interest services may be exempted for metropolitan railway routes passing through population-declining areas under Article 2, subparagraph 12 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City: <Amended on 2026.6.2>
1. Amounts of reductions in railway fares and charges granted by a railroad operator pursuant to other statutes or for national policies or public purposes;
2. Operating losses incurred from maintaining basic railway services for public purposes where, despite appropriate management improvement measures taken by the railroad operator, demand is so low that it is extremely difficult to achieve a balance between revenue and expenses, or where services at a station would otherwise have to be restricted or discontinued;
3. Expenses incurred by a railroad operator in implementing special-purpose national projects.
④ To guarantee the mobility rights of persons with reduced mobility and eliminate disparities in mobility between regions, the State may support expenses necessary for introducing and operating special transportation services under the Act on Promotion of Transportation Convenience of Mobility Disadvantaged Persons.

Article 135 (Special provisions concerning designation of transportation and logistics hubs)
① Notwithstanding Article 37 of the National Transport System Efficiency Act, where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City requests designation of a transportation and logistics hub within the Integrated Special City for balanced regional development, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may give priority to consideration of the request. Where a port is included in the transportation and logistics hub, the Minister shall consult with the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for establishing and operating transportation and logistics hubs designated under paragraph ①.

Article 136 (Special provisions concerning support for locally managed ports)
① Notwithstanding Article 79 (1) of the Harbor Act, the State may subsidize part of the costs of ports managed by the Integrated Special City in any of the following cases:
1. Where the port contributes to balanced regional development and improved transportation and logistics convenience for island and remote-area residents;
2. Where linkage to a large-scale national project, such as offshore wind power, is deemed necessary;
3. Where recovery and restoration following a major disaster, such as the April 16 Sewol Ferry Disaster, are necessary;
4. Where State support is otherwise deemed necessary to secure the public nature of the port.
② The objects, ratios, procedures and standards of subsidies under paragraph ① and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 137 (Support for above-ground installation of environmentally friendly vehicle charging facilities)
Where charging facilities for environmentally friendly vehicles are to be installed above ground within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City or underground charging facilities are to be relocated above ground under Article 11-2 (1) and (2) of the Act on Promotion of Development and Distribution of Environment-Friendly Motor Vehicles, the State may support the necessary expenses.

Article 138 (Special provisions concerning public housing in areas with declining populations)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may supply public rental housing under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Special Act on Public Housing (excluding public rental housing intended for conversion to sale), exclusively to young people and newly married couples, in areas with declining populations under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Special Act on Support for Areas with Declining Populations and areas of concern for population decline under subparagraph 1-2 of the same Article, in accordance with criteria and procedures separately determined following consultation with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
② When supplying public rental housing under paragraph ①, the Mayor may separately prescribe the following matters following consultation with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport:
1. Rental conditions for public rental housing under Article 49 of the Special Act on Public Housing;
2. Standard lease contracts for public rental housing under Article 49-2 of the Special Act on Public Housing;
3. Cancellation or termination of lease contracts and refusal to renew lease contracts under Article 49-3 of the Special Act on Public Housing.

Article 139 (Special provisions concerning station-area development)
① Notwithstanding Articles 8 and 9 of the Act on the Development and Use of Station Areas and Articles 36, 77 and 78 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may establish a project plan for changing development zones within station areas to use zones permitting high-density development or relaxing restrictions on building coverage and floor-area ratios.
② Matters necessary for changes of use zones and relaxation of building coverage and floor-area ratio restrictions under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree within the scope of Articles 77 and 78 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act.

Article 140 (Special provisions concerning State property for station-area development)
① Where deemed necessary to revitalize station areas within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City and implement projects efficiently, the State may, notwithstanding the State Property Act, permit project implementers designated and publicly notified by the Mayor of the Integrated Special City for station-area development projects to use, profit from or borrow State property at reduced rates (hereinafter referred to as "lease" in this Article).
② Notwithstanding Article 18 (1) of the State Property Act, the State may permit a project implementer under Article 12 of the Act on the Development and Use of Station Areas to construct buildings or other permanent facilities on railroad facilities under Article 3, subparagraph 2 of the Framework Act on the Development of Railroad Industry for which permission for occupation has been obtained. In such cases, conditions shall be imposed requiring donation of such facilities to the State or restoration to their original condition and return upon expiration of the lease, considering the types of facilities, etc.

Article 141 (Special provisions concerning designation of regional revitalization areas)
Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City requests designation of a regional revitalization area under Article 67 of the Regional Development and Support Act, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may designate the relevant area.

Article 142 (Special provisions on revitalization of regional station areas)
① The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall formulate policies to create an industrial ecosystem in which diverse economic activities and values can be generated through a network of railway stations linking stations with surrounding areas.
② Railway business operators (meaning railway business operators under Article 2, subparagraph 8 of the Railroad Business Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) shall cooperate with the State and local governments in supporting the formulation and implementation of comprehensive policies for developing and supporting railway economic zones within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City.
③ The State, the Integrated Special City and railway business operators may support the establishment of infrastructure necessary to create railway economic zones.
④ Notwithstanding Article 44 of the National Transport System Efficiency Act, where the Mayor requests establishment of a multimodal transfer center within the Integrated Special City for balanced national and regional development, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may give priority to reflecting the request in the master plan under that Article.

Article 143 (Special provisions concerning development of innovation cities)
① The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may provide administrative and financial support for developing innovation cities in the Integrated Special City (meaning innovation cities under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Special Act on the Construction and Development of Innovation Cities).
② The State shall ensure that integration causes no disadvantages when designating prospective innovation city development districts within the Integrated Special City's jurisdiction under Article 2, subparagraph 4 of the Special Act on the Construction and Development of Innovation Cities even after establishment of the Integrated Special City.

Article 144 (Special provisions concerning relocation of public institutions)
① When implementing policies to relocate public institutions from the Seoul metropolitan area to other regions under Article 25 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth, the State shall give priority to considering the Integrated Special City as a destination. <Amended on 2026.6.2>
② Notwithstanding Article 29 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may sell public property by negotiated contract to the head of a public institution under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions situated within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City established under this Act.
③ Notwithstanding Article 47 of the Special Act on the Construction and Development of Innovation Cities, the head of a relocated public institution may prepare and implement support measures, including relocation allowances, for relocating employees and their families as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
④ Notwithstanding Article 29-2 of the Special Act on the Construction and Development of Innovation Cities, the ratio for recruiting local talent from the Integrated Special City may be separately determined and increased for relocated public institutions.

Article 145 (Special provisions concerning sale of public property to attract public institutions)
Notwithstanding Article 29 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may sell public property by negotiated contract to the head of a public institution under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions in a population-declining area under Article 2, subparagraph 12 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth. <Amended on 2026.6.2>

Article 146 (Special provisions concerning support for areas surrounding relocated military airports)
① Where a military airport is relocated within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City under the Special Act on the Relocation of Military Airports and Support Therefor and the Special Act on Relocation of Gwangju Military Airport and Development of the Former Site, the Integrated Special City may subsidize part of the expenses necessary for support projects from its own financial resources notwithstanding Article 9 (2) of the Special Act on the Relocation of Military Airports and Support Therefor.
② Matters concerning the raising and operation of the financial resources under paragraph ① and other matters necessary for supporting areas surrounding relocated military airports may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ Where a military airport is relocated within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City under the Acts specified in paragraph ①, the Mayor may designate a target area and request the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to designate a national industrial complex notwithstanding Article 6 (2) of the Industrial Sites and Development Act, to achieve balanced development and acceptance by residents in the surrounding relocation area. In such cases, the Mayor shall consult with the heads of relevant administrative agencies in advance.
④ Methods and procedures for designation of national industrial complexes under paragraph ③ shall be governed by the Industrial Sites and Development Act and the Special Act on Simplification of Approval and Permission Procedures for Industrial Complexes.

Article 147 (Support for military airport relocation, etc.)
① The Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall formulate and implement policies to create an industrial ecosystem in which diverse economic activities and values can be generated through aviation networks connecting Muan Airport with its surrounding areas.
② An airport operator (meaning an airport operator under Article 2, subparagraph 34 of the Aviation Business Act; hereinafter the same shall apply) may cooperate with and provide necessary support to the State and local governments to create the industrial ecosystem under paragraph ①.
③ The State, the Integrated Special City and airport operators may provide aviation business operators with administrative and financial support necessary for operations to revitalize airports, including attracting international routes.

Article 148 (Securing global logistics competitiveness)
The Government shall endeavor to efficiently and organically integrate maritime, aviation and road logistics systems to enable the Integrated Special City to secure competitiveness as a multimodal logistics hub.

Article 149 (Special provisions on relaxation of standards for designation of free trade zones in port hinterlands)
Notwithstanding Article 5, subparagraph 1 of the Act on the Designation and Management of Free Trade Zones, where a free trade zone is to be designated in a port under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Harbor Act or its hinterland within the Integrated Special City, the Mayor may, following consultation with relevant agencies, including the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries, request the Minister of Trade and Industry to relax the criteria for designating a free trade zone. Where the Minister of Trade and Industry finds such a request reasonable, the Minister may apply relaxed designation criteria.

CHAPTER II INDUSTRIAL REVITALIZATION

Article 150 (Establishment of basic plans)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall establish a basic plan for the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as the "basic plan"). The Mayor shall consult in advance with the Minister of Education and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City concerning matters under paragraph ② 10.
② The basic plan shall include the following matters:
1. Basic policies for creating and developing the Integrated Special City;
2. Balanced regional development and enhancement of the welfare of residents of the Integrated Special City;
3. Designation of living and economic zones and development, improvement and conservation of metropolitan living zones;
4. Population policies, including expansion of the living population;
5. Local diplomacy, including international exchanges and international cooperation;
6. Improvement of spatial structures and planned utilization and management of land by use;
7. Development of local communities and improvements in living conditions, including safety and disaster prevention;
8. Plans and implementation of regional strategic industries;
9. Development of local tourism industries and utilization, development and conservation of tourism resources;
10. Promotion of education and development of human resources;
11. Medical services, public health and social welfare;
12. Promotion of agriculture, forestry, livestock and fisheries;
13. Conservation and management of the environment and utilization and development of land, water and other natural resources;
14. Utilization, development and conservation of marine areas;
15. Conservation of local culture and promotion of culture and the arts;
16. Establishment and promotion of infrastructure for informatization;
17. Institutional improvements, including regulatory innovation to strengthen autonomy;
18. Procurement of investment resources necessary for development projects (meaning projects implemented under the basic plan; hereinafter referred to as "development projects") and establishment of annual investment plans;
19. Plans for metropolitan facilities (meaning project plans concerning transportation, water supply, sewage treatment, waste treatment, energy supply and information and communication facilities within the same living zone);
20. Other matters deemed necessary by the Mayor.
③ When establishing or amending a basic plan, the Mayor shall undergo consultation on a strategic environmental impact assessment under Article 16 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
④ The Mayor shall revise and supplement the basic plan every five years.
⑤ Paragraph ① shall apply mutatis mutandis where the Mayor amends a basic plan established under that paragraph: Provided, That this shall not apply to amendments to minor matters prescribed by Presidential Decree.
⑥ Procedures and methods for establishing basic plans shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 151 (Finalization of basic plans)
① When establishing, amending or abolishing a basic plan, the Mayor shall report to the Integrated Special City Council.
