② When establishing, amending or abolishing a basic plan, the Mayor shall publicly notify it as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance and notify the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, the Support Committee and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City.

Article 152 (Basic Plan Deliberation Council)
① A Basic Plan Deliberation Council (hereinafter referred to as the "Deliberation Council") shall be established in the Integrated Special City to deliberate on the following matters:
1. Establishment, amendment and abolition of basic plans;
2. Comprehensive coordination of basic plans;
3. Reflection of residents' opinions in basic plans and residents' participation;
4. Return of development gains to local communities;
5. Evaluation of basic plans;
6. Designation and cancellation of investment promotion districts under Articles 164 and 165;
7. Designation, alteration and cancellation of rural vitality promotion special zones under Article 277;
8. Designation, alteration and cancellation of forest use promotion districts under Article 380;
9. Other matters prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② The Deliberation Council shall consist of not more than 20 members, including one chairperson and two vice chairpersons, classified as ex officio members and commissioned members.
③ The Mayor shall serve as chairperson; the vice chairpersons shall be a Vice Mayor designated by the Mayor and one person elected by the Deliberation Council.
④ Ex officio members of the Deliberation Council shall be the following persons, and commissioned members shall be appointed by the Mayor as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance:
1. A Deputy Superintendent of Education appointed as a state public official under the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City pursuant to Article 30 (1) of the Local Education Autonomy Act;
2. A state public official in the Senior Civil Service Corps belonging to a special local administrative agency located within the Integrated Special City;
3. A public official in the Senior Civil Service Corps of the Korea Forest Service.
⑤ Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Deliberation Council, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ④, shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 153 (Application of Acts to development projects)
Where matters concerning implementation of a development project are not prescribed by another Act, the Mayor shall apply this Act: Provided, That development projects involving foreign investment shall be governed by the Foreign Investment Promotion Act and industrial complex development projects by the Industrial Sites and Development Act.

Article 154 (Preliminary surveys)
① The Mayor or a person intending to implement a development project may conduct preliminary surveys as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance to establish a project plan under Article 156.
② Preliminary surveys under paragraph ① shall include the project's effects on natural ecosystems and landscapes within the development project district and other matters prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ Where deemed necessary for a preliminary survey under paragraph ①, the Mayor or a person intending to implement the project may enter land owned or occupied by another person or temporarily use it for storage of materials, passage or temporary roads.
④ Articles 130 and 131 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to compensation for losses arising from entry onto or temporary use of land under paragraph ③.

Article 155 (Designation of development project implementers)
The Mayor shall designate a development project implementer from among persons falling under the following subparagraphs: Provided, That where a private investment project is to be implemented under the Act on Public-Private Partnerships in Infrastructure, an entity prescribed by that Act shall implement it:
1. The State or a local government;
2. Public institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree;
3. Government-funded institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree;
4. Local public corporations established under the Local Public Enterprises Act;
5. Persons falling under Article 11 (1) 5 through 9, 9-2, 10 or 11 of the Urban Development Act.

Article 156 (Approval for implementation of development projects)
① A person intending to implement a development project shall obtain approval for its implementation from the Mayor: Provided, That where the person intending to implement the project is the State, a public institution under Article 4 (1) of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, or a local public enterprise established by the Integrated Special City under the Local Public Enterprises Act, the person shall hear the Mayor's opinion.
② The scope of development projects for which approval for implementation or hearing the Mayor's opinion is required under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ A person seeking implementation approval or the Mayor's opinion under paragraph ① shall prepare and submit a project plan and accompanying documents to the Mayor as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. The plan and accompanying documents submitted shall include measures for giving priority to employing residents of the Integrated Special City.
④ As prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance, the Mayor may grant implementation approval under paragraph ① subject to supplementation where some requirements for the project plan and accompanying documents are incomplete.
⑤ A development project shall commence within one year from the date on which implementation approval is obtained under paragraph ①: Provided, That where postponement is unavoidable, the Mayor may extend the commencement deadline once, for a period not exceeding one year.
⑥ Where a development project is not commenced by the deadline under paragraph ⑤ following implementation approval under paragraph ①, that approval shall cease to be effective on the day following expiration of the commencement deadline. In such cases, the Mayor shall publicly announce that fact as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑦ Upon an application by a person seeking approval under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall, unless there is a special reason not to do so, designate a responsible public official to handle affairs concerning project implementation approval.
⑧ Paragraphs ① through ⑦ shall apply mutatis mutandis to changes to an existing development project: Provided, That this shall not apply to changes to minor matters prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑨ Where the Mayor grants approval for implementation of a development project, the Mayor shall publicly notify the approval as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. The same shall apply to changes to a development project approved for implementation.

Article 157 (Deemed authorization and permission)
① Where a person intending to implement a development project under any of Article 155, subparagraphs 1 through 4 obtains approval or approval of changes for implementing a development project under Article 156, the person shall be deemed to have obtained the following permissions, authorizations, designations, approvals, consultations, reports, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "authorization and permission, etc."), limited to matters consulted on in advance with the heads of the administrative agencies responsible for such authorization and permission (including completion of procedures for deliberation or hearing opinions under relevant statutes). Upon public notification of project implementation approval under Article 156 (9), authorization and permission, etc. under relevant Acts shall be deemed publicly notified or announced:
1. Building permission under Article 11 of the Building Act; building reports under Article 14, changes to permits and reported matters under Article 16, permission to construct and reports of construction of temporary buildings under Article 20, consultations on construction of public buildings under Article 29, and reports on construction of structures under Article 83 of that Act;
2. Permission to extract aggregates under Article 22 of the Aggregate Extraction Act;
3. Reports on commencement, changes and completion of projects under Article 86 (1) of the Act on the Establishment and Management of Spatial Data;
4. Permission to occupy or use public waters under Article 8, consultation or approval under Article 10, approval of implementation plans for occupation or use under Article 17, licenses to reclaim public waters under Article 28, public notification of reclamation licenses under Article 33, consultation or approval concerning reclamation by the State, etc. under Article 35, approval of implementation plans for reclamation of public waters under Article 38, and approval of changes to reclamation purposes under Article 49 of the Public Waters Management and Reclamation Act;
5. Changes or abolition of use of public property under Article 11 and permission to use it under Article 20 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act;
6. Approval of business plans under Article 15, permissions, cancellations and reports under the subparagraphs of Article 16 (1), designation of tourist destinations under Article 52, approval of development plans under Article 54, and permission to implement development projects under Article 55 of the Tourism Promotion Act;
7. Establishment of intelligent transportation system implementation plans under Article 76 and establishment and approval of implementation plans under Article 79 of the National Transport System Efficiency Act;
8. Permission to use administrative property under Article 30 of the State Property Act;
9. Determination of urban or Gun management plans under Article 30 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act (limited to plans under Article 2, subparagraph 4 (c) and (e) of that Act), permission to occupy or use common utility tunnels under Article 44-3 (2), permission for development activities under Article 56, designation of implementers of urban or Gun planning facility projects under Article 86, authorization of implementation plans under Article 88, and public notification of implementation plans under Article 91 of that Act;
10. Cancellation of a dairy farming district designated under Article 4 (1) of the Dairy Farming Promotion Act;
11. Permission to use agricultural production infrastructure under Article 23 and approval of project plans for developing rural tourism and recreation complexes under Article 82 (2) of the Rearrangement of Agricultural and Fishing Villages Act;
12. Alteration or cancellation of agricultural promotion areas or use districts under Article 31, permission or consultation concerning conversion of farmland under Article 34, reports on farmland conversion under Article 35, permission or consultation concerning temporary use of farmland for other purposes under Article 36, and approval of changes of use under Article 40 of the Farmland Act;
13. Permission or reports concerning installation of emission facilities under Article 23 of the Clean Air Conservation Act, Article 33 of the Water Environment Conservation Act and Article 8 of the Noise and Vibration Control Act;
14. Permission for road construction works by persons other than road management authorities under Article 36, permission to occupy roads under Article 61, and consultation or approval with road management authorities under Article 107 of the Road Act (limited to matters concerning designation and public notification of road routes under Article 19, determination of road zones under Article 25, permission for road works under Article 36 and permission to occupy roads under Article 61 of that Act);
15. Designation of urban development zones under Article 3, establishment and amendment of development plans under Article 4, designation of urban development project implementers under Article 11, and authorization of implementation plans under Article 17 of the Urban Development Act;
16. Permission to occupy urban parks under Article 24 of the Act on Urban Parks and Green Areas;
17. Review of traffic impact assessment statements under Article 16 of the Urban Traffic Improvement Promotion Act (excluding deliberation on traffic impact assessment statements under Article 17 of that Act);
18. Designation of general logistics complexes under Article 22 and approval of implementation plans for logistics complex development under Article 28 of the Act on the Development and Management of Logistics Facilities;
19. Permission to establish private roads under Article 4 of the Private Road Act;
20. Permission to cut trees, etc. in erosion control areas under Article 14 and cancellation of designation of erosion control areas under Article 20 of the Erosion Control Work Act;
21. Designation of industrial complex development project implementers under Article 16 and approval of implementation plans for national industrial complex development, general industrial complex development and urban high-tech industrial complex development under Articles 17, 18 and 18-2 of the Industrial Sites and Development Act;
22. Approval of and reports on establishment of factories, etc. under Article 13 (1) of the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act;
23. Permission to convert mountainous districts under Article 14, reports on conversion of mountainous districts under Article 15, permission and reports for temporary use of mountainous districts under Article 15-2, and permission to extract soil and stones under Article 25 of the Mountainous Districts Management Act;
24. Consent to building permits, etc. under Article 6 (1) of the Act on Installation and Management of Firefighting Systems;
25. Consultation with management authorities under Article 5, amendments to comprehensive plans and implementation plans for improvement of small rivers under Articles 6 and 8, permission for improvement of small rivers, etc. under Article 10, and permission to occupy small rivers, etc. under Article 14 of the Small River Maintenance Act;
26. Authorization, etc. of water supply businesses under Articles 17 and 49 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act (limited to cases where the project implementer is a general waterworks business operator or industrial waterworks business operator under that Act), authorization to install private water supply systems under Article 52, and authorization to install private industrial waterworks under Article 54 of that Act;
27. Consultation on plans for energy use under Article 10 of the Energy Use Rationalization Act;
28. Registration of establishment of large-scale stores under Article 8 of the Distribution Industry Development Act;
29. Alteration and cancellation of designation of forestry promotion zones under Article 20 of the Forestry and Mountain Villages Development Promotion Act;
30. Consultation with park management authorities under Article 71 (1) of the Natural Parks Act (limited to permission for acts within park areas under Article 23 of that Act);
31. Permission for relocation of graves under Article 27 of the Act on Funeral Services, etc.;
32. Authorization of or reports on construction plans for electric facilities for private use under Article 8 of the Electrical Safety Management Act;
33. Approval of housing project plans under Article 15 of the Housing Act;
34. Consultation on the feasibility of supplying integrated energy under Article 4 of the Integrated Energy Supply Act;
35. Approval of business plans under Article 12 of the Installation and Utilization of Sports Facilities Act;
36. Permission for changes to the form and quality of land, etc. under Article 21-2 and permission or consultation concerning conversion of grassland under Article 23 of the Grassland Act;
37. Approval of implementation plans for housing site development projects under Article 9 of the Housing Site Development Promotion Act;
38. Approval of or reports on installation of waste treatment facilities under Article 29 of the Wastes Control Act;
39. Authorization to install public sewerage systems (limited to excreta treatment facilities) under Article 11, permission to implement public sewerage construction under Article 16, permission to occupy public sewerage systems under Article 24, reports on installation of drainage facilities under Article 27, and reports on installation of individual sewage treatment facilities under Article 34 (2) of the Sewerage Act;
40. Consultation with or approval of river management authorities under Article 6, permission to implement river works and authorization of river work implementation plans under Article 30, permission to occupy rivers under Article 33, and permission to use river water under Article 50 of the River Act;
41. Permission to implement port development projects under Article 9 (2) and approval of implementation plans for port development projects under Article 10 (2) of the Harbor Act.
② A project implementer who wishes to benefit from the deemed authorization and permission, etc. under paragraph ① shall submit the documents required by the relevant Acts together with the application for implementation approval or approval of changes to a development project.
③ Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City intends to approve or approve changes to a development project, or to hear opinions concerning such a project, and the project includes any matter falling under a subparagraph of paragraph ①, the Mayor shall consult in advance with the heads of relevant administrative agencies (including completing deliberation or opinion-hearing procedures under relevant statutes). Upon granting implementation approval or approval of changes, the Mayor shall promptly notify the heads of relevant administrative agencies of the details.
④ When intending to approve or approve changes to implementation of a development project, the Mayor may convene a consultation council on deemed authorization and permission, etc. in which the heads of relevant administrative agencies participate to process the authorization and permission, etc.
⑤ Matters concerning the composition, functions and operation of the consultation council under paragraph ④ and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑥ Where authorization and permission, etc. under another Act are deemed obtained pursuant to paragraph ①, license taxes, fees, etc. imposed under relevant Acts shall be exempted.
⑦ Except as otherwise provided in paragraphs ① through ⑥, the standards, effects, etc. of deemed authorization and permission shall be governed by Articles 24 through 26 of the Framework Act on Administration: Provided, That notwithstanding the former part of Article 24 (4) of the Framework Act on Administration, an agency requested to consult concerning a matter under paragraph ① 28 shall present its opinion within 30 days.

Article 158 (One-stop processing organizations for development projects)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may establish a one-stop processing organization under the Mayor's jurisdiction to promptly and comprehensively handle affairs concerning approval for implementation of development projects under Article 156 and civil petitions directly handled under Article 17 (2) of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act.
② Where necessary to establish the organization under paragraph ①, the Mayor may request relevant administrative agencies and other relevant institutions and organizations to dispatch public officials, executives or employees.
③ Heads of relevant administrative agencies, institutions or organizations dispatching public officials, executives or employees upon a request under paragraph ② shall not accord them unfavorable treatment in promotion, transfer, welfare benefits, etc.
④ Where necessary in handling the affairs under paragraph ①, the Mayor may request cooperation, including submission of data, from relevant administrative agencies, institutions or organizations.
⑤ Matters necessary for the composition and operation of the one-stop processing organization, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ④, shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 159 (Establishment and operation of special land accounts)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may establish and operate a special land account to stabilize land prices, promote efficient development and supply of land for development and desirable development, and facilitate public projects through early acquisition of public land.
② Revenue of the special land account shall consist of the following:
1. Contributions from other local governments;
2. Transfers from the general account and other special accounts of the Integrated Special City;
3. Income from real estate received in payment in kind under Article 117 of the Local Tax Act (including real estate acquired with special land account funds);
4. Income from disposal or lease of public property;
5. Proceeds from issuing land bonds.
③ Expenditures of the special land account shall consist of the following:
1. Funds for acquiring land;
2. All expenses necessary for management and operation of the special land account;
3. Repayment of proceeds from issuing land bonds;
4. Funds necessary for projects prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance to achieve the purposes for which the special land account was established.
④ Land received in payment in kind under paragraph ② 3 and land acquired under paragraph ③ 1 may be leased, exchanged, transferred, sold or otherwise disposed of as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance, notwithstanding Articles 19 through 21, 28, 29, 36, 39 and 40 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act.
⑤ To stably acquire and dispose of land for development, the Mayor may acquire or dispose of land without obtaining a resolution of the Integrated Special City Council notwithstanding Article 47 (1) 6 of the Local Autonomy Act and Article 10-2 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act. In such cases, the Mayor shall report to the Integrated Special City Council on the results of acquiring or disposing of the land.
⑥ Matters necessary for the establishment and operation of special land accounts, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ⑤, shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 160 (Entrustment of acquisition of land, etc.)
① A project implementer may entrust the affairs of acquiring land, etc. for development projects (meaning land, etc. under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Act on Acquisition of and Compensation for Land, etc. for Public Works Projects; hereinafter the same shall apply), compensation for losses, sales management, etc. to the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, local public enterprises under the Local Public Enterprises Act, or other persons prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance, as prescribed by that ordinance.
② Where affairs of acquiring land, etc., compensation for losses, sales management, etc. are entrusted under paragraph ①, entrustment fees, etc. shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 161 (Tax reductions or exemptions)
Where necessary to facilitate development projects, local taxes may be reduced or exempted as prescribed by the Restriction of Special Local Taxation Act.

Article 162 (Reduction or exemption of charges)
Where necessary to facilitate development projects following establishment of the Integrated Special City, development charges, farmland preservation charges, expenses for creation of alternative grassland, expenses for creation of alternative forest resources, traffic inducement charges, ecosystem conservation charges, environmental improvement charges, infrastructure installation expenses and metropolitan transportation facility charges may be reduced or not imposed as prescribed by the Restitution of Development Gains Act, Farmland Act, Grassland Act, Mountainous Districts Management Act, Urban Traffic Improvement Promotion Act, Natural Environment Conservation Act, Environmental Improvement Cost Allocation Act, National Land Planning and Utilization Act, and Special Act on the Management of Metropolitan Transportation in Metropolitan Areas.

Article 163 (Support for areas near development project districts)
The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may support projects to resolve inconvenience to residents or improve their living environment resulting from development projects approved or on which opinions were heard under Article 156, and may provide loans or subsidies for income-generating projects, etc. to increase residents' income.

Article 164 (Designation of investment promotion districts)
① To attract investment of at least the level prescribed by Presidential Decree into the Integrated Special City, the Mayor may designate all or part of its jurisdiction as a Jeonnam-Gwangju Investment Promotion District (hereinafter referred to as an "investment promotion district") following deliberation by the Basic Plan Deliberation Council and consultation on strategic environmental impact assessment under Article 16 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
② When intending to designate an investment promotion district under paragraph ①, the Mayor may give priority to the following areas:
1. Areas desired by investors;
2. Areas meeting conditions prescribed by Presidential Decree that are favorable for attracting investment.
③ Upon designating an investment promotion district under paragraphs ① and ②, the Mayor shall publicly notify the following:
1. The name, location and area of the investment promotion district;
2. Methods of developing or managing the investment promotion district;
3. Principal business particulars, including investment amounts, investment implementation periods and employment plans;
4. Other matters prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
④ Investment promotion districts shall be managed by the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
⑤ Where necessary to ascertain whether investment is implemented in accordance with publicly notified particulars under paragraph ③, the Mayor may require investors to submit relevant materials.
⑥ The Mayor may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, government-funded institutions or government-invested institutions to provide data, statistics, etc. necessary for analyzing efficient management of investment promotion districts and their impacts on regional economies.
⑦ Procedures and methods for designation and matters necessary for management of investment promotion districts shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 165 (Cancellation of designation of investment promotion districts)
① Where investment under Article 164 ceases to meet the standards prescribed by Presidential Decree, the Mayor shall cancel designation of the investment promotion district following deliberation by the Basic Plan Deliberation Council.
② Methods and procedures for canceling designation of investment promotion districts under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 166 (Financial support, etc. for investment promotion districts)
① The State or the Integrated Special City may provide loans for acquiring sites to be leased to enterprises located in investment promotion districts, reduce or exempt rents for land, etc., and provide other funds necessary for development projects. Standards and procedures for financial support shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Where necessary to promote investment, the Integrated Special City may pay employment subsidies, education and training subsidies, etc. to enterprises investing within its jurisdiction as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ Notwithstanding the State Property Act, the Public Property and Commodity Management Act and other statutes, the State and the Integrated Special City may permit cooperating enterprises prescribed by Presidential Decree to use or profit from, lend, or sell State or public property owned by the State or the Integrated Special City by negotiated contract.
④ The State and the Integrated Special City may give priority to administrative and financial support for investment promotion districts designated under Article 164 (1) that are closely connected to metropolitan logistics infrastructure, such as ports and railways, or that require establishment of infrastructure to operate large-scale manufacturing facilities.

Article 167 (Special provisions concerning lease and sale of State and public property)
① Notwithstanding the relevant provisions of the State Property Act and the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, the Minister of Finance and Economy, the managing agency of State property, or the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may permit an enterprise located in an investment promotion district to use or profit from, lend (hereinafter referred to as "lease" in this Article), or sell land, factories or other State or public property owned by the State or the Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as "property, etc." in this Article) by negotiated contract.
② Notwithstanding Article 35 (1) and Article 46 (1) of the State Property Act and Article 21 (1) and Article 31 (1) of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, the lease period for property, etc. under paragraph ① may be up to 30 years. The lease period may be renewed, but each renewal shall not exceed 30 years.
③ Notwithstanding Article 18 of the State Property Act and Article 13 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, where property, etc. owned by the State or the Integrated Special City is leased under paragraph ①, the lessee may construct factories or other permanent facilities on the land. The land may be leased on the condition that the facilities are donated to the State or the Integrated Special City, or restored to their original condition and returned, upon expiration of the lease, taking account of the types of facilities, etc.
④ Notwithstanding Article 32 (1) and Article 33 of the State Property Act (including cases where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 47 of that Act) and Articles 22 (1), 23, 32 and 33 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, rent for property, etc. leased under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree for State property and by Integrated Special City ordinance for public property and may, where necessary, be denominated in foreign currency.
⑤ Where property, etc. under paragraph ① is sold to an enterprise located in an investment promotion district and the purchaser is deemed unable to pay the purchase price in a lump sum, the due date may be extended or payment in installments permitted as prescribed by Presidential Decree for State property and Integrated Special City ordinance for public property, notwithstanding Article 50 (1) and (2) of the State Property Act and Article 37 (1) of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act.
⑥ Notwithstanding the following Acts, rent for property, etc. leased to enterprises located in investment promotion districts under paragraph ① may be reduced or exempted as prescribed by Presidential Decree for State property and Integrated Special City ordinance for public property:
1. Article 34 of the State Property Act (including cases where applied mutatis mutandis under Article 47 of that Act);
2. Articles 24 and 34 of the Public Property and Commodity Management Act.
⑦ An enterprise to which public property is to be sold under paragraph ① shall meet the requirements prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑧ Article 27 of the Industrial Sites and Development Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to restrictions on the sale or disposal of State or public land within development project districts for which implementation approval has been obtained.
⑨ A project implementer to which public land is to be sold following development project implementation approval shall meet the requirements prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑩ Notwithstanding the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, the Mayor may lease public property by negotiated contract to a person who has obtained approval for implementation of a development project. Paragraphs ② through ④ and ⑥ shall apply to such leases.

Article 168 (Promoting relocation of enterprises to investment promotion districts)
① The State may formulate and implement policies to encourage relevant enterprises to relocate to investment promotion districts to develop industries within the Integrated Special City.
② The Mayor may formulate and implement policies to encourage enterprises to relocate to investment promotion districts following consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies to promote industrial development within the Integrated Special City.
③ Matters necessary for formulating and implementing relocation policies under paragraphs ① and ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 169 (Special provisions on designation of research and development special zones)
① To promote research and development by universities, research institutes and enterprises and support commercialization of research results and business startups, the Mayor may request the Minister of Science and ICT to designate a research and development special zone under Article 4 of the Special Act on the Promotion of Research and Development Special Zones. The Minister shall give priority to efforts to ensure that the requested area can be designated as a research and development special zone.
② When designating a research and development special zone in the Integrated Special City under paragraph ①, the designation requirements may be differently prescribed by Presidential Decree notwithstanding Article 4 (2) and (6) of the Special Act on the Promotion of Research and Development Special Zones.

Article 170 (Special provisions concerning changes to research and development special zones)
① Notwithstanding Article 4-2 (1) and (2) of the Special Act on the Promotion of Research and Development Special Zones, at the request of the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, the Minister of Science and ICT may alter the area of a research and development special zone within the following limits. The Mayor shall consult with the heads of relevant administrative agencies before making the request:
1. Where the area of an individually designated district within a research and development special zone is at least one million square meters: An alteration of less than 100,000 square meters;
2. Where the area of an individually designated district is less than one million square meters: An alteration of less than ten percent of the district's area.
② Article 4 (4), (7) and (8) of the Special Act on the Promotion of Research and Development Special Zones shall apply mutatis mutandis to changes under paragraph ①. In such cases, "designation" shall be construed as "alteration".

Article 171 (Special provisions concerning establishment of regional organizations of government-funded research institutions in science and technology)
① To enhance the science and technology capacity of the Integrated Special City, the Mayor may request a research council under the Act on the Establishment, Operation and Fostering of Government-Funded Science and Technology Research Institutes, etc. to establish a regional organization under Article 5 (3) of the same Act.
② Upon receiving a request under paragraph ①, the Minister of Science and ICT shall give priority to efforts to ensure that the regional organization is established.
③ The Mayor shall provide administrative and financial support to enable the regional organization to operate effectively.

Article 172 (Special provisions concerning environmental impact assessment)
① A project implementer under Article 22 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act shall request consultation with the Mayor of the Integrated Special City notwithstanding Article 27 of the same Act: Provided, That this shall not apply where the project implementer is the head of a central administrative agency, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, a public institution under Article 4 (1) of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, or a local public enterprise established by the Integrated Special City under the Local Public Enterprises Act, or where the project area includes land outside the Integrated Special City's jurisdiction.
② The authority of the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment under Articles 24, 28 through 40, 40-2, 41, 51, 52, 66, 66-2 and 76 (6) of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act (limited, in the case of Article 76 (6), to imposition and collection of administrative fines relating to transferred powers) shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
③ When reviewing an environmental impact assessment statement or related materials following a request for consultation under paragraph ①, the Mayor may hear opinions from an institution with expertise in environmental impact assessment (meaning an institution prescribed by Presidential Decree under the main sentence of the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 28 (2) of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, or an institution separately designated and publicly notified by the Mayor following consultation with the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment) or from relevant experts, or may commission field investigations.
④ Fields and detailed items of environmental impact assessments conducted under paragraph ①, designation and public notification of specialized environmental impact assessment institutions under paragraph ③, preparation of assessment statements, collection of opinions and other assessment procedures shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑤ Institutions for re-assessment under Article 41 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act shall be deemed to include institutions separately designated and publicly notified by the Mayor following consultation with the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment under paragraph ③.

Article 173 (Special provisions concerning small-scale environmental impact assessment)
① A project implementer under Article 43 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act shall request consultation with the Mayor of the Integrated Special City notwithstanding Article 44 of the same Act: Provided, That this shall not apply where the project implementer is the head of a central administrative agency, the Mayor, a public institution under Article 4 (1) of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, or a local public enterprise established by the Integrated Special City under the Local Public Enterprises Act, or where the project area includes land outside the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City.
② When reviewing a small-scale environmental impact assessment statement or related materials following a request under paragraph ①, the Mayor may hear opinions from an institution with expertise in small-scale environmental impact assessment (meaning an institution prescribed by Presidential Decree under the main sentence of Article 17 (2) of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act as applied mutatis mutandis under Article 45 (2) of that Act, or an institution separately designated and publicly notified by the Mayor following consultation with the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment) or from relevant experts, or may commission field investigations.
③ The authority of the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment under Articles 44 through 46, 46-2 and 47 through 49 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act concerning matters for which consultation with the Mayor is required under paragraph ① shall be vested in the Mayor.
④ Fields and detailed items of small-scale environmental impact assessments conducted under paragraph ①, designation and public notification of specialized environmental impact assessment institutions under paragraph ②, preparation of assessment statements, collection of opinions and other assessment procedures shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 174 (Duration of special provisions)
① The special provisions under Articles 172 and 173 shall remain effective until the third anniversary of the date this Act enters into force.
② By three months before expiration of the period under paragraph ①, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall evaluate the operational performance of the special provisions under Articles 172 and 173 and notify the Mayor of the Integrated Special City of opinions concerning extension or abolition of their duration, etc. The Mayor shall take necessary measures in accordance with the opinions received.
③ The Minister may request the Mayor to submit data necessary for an evaluation under paragraph ②. The Mayor shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so.
④ Matters necessary for evaluation methods and procedures under paragraph ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 175 (Special provisions concerning consultation on natural landscape impacts)
① When granting authorization or permission, etc. for development projects and other projects falling under Articles 172 and 176, authority of the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
② Notwithstanding Article 28 (1) of the Natural Environment Conservation Act, the Mayor shall determine whether to grant authorization or permission, etc. after deliberation by the Natural Landscape Deliberation Committee under paragraph ④ concerning impacts on natural landscapes, conservation measures, etc.
③ The powers of the heads of local environmental agencies under Articles 28 and 29 of the Natural Environment Conservation Act shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
④ The Mayor shall establish the Integrated Special City Natural Landscape Deliberation Committee for specialized and efficient review and deliberation in relation to natural landscape impact consultation, etc. Its detailed composition and operation shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑤ The Natural Environment Conservation Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the methods and procedures for consultation and the Natural Landscape Deliberation Committee under paragraphs ① through ④. In such cases, "head of a local environmental agency" shall be construed as "Mayor of the Integrated Special City".

Article 176 (Special provisions concerning climate change impact assessments)
① A project implementer required to request consultation with the Mayor of the Integrated Special City under Article 172 (1) shall also request consultation with the Mayor concerning review of a climate change impact assessment, notwithstanding Article 23 (2) of the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth for Coping with Climate Crisis.
② When reviewing the results of a climate change impact assessment following a request for consultation under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall hear the opinion of the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and reflect that opinion to the greatest extent possible.
③ The authority of the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment under Article 23 of the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth for Coping with Climate Crisis concerning consultation under paragraph ① shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.

Article 177 (Creation of carbon-neutral cities)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall create a carbon-neutral city based on improving energy efficiency of urban spaces and transforming citizens' awareness to improve the quality of life of citizens and promote sustainable regional development.
② To create a carbon-neutral city in the Integrated Special City, the State may implement green growth projects, including various carbon-neutrality pilot projects linked to national projects, green technology industries, and projects for responding and adapting to the climate crisis.
③ The State may implement projects to promote environmental, social and governance (ESG) management among enterprises and public institutions within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City.
④ The Mayor shall establish a comprehensive carbon-neutral city plan for the Integrated Special City every five years, including:
1. Projects to reduce greenhouse gas emissions and increase energy self-sufficiency of the carbon-neutral city;
2. Projects to create, expand and improve carbon sinks, etc. under Article 33 (1) of the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth for Coping with Climate Crisis;
3. Conservation of ecological corridors and restoration of ecosystems within the carbon-neutral city;
4. Creation of a resource-circulating city to respond to the climate crisis;
5. Other projects necessary to respond to the climate crisis, transition to a carbon-neutral society and improve environmental quality in the carbon-neutral city.
⑤ The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary to implement carbon-neutral city creation projects.

Article 178 (Preliminary surveys for comprehensive carbon-neutral city plans)
① The Mayor shall analyze the present circumstances of relevant Sis, Guns, Gus and areas within a carbon-neutral city to systematically and systematically develop and manage carbon-neutral city project zones.
② Preliminary surveys shall consider:
1. Analysis of factors relating to carbon neutrality, including greenhouse gas emissions and greenhouse gas absorption according to land use;
2. Analysis of population, including registered population, population density and the number of persons engaged in primary, secondary and tertiary industries;
3. Analysis of basic urban characteristics, including areas of urban land by use and infrastructure conditions;
4. Analysis of vulnerability to climate disasters, including exposure to heat waves, floods, sea-level rise and drought, sensitivity to climate disasters and capacity to adapt to the climate crisis.

Article 179 (Special provisions concerning designation and evaluation of climate crisis adaptation centers)
① Notwithstanding Article 46 of the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth for Coping with Climate Crisis, the Mayor may designate an Integrated Special City Climate Crisis Adaptation Center (hereinafter referred to as an "Adaptation Center") to support the formulation and implementation of local climate crisis adaptation measures.
② Adaptation Centers shall carry out projects concerning climate crisis adaptation, including surveys and research for implementing climate crisis adaptation measures.
③ The Mayor may evaluate the performance and other results of Adaptation Centers.
④ The State and the Integrated Special City may support all or part of the expenses necessary for Adaptation Centers to perform their projects within budgetary limits.

Article 180 (Special financial support for carbon neutrality support centers)
Where necessary, the State may provide administrative and financial support within budgetary limits to carbon neutrality support centers designated and operated under Article 68 of the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth for Coping with Climate Crisis in the former jurisdictions of Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City.

Article 181 (Designation of special districts for just transition)
① The Integrated Special City may request the Government to designate any of the following areas as a special district for just transition under Article 48 of the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth for Coping with Climate Crisis (hereinafter referred to as a "special district"). The Government may designate an area as a special district following deliberation by the committee under Article 15 (1) of the same Act:
1. An area where the employment environment has changed substantially or is expected to change due to rapid job losses, regional economic recession or changes in industrial structures during the transition to a carbon-neutral society;
2. An area where rapid changes in the social or economic environment are expected or have occurred during the transition to a carbon-neutral society and which satisfies the requirements under Article 48 (1) 2 of the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth for Coping with Climate Crisis;
3. Other areas deemed by the committee under Article 15 (1) of that Act to require designation as special districts to address social and economic inequality that may arise during the transition to a carbon-neutral society.
② Where the grounds for designation under paragraph ① cease to exist, the Integrated Special City may request alteration or cancellation of designation of a special district following deliberation by the committee under Article 15 (1) of the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth for Coping with Climate Crisis. In such cases, Article 48 (3) of the same Act shall apply mutatis mutandis.
③ The State may provide necessary administrative and financial support to special districts.

Article 182 (Special provisions concerning charges for occupation and use of public waters)
Notwithstanding Article 13 (3) of the Public Waters Management and Reclamation Act, where the Integrated Special City is closest to the permitted area, an amount equivalent to 80 percent of the occupation and use fees shall accrue as revenue to the Integrated Special City: Provided, That any amount exceeding the revenue otherwise accruing to a Metropolitan City, Do or Special Self-Governing Province under Article 13 (3) of the same Act shall be used for fishery resource creation projects under the subparagraphs of Article 41 (1) of the Fishery Resources Management Act.

Article 183 (Promotion of and support for the hydrogen industry)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall promote policies necessary to establish a foundation for development, stimulate research and development, and promote commercialization in relation to:
1. Fostering and supporting region-specific hydrogen industries;
2. Distributing and promoting services related to local hydrogen industries;
3. Other matters recognized by the Mayor as hydrogen industries.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for fostering the hydrogen industry in the Integrated Special City.

Article 184 (Responsibilities of the State for restoring competitiveness of national key industries)
① The State may formulate and implement policies necessary to strengthen competitiveness and transform industrial structures of the following national key industries within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City:
1. The petrochemical industry;
2. The steel industry;
3. The shipbuilding industry.
② Policies under paragraph ① shall include:
1. Analysis of factors weakening competitiveness of national key industries, including global oversupply, changes in trading conditions and carbon-neutrality policies;
2. Measures to establish stable electricity supply and demand conditions and ease energy costs for energy-intensive industries, including petrochemicals and steel;
3. Measures to improve and restructure aging industrial complexes and infrastructure;
4. Measures to stabilize the management and strengthen competitiveness of small and medium-sized enterprises and suppliers;
5. Other matters necessary to restore competitiveness of national key industries.
③ The State shall endeavor to formulate and implement policies under paragraph ① in connection with national industrial policies, carbon-neutrality and energy transition policies, and balanced regional development policies.
④ The State may provide administrative and financial support for the smooth implementation of policies to restore competitiveness under paragraph ①, giving priority to linkages with existing support systems and financial projects under relevant statutes.

Article 185 (Administrative and financial support for fostering high-tech industries)
The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for the Integrated Special City to foster the following high-tech industries:
1. Defense industries related to space, artificial intelligence (AI), drones under Article 2 (1) 1 of the Act on the Promotion of Utilization of Drones and Creation of Infrastructure Therefor, semiconductors, robots, etc.;
2. Space defense components and equipment industries;
3. Advanced space industries, including space launch vehicles;
4. Advanced biohealth industries, including innovative biopharmaceuticals and digital healthcare services;
5. Nano-semiconductor industries;
6. Robotics industries;
7. Future mobility parts industries, including mobility wireless communications, autonomous driving and specialized vehicle road management services;
8. Hydrogen fuel cell and secondary battery industries;
9. Ceramic and advanced or rare-material industries;
10. Artificial intelligence and virtual convergence industries;
11. Cosmetics industries;
12. Energy industries, including nuclear energy and solar power;
13. Three-dimensional printing industries;
14. Optical convergence industries;
15. Marine convergence industries;
16. Large-scale research equipment industries involving equipment valued at 50 billion won or more;
17. Other strategic and emerging industries that the Mayor wishes to foster.

Article 186 (Special provisions concerning designation of specialized complexes for national high-tech strategic industries)
① Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City applies for designation of a specialized complex for national high-tech strategic industries under the latter part of the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 16 (1) of the Special Act on Strengthening and Protecting Competitiveness of National High-Tech Strategic Industries, the Minister of Trade and Industry may give priority to designating the relevant area as such a specialized complex.
② For efficient establishment and operation of an area designated as a specialized complex for strategic industries under Article 16 of that Act, the State may delegate to the Mayor authority concerning execution of related budgets, authorization and permission, etc. as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 187 (Special provisions concerning fostering the quantum industry)
① When establishing a comprehensive quantum plan under Article 5 of the Act on the Promotion of Quantum Science and Technology and Quantum Industry, the State may include matters supporting the fostering of the quantum industry in the Integrated Special City.
② To support the Integrated Special City in securing source technologies in quantum science and technology and linking them to the quantum industry, the State may designate research institutes, etc. established within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City under Article 18 (1) of that Act as quantum science and technology research centers and quantum fabrication facilities.

Article 188 (Special provisions concerning designation of drone special liberalization zones)
Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City requests designation of a drone special liberalization zone under Article 10 of the Act on the Promotion of Utilization of Drones and Creation of Infrastructure Therefor, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may give priority to reviewing the request.

Article 189 (Special provisions concerning consultation and coordination of projects supporting small and medium-sized enterprises)
When establishing or changing projects supporting small and medium-sized enterprises, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may analyze and review their appropriateness and proceed with the projects notwithstanding the results of consultation and coordination with the Minister of SMEs and Startups under Article 20-5 of the Framework Act on Small and Medium Enterprises.

Article 190 (Special provisions concerning establishment of industrial solidarity cooperative bodies to promote cooperation among enterprises)
① To establish an ecosystem of solidarity and cooperation in regional strategic industries, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may designate an industrial solidarity cooperative body involving enterprises, universities, research institutes, etc. and provide integrated support for the following projects:
1. Joint research and development (R&D) and mutual sharing and utilization of core technologies and intellectual property rights;
2. Joint investment in and use of production facilities and equipment, and establishment of systems for mutual supply of components and raw materials;
3. Joint brand development, development of online and offline markets, joint marketing, and acquisition of certifications.
② With respect to acts under the subparagraphs of paragraph ① for which the Mayor has consulted the Fair Trade Commission when designating and providing integrated support to an industrial solidarity cooperative body under paragraph ①, authorization by the Fair Trade Commission under Article 40 (2) of the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act shall be deemed granted.
③ When intending to conduct consultation under paragraph ②, the Mayor shall submit to the Fair Trade Commission the documents prescribed by Article 40 (3) of the Monopoly Regulation and Fair Trade Act.
④ The Mayor shall process applications, designations, provision of incentives and follow-up management concerning industrial solidarity cooperative bodies through a single integrated service window. Where requests for related authorization or permission and regulatory improvement are received, the Government shall give them the highest priority for review notwithstanding other statutes and notify the Mayor of the results.

Article 191 (Linked and integrated management of specialized regional development zones, clusters and districts)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may link and comprehensively manage special zones, clusters and districts designated and operated under the Act on Special Cases concerning Regulation of Regulation-Free Special Zones and Special Economic Zones for Specialized Regional Development, the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act, etc.
② For linked and integrated management of special zones, clusters and districts under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall establish an integrated management plan and consult with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies.

Article 192 (Special provisions concerning requests for designation of national industrial complexes)
① Notwithstanding Article 6 (2) of the Industrial Sites and Development Act, where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City deems designation of a national industrial complex necessary, the Mayor may identify a target area and request the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to designate it as a national industrial complex. The Mayor shall consult with the heads of relevant administrative agencies in advance.
② The methods and procedures for designation of a national industrial complex pursuant to a request under paragraph ① shall be governed by the Industrial Sites and Development Act and the Special Act on Simplification of Approval and Permission Procedures for Industrial Complexes.

Article 193 (Special provisions concerning industrial locations and development)
① The authority of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport under Articles 4 (1) and (3), 7 (7), and 7-4 (1) of the Industrial Sites and Development Act shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City: Provided, That authority concerning national industrial complexes is excluded.
② With respect to national industrial complex development projects conducted by project implementers designated by the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and project implementers falling under Article 16 (1) 1 and 2 of the Industrial Sites and Development Act when development plans are established under Article 6 of that Act, the authority of the Minister under Articles 17 (1) and (2), 19-2 (1), the former and latter parts of Article 21 (2), the former and latter parts of Article 26 (3), the former part of Article 27 (2), Article 37 (1), the former and latter parts of Article 37 (2), Article 37 (5), Article 47 (1), and Article 48 of that Act shall be vested in the Mayor: Provided, That authority concerning national industrial complexes is excluded.
③ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Land, Infrastructure and Transport under Article 4 (4), the proviso to Article 7 (1), the proviso to Article 7-2 (1), Article 7-4 (1), the proviso to Article 7-4 (2), the former part and proviso to Article 8 (2), the former part of Article 18-2 (1), Article 19 (1), Article 19-2 (1), Article 37 (4) and (5), Article 46-2 (3), Article 46-4 (2), and Article 46-6 (4) of the Industrial Sites and Development Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance insofar as the Mayor has consulted in advance with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport: Provided, That authority concerning national industrial complexes is excluded.

Article 194 (Special provisions concerning support for industrial complex infrastructure)
Notwithstanding Article 29 of the Industrial Sites and Development Act, infrastructure prescribed by Presidential Decree, including access roads constructed to connect newly established industrial complexes in the Integrated Special City with hub airports and ports, and roads and railways constructed to connect them to national backbone railway networks, may be supported by national funds within budgetary limits.

Article 195 (Special provisions concerning development of industrial complexes exclusively for lease)
Notwithstanding Article 46-6 of the Industrial Sites and Development Act, the State may provide national funding for the expenses necessary to acquire land designated as an industrial complex exclusively for lease within the Integrated Special City.

Article 196 (Special provisions concerning establishment of basic environmental facilities within industrial complexes)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City or the head of the Si, Gun or Gu in which an industrial complex is situated may install and operate waste treatment facilities under Article 2, subparagraph 8 of the Wastes Control Act on land within an industrial complex (including national industrial complexes) to establish basic environmental facilities. In such cases, those facilities shall be deemed infrastructure of the industrial complex notwithstanding provisions concerning industrial complex management master plans, restrictions on industries permitted to locate in the complex and other relevant provisions under the Industrial Sites and Development Act and the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act.
② Where necessary to install and operate waste treatment facilities under paragraph ①, the Mayor or the head of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu may consult with authorities responsible for designating and managing the industrial complex and take necessary measures, such as changes to its management master plan or development plan. The relevant agencies shall cooperate unless there is a special reason not to do so.

Article 197 (Special provisions concerning delegation of authority over regulatory exceptions for high-tech strategic industries)
① To foster high-tech strategic industries, the Minister of Trade and Industry may delegate to the Mayor of the Integrated Special City (limited to the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City) the Minister's authority concerning expedited regulatory verification under Article 10-2, applications for regulatory exceptions for demonstration under Article 10-3 (1), (3) and (4), and applications for temporary permits under Article 10-6 (1), (3) and (4) of the Industrial Convergence Promotion Act. Where the Mayor requests the State to deliberate on expedited regulatory verification, etc., the State may give priority to deliberating on whether to approve special provisions.
② The State and the Integrated Special City may provide necessary administrative and financial support to persons granted regulatory exceptions or temporary permits under paragraph ①.

Article 198 (Special provisions concerning amendment of national industrial complex development and implementation plans)
① Notwithstanding Articles 6 (3) and 17-2 (1) and (2) of the Industrial Sites and Development Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may request the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to amend development plans and development implementation plans for national industrial complexes within the former jurisdictions of Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City.
② Methods and procedures for amending national industrial complex development plans and development implementation plans under paragraph ① shall be governed, mutatis mutandis, by the Industrial Sites and Development Act.

Article 199 (Designation of competitiveness enhancement project districts for aging industrial hub complexes)
① Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City requests designation of a competitiveness enhancement project district under Article 2, subparagraph 5 of the Special Act on Revitalization and Strengthening Competitiveness of Aging Industrial Complexes, an authority responsible for formulating strategic plans under subparagraph 6 of the same Article may give priority to designating the relevant area as a competitiveness enhancement project district under Article 11 of that Act.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for infrastructure improvement projects under paragraph ①.

Article 200 (Special support for energy self-sufficiency and carbon neutrality of aging industrial hub complexes)
① Where enterprises located in aging industrial hub complexes within the Integrated Special City intend to install or construct renewable energy generation facilities, etc. using factories, idle land, etc., the State and the Integrated Special City may provide necessary administrative and financial support.
② Where a resident enterprise intends to install or construct generation facilities, etc. under paragraph ①, the Mayor may, notwithstanding Article 33 of the Industrial Cluster Development and Factory Establishment Act, consult with the industrial complex designation and management authorities under paragraph (2) of that Article and give priority to processing related authorization and permission procedures, including amendments to the industrial complex management master plan, or conduct integrated deliberation.
③ Where necessary to facilitate installation and construction of facilities under paragraph ①, the Mayor may reduce or exempt acquisition and property taxes arising from the acquisition of such facilities as prescribed by the Restriction of Special Local Taxation Act.

Article 201 (Special support for relocation of aging industrial complexes)
① Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City cancels designation of an industrial complex under Article 13 (2) 2 (b) of the Industrial Sites and Development Act, the Mayor may formulate and implement a comprehensive plan for relocation of the aging industrial complex, including consideration of maintaining industrial functions within the complex, minimizing job losses and effects on the regional economy. The Mayor may delegate or have the relevant Si, Gun or Gu perform all or part of the related affairs on the Mayor's behalf.
② Where the Mayor establishes a comprehensive plan under paragraph ① following consultation with the State, the Mayor may request State support for the following expenses:
1. Site preparation and infrastructure installation expenses for relocating the industrial complex;
2. Relocation expenses of enterprises arising from the industrial complex relocation, including construction, extension or renovation of factories.

Article 202 (Special provisions concerning the Special Act on the Promotion of Venture Businesses)
① Notwithstanding Articles 17-2 (1), (3) and (4), 17-4 (4), 17-5, 17-6, 18-4 (1) through (3), and 29 (limited to hearings relating to transferred powers) of the Special Act on the Promotion of Venture Businesses, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may designate, revoke designation of or cancel venture business promotion districts and new technology startup clustering zones after prior consultation with the Minister of SMEs and Startups.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under Article 17-2 (2), the latter part of 17-2 (3), the main sentence of 17-2 (4), Article 17-4 (1) and (7), the former part of Article 18 (1), Article 18 (2) 1 through 3, Article 18 (6), Article 21 (2) and the former part of Article 21 (3) of the Special Act on the Promotion of Venture Businesses may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ The heads of institutions located in new technology startup clustering zones designated by the Mayor and the Mayor who designated venture business promotion districts shall cooperate when the Minister of SMEs and Startups requests relevant data or conducts on-site fact-finding surveys to verify performance.

Article 203 (Special provisions concerning venture business investment and policy financing)
① To advance industrial structures and foster emerging industries in the Integrated Special City, the State may comprehensively provide venture investment, policy financing and guarantees to venture businesses and startups situated in the Integrated Special City.
② To achieve the purpose of paragraph ①, the State may provide the following support within budgetary limits:
1. Contributions to individual investment associations, venture investment associations or policy-purpose funds;
2. Preferential financing systems for small and medium-sized enterprises and establishment and operation of guarantee systems;
3. Support for commercialization investment and follow-on investment linked to demonstration projects, regulatory exception projects and national research and development projects.

Article 204 (Designation and operation of startup cluster pilot districts)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may designate and operate startup cluster pilot districts to revitalize the startup ecosystem and promote regional economic development.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support to enterprises within startup cluster pilot districts designated by the Mayor.

Article 205 (Promotion of industry-academia cooperation in future high-tech industries)
① To promote research and development, industrial technology, human resource development and regional economic revitalization, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may designate an area meeting any of the following requirements as a leading district for cooperation between industry and universities (hereinafter referred to as "industry-academia cooperation"):
1. An area where institutions engaging in industry-academia cooperation and their support facilities, etc. are collectively located or expected to be located;
2. An area where enterprises implementing investment or technological development projects relating to industry-academia cooperation are located or wish to invest;
3. Another area recognized as requiring designation as a leading industry-academia cooperation district.
② The State and the Integrated Special City may provide administrative and financial support in the following matters concerning establishment and operation of leading industry-academia cooperation districts designated under paragraph ①:
1. Training of personnel in response to industrial demand and future industrial development;
2. Research, development and commercialization for creating and disseminating new knowledge and technology;
3. Technology transfer to industry and provision of industrial consultancy;
4. Joint utilization of tangible and intangible resources, including personnel, facilities, equipment and research and development information;
5. Other matters necessary to revitalize industry-academia cooperation.

Article 206 (Special provisions concerning establishment of investment finance corporations)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may contribute capital to establish and operate an institution for planning and managing policy funds, managing, disposing of and developing public assets, investing in strategic projects, etc.
② Where deemed necessary to respond to local extinction or promote innovative regional growth, the Mayor may establish and contribute to a collective investment scheme under the Financial Investment Services and Capital Markets Act.

Article 207 (Special financial support for enterprises relocating to the region)
When providing support under Article 24 (1) and (2) of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth to enterprises relocating to the Integrated Special City or newly establishing or expanding workplaces there, the State may provide preferential support by applying Article 51 of the same Act mutatis mutandis. <Amended on 2026.6.2>

Article 208 (Special financial support for reshoring enterprises)
When providing support under Article 12 of the Act on Support for Reshoring Enterprises to enterprises returning to the Republic of Korea and relocating to the Integrated Special City, the State may provide preferential support by applying Article 51 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth mutatis mutandis. <Amended on 2026.6.2>

Article 209 (Special support for investing enterprises)
To promote investment within the Integrated Special City, the State may increase the national subsidy ceilings and cost-sharing ratios for enterprises located in investment promotion districts notwithstanding Article 14-2 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act, Article 12 of the Act on Support for Reshoring Enterprises and Article 24 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth. <Amended on 2026.6.2>

Article 210 (Special provisions concerning cash support for foreign investment)
When providing cash support under Article 14-2 (1) of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act to foreigners making foreign investments in the Integrated Special City, including establishment or expansion of workplaces and research and development, the State and the Integrated Special City may provide preferential support by applying Article 51 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth mutatis mutandis. <Amended on 2026.6.2>

Article 211 (Payments arising from current transactions)
Payments for current transactions in the Integrated Special City not exceeding the amount prescribed by Presidential Decree may be made directly between transaction parties in means of external payment under Article 3 (1) 4 of the Foreign Exchange Transactions Act.

Article 212 (Exclusion of application of other Acts to foreign-invested enterprises)
Article 12 of the Act on Prohibition of Age Discrimination in Employment and Elderly Employment Promotion shall not apply to foreign-invested enterprises within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City (meaning foreigners and foreign-invested enterprises under Article 2 (1) 1 and 6 of the Foreign Investment Promotion Act; hereinafter the same shall apply). Where a foreign-invested enterprise recruits older persons, the Mayor may provide employment subsidies within budgetary limits as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 213 (Special provisions concerning the Immigration Act)
Notwithstanding Articles 8 and 10 of the Immigration Act, the Minister of Justice may separately prescribe visa issuance procedures and maximum periods of stay granted on each occasion for each status of stay for foreigners employed by research institutes, enterprises, etc. located in districts or complexes within the Integrated Special City prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 214 (Supply of housing to foreigners)
Where a project entity under Article 2, subparagraph 10 of the Housing Act constructs and supplies privately built housing within an investment promotion district, it may provide a special allocation, limited to one occasion, to foreigners who meet the conditions prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance and own no housing as of the public announcement of recruitment of occupants, on the basis of one dwelling per household, within a limit of ten percent of the quantity constructed: Provided, That special allocations exceeding ten percent may be made with the Mayor's approval.

Article 215 (Special provisions concerning free economic zone development plans)
Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City requests amendments to a free economic zone development plan under Article 7 of the Special Act on Designation and Management of Free Economic Zones, the Minister of Trade and Industry shall give priority to considering the request.

Article 216 (Provision of foreign-language services)
① To improve convenience for foreign investors, etc., the State and the Integrated Special City shall provide foreign-language services within the Integrated Special City, including receiving and processing official documents prepared in foreign languages.
② The scope and methods of providing foreign-language services under paragraph ① and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 217 (Designation and support of specialized industries in Sis, Guns and Gus)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall designate at least one specialized industry for each Si, Gun and Gu within the jurisdiction, taking into account regional conditions and industrial foundations.
② To foster and support specialized industries under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall formulate and implement support plans for specialized industries for each Si, Gun and Gu and may determine support recipients, support methods, performance evaluation and adjustment measures, where necessary.
③ The State may provide administrative and financial support to foster specialized industries under paragraphs ① and ②, as prescribed by relevant statutes.
④ Details necessary for implementing paragraphs ① through ③ shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 218 (Special provisions concerning support for small and medium-sized enterprises)
The authority of the Minister of SMEs and Startups under the following provisions shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City:
1. Articles 4 (1) and 10, subparagraph 5 of the Act on the Promotion of Activities of Enterprises Owned by Persons with Disabilities;
2. Article 26 of the Act on Facilitation of Purchase of Small and Medium Enterprise-Manufactured Products and Support for Development of Their Markets;
3. Articles 5, 43 (1) and 45 of the Act on the Promotion of Small and Medium Enterprises;
4. Article 19 (2) of the Act on Fostering of Regional Small and Medium Enterprises and Promotion of Innovation;
5. Articles 4, 9 (3) and (4), and 11, subparagraph 4 of the Act on Support for Female-Owned Businesses.

Article 219 (Special provisions concerning priority purchase of technology-developed products)
