The authority to require priority purchasing measures among the powers of the Minister of SMEs and Startups or the heads of relevant central administrative agencies under Article 13 (2) of the Act on Facilitation of Purchase of Small and Medium Enterprise-Manufactured Products and Support for Development of Their Markets shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.

Article 220 (Special provisions concerning joint welfare projects for employees of small and medium-sized enterprises)
① To improve welfare of employees of small and medium-sized enterprises and attract and retain local talent, the Government and the Mayor may operate and support metropolitan-level joint welfare projects involving local enterprises, small merchants, service businesses, etc.
② The Mayor may organize and operate a support council involving the Korea Federation of SMEs, chambers of commerce and industry, labor unions, small and medium-sized enterprises, etc. for joint welfare projects under paragraph ①.
③ The State and the Integrated Special City may provide financial support necessary for establishing and operating the joint welfare projects under paragraph ①.
④ In connection with local love gift certificates under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Act on Promotion of Use of Local Love Gift Certificates, the Mayor may issue and operate welfare cards as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑤ To efficiently operate joint welfare projects under paragraph ①, the Mayor may establish and operate a Jeonnam-Gwangju Small and Medium Enterprise Welfare Center and entrust its operation to a specialized institution prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 221 (Special comprehensive State support for small merchants)
① The State may provide necessary support in cooperation with local governments to stabilize the business operations and promote the sustainable growth of small merchants affected by changes in business environments, restructuring of commercial districts or economic disparities between regions following establishment of the Integrated Special City.
② The State may establish and implement special financial and policy support provisions within the scope of linkage to existing small merchant support systems to provide support under paragraph ①.
③ In implementing support under paragraphs ① and ②, the State may give priority to small merchants in any of the following areas: <Amended on 2026.6.2>
1. Population-declining areas under Article 2, subparagraph 12 and areas of concern for population decline under subparagraph 12-2 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth;
2. Rural areas under Article 3, subparagraph 5 of the Framework Act on Agriculture, Rural Community and Food Industry, mountain villages under Article 3, subparagraph 2 of the Framework Act on Forestry, and fishing villages under Article 3, subparagraph 6 of the Framework Act on Fisheries and Fishing Villages Development;
3. Economically vulnerable areas where business conditions for small merchants have deteriorated.
④ The State may support local governments' improvement policies to ensure that financial and business conditions for small merchants do not deteriorate compared with conditions before establishment of the Integrated Special City.
⑤ To increase sales of small merchants and neighborhood commercial districts within the Integrated Special City and revitalize the regional economy, the State may expand and operate small merchant support projects, including issuance, distribution and discount support of local love gift certificates under the Act on Promotion of Use of Local Love Gift Certificates and Onnuri gift certificates under the Special Act on the Development of Traditional Markets and Shopping Districts.
⑥ Support under paragraphs ① through ⑤ shall be implemented according to the division of roles between relevant central administrative agencies and local governments, and the State and local governments shall jointly bear the necessary funding.

Article 222 (Special provisions concerning establishment of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Small Merchant and Market Promotion Fund)
① The Mayor may establish and operate the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Small Merchant and Market Promotion Fund (hereinafter referred to as the "Fund" in this Article) to support business stability, growth and structural advancement of small merchants, including merchants in traditional markets, etc.
② The Fund shall be financed by:
1. Contributions from the Integrated Special City;
2. Income from operation of the Fund and other income.
③ Matters necessary for management and operation of the Fund shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 223 (Establishment of a citizen-participatory digital ecosystem for a regional circular economy)
① The Mayor may establish and operate a regional circular economy ecosystem based on digital technologies to strengthen an independent circular structure of the regional economy, efficiently manage regional public assets, and expand citizen participation.
② The regional circular economy ecosystem under paragraph ① shall include:
1. A system for issuance and distribution of digital local currency of the Integrated Special City;
2. A citizen-participatory management system for regional public assets;
3. Digital platforms supporting transactions by local enterprises and small merchants;
4. Joint investment platforms for citizen-participatory regional development projects;
5. A system for earning and redeeming rewards points for participation in public interest activities;
6. Platforms for revitalizing the regional data economy.

Article 224 (Special provisions concerning funds for promoting youth startups)
① To secure financial resources necessary for promoting youth startups and supporting youth startup enterprises within the Integrated Special City, the Mayor may establish and operate a youth startup enterprise promotion fund (hereinafter referred to as the "Fund" in this Article) as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② The Fund shall be financed by:
1. Support payments and subsidies from local governments;
2. Contributions from the general account of the Integrated Special City;
3. Donations and sponsorships;
4. Other amounts received pursuant to statutes.
③ The Fund shall be used for:
1. Support for projects promoting youth startups;
2. Support for youth startup enterprises;
3. Support for other projects deemed necessary by the Mayor.
④ The State may provide administrative and financial support to promote youth startup enterprises in the Integrated Special City.

Article 225 (Designation of opportunity development special zones)
① Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City applies for designation of an opportunity development special zone under Article 23 (1) of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth, the Minister of Trade and Industry may give priority to designating the area pursuant to paragraph (2) of the same Article. <Amended on 2026.6.2>
② The State and the Integrated Special City may provide administrative and financial support to individuals and corporations investing in opportunity development special zones.

Article 226 (Special provisions concerning support for industrial crisis areas)
Preferential support may be provided by applying Article 51 of the Special Act on Local Autonomy and Decentralization and Balanced Growth mutatis mutandis to areas designated as preemptive response areas for industrial crises under Article 8 of the Special Act on Response to Local Industrial Crises and Recovery of Regional Economies and as special industrial crisis response areas under Article 10 of that Act within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City. <Amended on 2026.6.2>

Article 227 (Special provisions concerning support for regional energy transition)
① Notwithstanding Article 30 of the Framework Act on Carbon Neutrality and Green Growth for Coping with Climate Crisis, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may formulate and implement policies giving priority to supporting energy transition, including measures to disseminate and expand new and renewable energy within the Integrated Special City in accordance with the basic principles under Article 3 of that Act to respond to the climate crisis. In such cases, the Mayor shall consult in advance with the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment under Article 7 of the Act on the Promotion of the Development, Use and Diffusion of New and Renewable Energy.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary to implement energy transition support policies under paragraph ①.

Article 228 (Creation of energy self-sufficient cities)
① The State shall actively support the Integrated Special City in becoming an energy self-sufficient city based on renewable energy and promising growth industries to promote the expansion of renewable energy, the use of distributed energy and sustainable urban competitiveness.
② For projects prescribed by Presidential Decree that ensure stable and efficient renewable energy supply to the energy self-sufficient city under paragraph ①, including distributed energy projects under the Special Act on the Promotion of Distributed Energy and construction of intelligent power grids under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Act on the Construction and Promotion of Use of Intelligent Electric Grids, the State may provide funds from the following funds or budgets:
1. The Electric Power Industry Infrastructure Fund under Article 48 of the Electric Utility Act;
2. The Special Account for Energy and Resources Projects under Article 3 of the Special Accounts Act on Energy and Resources Projects.
③ Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City deems it necessary to designate a national industrial complex under Article 2, subparagraph 8 (a) of the Industrial Sites and Development Act to create an energy self-sufficient city, the Mayor may request the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport to designate one.

Article 229 (Special provisions concerning electric utility businesses)
① The authority of the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment under Articles 7, 9, 10, 12, 13, 61 (1) through (5), 71, and 108 (3) of the Electric Utility Act (limited, in the case of Article 108 (3), to imposition and collection of administrative fines relating to transferred powers), and Articles 8 (1), 20 and 52 (3) of the Electrical Safety Management Act (limited, in the case of Article 52 (3), to imposition and collection of administrative fines relating to transferred powers), shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, limited to solar and wind power generation businesses with a capacity of not more than 20,000 kilowatts among renewable energy sources under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Act on the Promotion of the Development, Use and Diffusion of New and Renewable Energy.
② A Renewable Energy Generation Project Deliberation Committee shall be established under the Mayor to deliberate on permits, authorization, etc. concerning power generation businesses under paragraph ①; matters necessary for the committee's composition, operation and functions shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ Where the Mayor grants permission or authorization, etc. under paragraphs ① and ② after deliberation by the Renewable Energy Generation Project Deliberation Committee under paragraph ②, such deliberation shall be deemed deliberation by the Electricity Commission under the Electric Utility Act notwithstanding Articles 7 (2), 10 (2) and 12 (1) of that Act.
④ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment under Articles 10 (3), the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 12 (5), the former part of Article 61 (1), Article 61 (2), the former part of Article 61 (3), Article 61 (5) and (6) of the Electric Utility Act and the former part of Article 8 (1), the former part of Article 8 (2), Article 8 (3) and (5) of the Electrical Safety Management Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance: Provided, That this shall be limited to solar and wind power generation businesses among the new and renewable energy sources under the Act on the Promotion of the Development, Use and Diffusion of New and Renewable Energy.
⑤ In addition to matters prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment under Article 7 (6) of the Electric Utility Act, specific standards and procedures for solar and wind power generation businesses taking regional characteristics into account may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 230 (Special provisions concerning designation of preliminary offshore wind power generation districts)
When intending to designate a preliminary district under Article 14 (1) of the Special Act on the Promotion of Offshore Wind Power Distribution and Fostering of the Industry, the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries shall consult with the Mayor of the Integrated Special City in advance before deliberation and resolution by the Offshore Wind Power Generation Committee under Article 6 of that Act. The Mayor may present opinions reflecting regional industrial development plans, compensation for losses of fishing rights, acceptance by local residents, and environmental and landscape characteristics, etc.

Article 231 (Special provisions concerning licensed aquaculture and permitted fishing in offshore wind power generation districts)
① To facilitate offshore wind power projects and promote coexistence with fisheries, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may, notwithstanding the Aquaculture Industry Development Act, permit licensed aquaculture in public waters designated as offshore wind power generation complexes to the extent that it does not interfere with installation or operation of offshore wind power generation facilities.
② The Mayor may permit fishing under the Fisheries Act in public waters within offshore wind power generation complexes to the extent that it does not interfere with the safety and operation of offshore wind power facilities.
③ The Mayor shall determine and publicly notify standards for permitting aquaculture and fishing under paragraphs ① and ②, eligible sea areas, types of fishing, safety management and restrictions on operations.

Article 232 (Special provisions concerning designation and development of ports)
① Notwithstanding Article 3 (3) 1 of the Harbor Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may request the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries to designate a port necessary for construction and subsequent management of offshore wind power generation facilities as a nationally managed coastal port. Upon receiving the request, the Minister may designate the port after consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies where designation is deemed reasonable. Development, management and operation of the designated port shall be governed by the Harbor Act and other relevant statutes.
② To facilitate offshore wind power generation projects, the State shall endeavor to ensure that port master plans can be promptly amended under Articles 5 and 7 of the Harbor Act where rapid changes in economic circumstances, including port facility supply and demand forecasts and port cargo volume forecasts, occur or where efficient port development, management or operation is necessary.
③ To facilitate offshore wind power generation projects, the State may establish a specialized offshore wind power industrial complex under Article 45 of the Special Act on Strengthening Competitiveness and Stabilizing Supply Chains of Materials, Components and Equipment Industries within the Integrated Special City having jurisdiction over preliminary districts or generation districts.

Article 233 (Fostering the floating solar photovoltaic industry)
① The State shall endeavor to encourage, protect and foster technology development, use and dissemination of floating solar photovoltaic systems among renewable energy sources under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Act on the Promotion of the Development, Use and Diffusion of New and Renewable Energy within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City.
② To foster floating solar photovoltaic systems under paragraph ①, the State shall formulate policies concerning technology development, demonstration projects, support for commercialization, institutional improvements concerning connections to power grids, and rationalization of related authorization and permission procedures.
③ When promoting floating solar photovoltaic systems, etc., the Mayor shall encourage resident-participatory business models enabling local residents to participate and a portion of profits to be returned to the region, and provide necessary support.

Article 234 (Special provisions concerning installation of new and renewable energy facilities in buffer greenbelts near industrial complexes)
Under Article 38 of the Act on Urban Parks and Green Areas, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may install or permit installation of new and renewable energy facilities in buffer green areas surrounding industrial complexes to the extent that such installation does not undermine the purpose of establishing the green areas.

Article 235 (Special support for building power grids to promote distributed energy)
① The State may provide administrative support for establishing facilities necessary for electricity transactions between distributed energy sources and consumers within the Integrated Special City.
② Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City requests transmission business operators or distribution business operators under Article 2, subparagraphs 6 and 8 of the Electric Utility Act to install transmission or distribution facilities, etc. to attract electricity demand within special areas for distributed energy under the Special Act on the Promotion of Distributed Energy (hereinafter referred to as "special distributed energy areas"), the State may support all or part of the expenses.
③ Procedures and methods for support under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree. Detailed standards may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree in consideration of the characteristics of projects within the Integrated Special City.
④ Where power grids expanded through construction projects under paragraph ① are used, the relevant distributed energy generator or consumer shall pay grid usage fees as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 236 (Special State support for alleviating renewable energy grid saturation)
① The State shall give priority to preparing comprehensive measures to alleviate power grid saturation in areas of the Integrated Special City where saturation occurs or is expected due to large-scale dissemination of renewable energy, including expansion of transmission and transformation facilities, establishment of grid management facilities and installation of energy storage devices, to stabilize the power grid and enable additional connections.
② The State shall secure financial resources necessary to implement grid saturation measures under paragraph ① and implement them in phases in cooperation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and electric utility business operators under Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Electric Utility Act.
③ The Mayor may request the State and relevant electric utility business operators to take measures necessary to alleviate grid saturation, and the State shall actively consult on such requests.

Article 237 (Support standards for grid stabilization devices)
To resolve power grid instability caused by the large-scale connection of renewable energy, the State shall establish separate support standards to guarantee reasonable profitability, taking into account that grid stabilization devices installed and operated for that purpose (including secondary battery-based energy storage systems) incur additional equipment and operating costs unlike ordinary power generation facilities.

Article 238 (Direct investment by the Integrated Special City and local public enterprises)
① The Integrated Special City and local public enterprises may invest in new and renewable energy generation projects or special-purpose corporations jointly established by public and private entities.
② The Integrated Special City and local public enterprises shall use part of the profits arising from new and renewable energy projects for regional community development and energy transition support.
③ Specific procedures, limits, reporting and auditing concerning investment by the Integrated Special City and local public enterprises shall be governed by relevant statutes.

Article 239 (Establishment of special accounts for profit sharing from new and renewable energy)
① The Mayor may establish a special account for sharing profits from new and renewable energy to ensure stable promotion of new and renewable energy generation projects and profit-sharing systems.
② The special account for sharing profits from new and renewable energy shall be used for:
1. Implementing publicly led and resident-participatory new and renewable energy projects and operating profit-sharing systems;
2. Installing and maintaining new and renewable energy infrastructure;
3. Education, publicity and strengthening residents' capacity relating to profit sharing from new and renewable energy;
4. Supporting technological development and establishment of regional industrial ecosystems for new and renewable energy;
5. Expenses necessary to raise, operate and manage the special account for profit sharing from new and renewable energy;
6. Other projects relating to profit sharing from new and renewable energy prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance;
7. Projects to improve living conditions for residents of neighboring areas, conserve fisheries and support regional development.

Article 240 (Support for publicly led new and renewable energy projects)
The State and the Integrated Special City may provide necessary administrative and financial support to ensure that new and renewable energy projects led by or involving public institutions, etc. contribute to securing the public interest, improving acceptance by residents and promoting mutual prosperity with local communities.

Article 241 (Special provisions on limits on capital contributions and bond issuance by local public enterprises engaging in new and renewable energy projects)
① Notwithstanding Articles 54 and 68 of the Local Public Enterprises Act, limits on capital contributions and bond issuance shall not apply where a local public enterprise invested in by the Integrated Special City contributes capital or issues bonds to participate in new and renewable energy generation projects or to establish and operate related corporations.
② A local public enterprise intending to contribute capital or issue bonds under paragraph ① shall consult with the Minister of the Interior and Safety. Notwithstanding paragraph ①, the Minister may impose restrictions or conditions on the scale of contributions or bond issuance, considering the financial soundness of the local public enterprise, project feasibility and impacts on the regional economy.
③ A local public enterprise intending to contribute capital or issue bonds under paragraph ① shall undergo a review of the necessity and feasibility of investment under Article 54 of the Local Public Enterprises Act or a feasibility review of new investment projects under Article 65-3 of the same Act.
④ Notwithstanding paragraph ③, the following projects shall be exempt from feasibility reviews:
1. Projects involving an amount not exceeding the amount prescribed by Presidential Decree;
2. Projects exempted from feasibility reviews under Articles 54 (3) and 65-3 (2) of the Local Public Enterprises Act.

Article 242 (Special provisions on establishment of artificial intelligence clusters)
① To strengthen global competitiveness of the artificial intelligence industry, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may designate a metropolitan-level cluster organically connecting research and development hubs, infrastructure and renewable energy (hereinafter referred to as a "cluster").
② The State shall directly implement or support the establishment, expansion and functional advancement of the following facilities within a cluster and may provide the necessary administrative, financial and technical support:
1. National artificial intelligence data centers;
2. Infrastructure and related facilities based on next-generation artificial intelligence semiconductors (including neural processing units).
③ The State may support expenses necessary for stable operation of the facilities under paragraph ②.
④ To ensure sustainable growth of clusters, the State may give priority to support for training specialized personnel through cooperation among universities, research institutions and enterprises, and attracting global talent.
⑤ Projects relating to construction of facilities or relocation of enterprises within clusters shall be deemed necessary to realize national artificial intelligence policies, and the heads of relevant administrative agencies may process related authorization and permission as deemed granted or expedite the procedures.

Article 243 (Establishment of a national artificial intelligence innovation hub)
① To establish a sustainable foundation for innovation that will enable the Republic of Korea to become one of the world's three leading powers in artificial intelligence, the State shall develop the Integrated Special City, where industrial, technical and demonstration infrastructure in artificial intelligence and energy is concentrated, as a national artificial intelligence innovation hub. The State may support expansion of education, experiential opportunities and public services to improve accessibility to artificial intelligence and the ability of citizens of the Integrated Special City to use it.
② The State may support construction and operation of integrated transportation, logistics, information and communications infrastructure connecting the national artificial intelligence innovation hub under paragraph ① with the entire Integrated Special City.

Article 244 (Special provisions concerning designation of artificial intelligence clusters)
① The State may designate as an artificial intelligence cluster a functional, physical and regional concentration of enterprises, institutions and organizations engaged in research and development of artificial intelligence and artificial intelligence technologies promoted by the Mayor under Article 23 (1) of the Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of a Foundation for Trust, and may provide administrative, financial and technical support.
② The State may designate a dedicated institution to comprehensively support related affairs so that artificial intelligence clusters established by the Mayor become effectively rooted in the region.
③ In designating a dedicated institution under paragraph ②, the State shall consider an institution recommended by the Mayor.
④ The State may make contributions or provide subsidies for all or part of expenses necessary to operate the dedicated institution and implement its projects.
⑤ Notwithstanding other Acts, the State may proactively establish infrastructure facilities such as electricity and water supply before demand arises in order to construct artificial intelligence data centers within an artificial intelligence cluster.
⑥ The State may support all or part of the expenses of persons intending to construct artificial intelligence data centers within a cluster.

Article 245 (Designation of artificial intelligence city demonstration districts and regulatory exceptions)
① To foster the Integrated Special City as a demonstration hub for artificial intelligence, energy, mobility, cultural convergence technologies, etc., the State may designate areas selected by the Mayor as artificial intelligence city demonstration districts (hereinafter referred to as "demonstration districts").
② A demonstration district designated under paragraph ① shall be deemed a specialized smart city district designated under Article 29 of the Act on the Promotion of Smart City Development and Industry, and that Article shall apply mutatis mutandis.
③ Notwithstanding the Act on the Management of Outdoor Advertisements, etc. and Promotion of Outdoor Advertisement Industry and other relevant statutes, the following special provisions may apply temporarily within demonstration districts to the extent necessary for demonstrating new technologies:
1. Regulatory exceptions concerning installation of digital and intelligent advertisements and public information facilities;
2. Regulatory exceptions concerning transportation for demonstrations of autonomous driving.

Article 246 (Special provisions concerning fostering the artificial intelligence data industry)
① At the request of the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, the State may provide integrated support within areas of the Integrated Special City for the entire cycle from collection and utilization of artificial intelligence data through technology development, demonstration and commercialization to remove barriers to use of such data.
② To systematically support the collection, management and utilization of artificial intelligence data and establish a safe and reliable environment for its use, the State may establish an artificial intelligence data bank under paragraph ③ within an area under paragraph ① and have an institution designated by the State or Mayor operate it.
③ In this Article, "artificial intelligence data bank" means a public infrastructure-based platform for managing and using data that collects, refines, combines, manages and provides data necessary for artificial intelligence learning, inference, validation and service development, and incorporates technical and administrative measures to protect personal information and ensure data security.
④ An artificial intelligence data bank shall perform the following functions:
1. Establishing and providing data for artificial intelligence training and validation using public and private data;
2. Processing and managing data for safe utilization, including de-identification, anonymization and combination;
3. Supporting access to and use of data for artificial intelligence technology development, demonstration and commercialization;
4. Supporting quality management, standardization and reliability of artificial intelligence data.
⑤ An institution designated by the State or Mayor under paragraph ② shall operate the artificial intelligence data bank in an interconnected and cooperative manner within the area under paragraph ①, taking into account consistency with national artificial intelligence and data policies and related projects under relevant statutes, including the Framework Act on the Development of Artificial Intelligence and Establishment of a Foundation for Trust, the Framework Act on Promotion of Data Industry and Utilization of Data, the Act on Promotion of the Provision and Use of Public Data, and the Personal Information Protection Act.
⑥ The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary to establish and operate artificial intelligence data banks under paragraph ②.
⑦ The State shall ensure that relevant central administrative agencies and public institutions actively cooperate in the provision and use of public data for the smooth operation of artificial intelligence data banks.

Article 247 (Linked development and support of cities specializing in artificial intelligence and energy convergence industries)
① Based on artificial intelligence infrastructure and energy resources in the Integrated Special City, the State shall jointly foster cities specializing in mobility, aerospace, biotechnology, healthcare, culture, etc. to promote balanced regional development and create new national growth engines.
② To promote linkages and convergence of high-tech industries, the Mayor shall establish an integrated basic plan for fostering specialized industrial cities every three years and may designate areas meeting the following requirements as specialized industrial cities following consultation with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies:
1. Enterprises, research institutes, universities, etc. in high-tech strategic industries are concentrated or are planned to be concentrated there;
2. Research, demonstration and production infrastructure and enterprise support facilities for high-tech strategic industries have been established or are planned to be established;
3. Mutual complementarity and linkage effects among specialized industrial ecosystems are recognized.
③ For areas designated under paragraph ②, the Mayor may apply for designation as specialized complexes under the Special Act on Strengthening and Protecting Competitiveness of National High-Tech Strategic Industries, the Special Act on Strengthening Competitiveness and Stabilizing Supply Chains of Materials, Components and Equipment Industries, etc.; the State may give priority to examining such applications.
④ Under an integrated basic plan for fostering specialized industrial cities pursuant to paragraph ②, the State and the Integrated Special City may provide administrative and financial support for:
1. Planning and coordination of joint research and development and demonstration projects among specialized industrial cities;
2. Establishment and promotion of joint utilization systems for infrastructure, data and resources among specialized industrial cities;
3. Integrated support for attracting enterprises and investments;
4. Operation of personnel training and exchange programs and joint publicity;
5. Transportation links among specialized industrial cities;
6. Other projects necessary to foster specialized industrial cities.

Article 248 (Introduction of agentic artificial intelligence administrative systems)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may introduce agentic artificial intelligence into all administrative processes to fully automate simple and repetitive duties.
② The Mayor shall deploy agentic artificial intelligence for principal administrative tasks, including handling civil petitions, reviewing authorization and permission, and identifying persons eligible for welfare benefits, and provide uninterrupted administrative services 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

Article 249 (Digital twin policy simulation)
① Before making major policy decisions involving budgets of ten billion won or more, the Integrated Special City may simulate policy effects and adverse effects using a digital twin that virtualizes the entire Integrated Special City.
② The State shall recognize a special provision permitting the use of the latest private-sector large language models (LLMs), following security processing, through the common government-wide artificial intelligence infrastructure even within national security networks.

Article 250 (Special provisions concerning designation and support of semiconductor industry specialized complexes)
① Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City requests designation of a semiconductor industry specialized complex under Article 16 (1) of the Special Act on Strengthening and Protecting Competitiveness of National High-Tech Strategic Industries, the Minister of Trade and Industry may give priority to designating the relevant area as such a complex.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for specialized semiconductor industry complexes designated under paragraph ①.
③ To facilitate establishment and operation of specialized semiconductor industry complexes, the State shall promptly establish and support the following industrial infrastructure facilities, and may support all or part of the expenses thereof according to criteria prescribed by Presidential Decree:
1. Facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree for electricity supply (including new and renewable energy generation);
2. Facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree for water supply;
3. Facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree for wastewater and waste treatment;
4. Roads prescribed by Presidential Decree connecting to specialized semiconductor industry complexes;
5. Other facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree as necessary for the smooth establishment and operation of specialized semiconductor industry complexes.

Article 251 (Support for new industrialization linking the semiconductor and defense industries)
① The State may provide support necessary to promote new industrialization linking the semiconductor and defense industries in the Integrated Special City.
② Matters necessary for support for new industrialization linking the semiconductor and defense industries shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ To support the Integrated Special City in securing foundational semiconductor technologies and connecting them to the semiconductor industry, the State may provide necessary administrative and financial support to research institutions situated within its jurisdiction.

Article 252 (Creation of a future mobility city)
The State may create a future mobility city in the Integrated Special City to systematically pursue artificial intelligence-based innovation in mobility and spatial connectivity and realize a sustainable urban model in which advanced mobility industries coexist with infrastructure.

Article 253 (Special provisions concerning establishment of future mobility clusters)
① To foster the Integrated Special City as a global hub of the future mobility industry, the Mayor may designate a Jeonnam-Gwangju Future Mobility Cluster (hereinafter referred to as a "cluster" in this Article) linking multiple industrial complexes, research complexes and demonstration zones within its jurisdiction. The cluster shall include:
1. Industrial complexes linked to the future mobility city under Article 252, the national industrial complex for future vehicles, etc.;
2. Establishment of technology development and demonstration infrastructure for future mobility, including autonomous vehicles, connected cars, environmentally friendly mobility, urban air mobility (UAM), drones, batteries, mobile robots, software and mobility as a service (MaaS);
3. Establishment of cooperation networks among component, materials and finished product manufacturers for joint development, production and supply chains, and smart manufacturing innovation systems;
4. Support for mutually beneficial cooperation between large enterprises and small and medium-sized enterprises and for international quality certification and standardization.
② The State may give priority to regulatory exceptions under Article 12, advanced mobility pilot projects under Article 15, and training of specialized personnel under Article 17 of the Act on the Promotion of and Support for Mobility Innovation for mobility-specialized cities designated under Article 10 of that Act, and may support the necessary expenses.
③ Heads of relevant administrative agencies receiving requests for consultation on authorization and permission concerning the establishment and operation of clusters, including relocation of enterprises, construction of facilities and changes to use districts, shall present their opinions within 30 days. Where no opinion is presented within that period, consultation shall be deemed completed.
④ The Mayor shall establish and operate a one-stop service window dedicated to the designation of clusters, attraction of enterprises, provision of incentives and follow-up management.
⑤ Where a request for financial support, financing or regulatory improvement concerning clusters is made, the State shall give the request the highest priority for review notwithstanding other statutes and notify the results within 30 days.

Article 254 (Special provisions concerning promotion of the mobility industry and delegation of authority over regulatory exceptions)
① The State may provide administrative, financial and technical support to the Integrated Special City to foster advanced mobility industries.
② To foster advanced mobility industries, the State may delegate to the Mayor the following powers:
1. Powers of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport concerning expedited verification of regulations under Article 11 and applications for regulatory exceptions under Article 12 (1) through (3) of the Act on the Promotion of and Support for Mobility Innovation;
2. Powers of the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport concerning applications for regulatory exceptions, etc. under Articles 49 (1), (4) and (5), 49-2 and 50 of the Act on the Promotion of Smart City Development and Industry;
3. Powers of the Minister of Trade and Industry concerning expedited regulatory verification under Article 10-2 and applications for regulatory exceptions for demonstration under Article 10-3 (1), (3) and (4) of the Industrial Convergence Promotion Act.

Article 255 (Special provisions concerning designation of autonomous vehicle pilot operation zones)
① Notwithstanding Article 7 of the Act on the Promotion of and Support for Commercialization of Autonomous Vehicles, where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City deems it necessary to designate an area within the jurisdiction as a pilot operation zone, the Mayor may designate such a zone following consultation with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport and deliberation and resolution by the Local Committee on Autonomous Vehicle Pilot Operation Zones. The same shall apply to changes to or cancellation of designation.
② Matters necessary for designation, alteration and cancellation of pilot operation zones other than those prescribed by this Act shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary under paragraph ①.

Article 256 (Designation of specialized complexes for the future vehicle parts industry)
① Where the Mayor applies to promote the future vehicle parts industry within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City, the Minister of Trade and Industry may give priority to designating the relevant area as a complex, district or area under the subparagraphs of Article 20 (1) of the Special Act on the Promotion of Transition and Development of Ecosystems of the Future Vehicle Parts Industry, pursuant to Article 20 of that Act.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for operating specialized future vehicle parts industry complexes designated under paragraph ①.

Article 257 (Special provisions concerning designation of urban air mobility pilot operation areas)
① Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City requests designation of a pilot operation area under Article 8 of the Act on the Promotion of and Support for Utilization of Urban Air Mobility, the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport shall give priority to reviewing the request.
② The State may provide necessary administrative and financial support under paragraph ①.

Article 258 (Designation of specialized complexes for materials, components and equipment industries)
① Where the Mayor applies for designation of a specialized complex for materials, components and equipment industries under Article 45 (2) of the Special Act on Strengthening Competitiveness and Stabilizing Supply Chains of Materials, Components and Equipment Industries to foster such industries within the Integrated Special City, the Minister of Trade and Industry may give priority to designating the relevant area.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for specialized complexes designated under paragraph ①.
③ Where the Mayor applies for designation of a supply chain center for materials, components and equipment industries under Article 23-3 of the Special Act on Strengthening Competitiveness and Stabilizing Supply Chains of Materials, Components and Equipment Industries to systematically collect and analyze supply chain information and support projects necessary to stabilize supply chains, the Minister of Trade and Industry may give priority to designating a person meeting the requirements under the subparagraphs of paragraph (1) of that Article within the relevant area.
④ The Minister of Trade and Industry may make contributions or provide subsidies within budgetary limits for expenses necessary for the operation of supply chain centers and performance of their projects.

Article 259 (Special provisions concerning designation and support of aerospace industry specialized complexes)
① Where the Mayor requests designation of an aerospace industry specialized complex under Article 8-2 of the Aerospace Industry Development Promotion Act, the Administrator of the Korea AeroSpace Administration may give priority to designating the relevant area.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for aerospace industry specialized complexes designated under paragraph ①.
③ The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for a national space industrial complex within the Integrated Special City's jurisdiction to foster the space industry and establish a space industry cluster.
④ The State may provide incentives, including subsidies and loans, to enterprises and institutions related to the space industry.
⑤ The Mayor may establish a special fund to support financing and operation of facilities necessary for the national space industrial complex.
⑥ The Mayor shall cooperate with relevant administrative agencies to link space industry policies and shall formulate and support policies to establish a space industry cluster in the Integrated Special City.

Article 260 (Special provisions concerning designation of space industry investment promotion districts)
① Notwithstanding Article 23-2 (1) of the Space Development Promotion Act, where the Mayor requests designation of a space industry investment promotion district, the Administrator of the Korea AeroSpace Administration may give priority to designating and establishing the relevant area as a space industry investment promotion district.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for space industry investment promotion districts designated under paragraph ①.

Article 261 (Special provisions concerning promotion of the secondary battery industry)
① To foster the Integrated Special City as a national strategic hub for the secondary battery industry, the State may concentrate preferential support on the following matters ahead of other regions:
1. Establishment of medium- and long-term comprehensive plans for fostering the secondary battery industry and linkage with national plans;
2. Establishment and joint use of infrastructure for research and development, demonstration, testing, and performance and reliability evaluation related to secondary batteries;
3. Promotion of specialized projects for localization of secondary battery raw materials, materials, components and equipment and establishment of stable supply chains;
4. Simplification of authorization and permission procedures or application of regulatory exceptions for facility and research and development investments in the secondary battery industry;
5. Specialized personnel support projects to train, attract and retain secondary battery experts;
6. State support for installing and expanding industrial infrastructure, including electricity, water supply, wastewater treatment and logistics facilities related to the secondary battery industry;
7. Priority designation of specialized strategic industry complexes under Article 16 (1) of the Special Act on Strengthening and Protecting Competitiveness of National High-Tech Strategic Industries;
8. Other matters necessary for strengthening the competitiveness of the secondary battery industry in the Integrated Special City.
② In promoting projects under paragraph ①, the State may give priority to the Integrated Special City in financial support projects.
③ Matters necessary for support under paragraphs ① and ② shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 262 (Establishment of specialized defense clusters)
① The State and the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may provide administrative and financial support necessary to expand specialized defense clusters.
② The State may provide incentives to defense-related enterprises and institutions, including subsidies and loans.
③ The Mayor may establish a special fund to finance and support operation of facilities necessary for specialized defense clusters.
④ The Mayor shall cooperate with relevant administrative agencies to coordinate defense industry policies and formulate and support policies for establishing specialized defense clusters in the Integrated Special City.

Article 263 (Special support for fostering the intelligent robotics industry)
① When establishing a master plan under Article 5 of the Intelligent Robots Development and Distribution Promotion Act, the State may give priority to reflecting matters necessary for the Integrated Special City to effectively develop and distribute intelligent robots.
② Notwithstanding Article 6 (2) of the Intelligent Robots Development and Distribution Promotion Act, the State may give priority to contributions, loans and other necessary administrative and financial support to persons implementing projects or duties requested by the Mayor for research and development, demonstration, distribution and commercialization of intelligent robots within the Integrated Special City.

Article 264 (Support for naval vessel maintenance, repair and overhaul)
① The State may support facilities or projects within the Integrated Special City to foster the maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) industry for Navy and Coast Guard vessels.
② The State may provide necessary financial, fiscal and other support to enterprises and institutions involved in vessel maintenance, repair and overhaul in the Integrated Special City.

Article 265 (Support for transition of the petrochemical industry)
To promote structural transition of the petrochemical industry, realize carbon neutrality and stabilize national supply chains, the State may provide the following support to the petrochemical industry within the Integrated Special City:
1. Upgrading aging petrochemical processes and transitioning to high-value-added and fine chemical processes;
2. Demonstration and commercialization of circular economy, recycling and bio-based chemical technologies;
3. Research, development and demonstration for transition to low-carbon and carbon-free petrochemical processes;
4. Employment stabilization and retraining of personnel during industrial transition.

Article 266 (Designation of low-carbon steel special zones)
① Where necessary to strengthen competitiveness of the steel industry and promote transition to carbon neutrality, the Minister of Trade and Industry may designate low-carbon steel special zones within the Integrated Special City under the Special Act on Strengthening Competitiveness of the Steel Industry and Transition to Carbon Neutrality.
② Designation, cancellation and support of low-carbon steel special zones shall be governed by Articles 23 through 25 of the Special Act on Strengthening Competitiveness of the Steel Industry and Transition to Carbon Neutrality.

Article 267 (Support for shipbuilding industry projects)
The State may concentrate support on the following shipbuilding-related projects within the Integrated Special City to strengthen the national competitiveness of the shipbuilding industry, promote environmentally friendly and digital transitions and ensure the sustainability of national key industries:
1. Development and demonstration of technologies for vessels and equipment using environmentally friendly fuels (including electricity, hydrogen and ammonia);
2. Digitalization and advancement of shipbuilding processes, including autonomous ships, smart shipbuilding and digital twins;
3. Automation and improvement of energy efficiency of production processes in the shipbuilding industry;
4. Employment stabilization, job transitions and training of specialized personnel following industrial transition in shipbuilding.

Article 268 (Financial support for industrial transition)
① In promoting industrial transition under this Act, the State shall give priority to linkage with existing national financial projects concerning industrial transition, carbon neutrality and energy transition.
② The State may provide financial support for projects under paragraph ① in phases within budgetary limits.
③ Financial support under this Act may be coordinated to avoid duplication with support for similar purposes under other Acts.

Article 269 (Special provisions on establishment of green convergence clusters)
① Under Article 5 of the Act on the Establishment and Fostering of Green Convergence Clusters, the State and the Integrated Special City may establish the following green convergence clusters to promote green industries, etc. in the Integrated Special City and strengthen the competitiveness of relevant enterprises:
1. Clean air industry clusters;
2. Resource circulation clusters for used solar photovoltaic panels;
3. Other green convergence clusters deemed necessary by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
② The State and the Integrated Special City may provide the following support to green convergence clusters and enterprises located therein:
1. Research and technological development of green industries, etc. under Article 3 of the Act on the Establishment and Fostering of Green Convergence Clusters (hereinafter referred to as "green industries, etc." in this Article);
2. Training of specialized personnel, promotion of startups and commercialization, and support for market entry in relation to green industries, etc.;
3. Demonstration of technologies relating to green industries, etc.;
4. Other matters deemed necessary by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment and the Mayor to foster and concentrate green industries.
③ The State may provide financial support necessary to establish and operate green convergence clusters under paragraphs ① and ②.

Article 270 (Special provisions concerning establishment of regional investment corporations)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may establish a regional investment corporation as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance to form investment capital within the region and establish a financing support system for venture businesses and emerging industries.
② The Government shall support preferential establishment of a regional investment corporation under paragraph ① within the Integrated Special City and provide all administrative support necessary for its establishment and operation.

Article 271 (Special provisions concerning the Environmental Health Act)
① Consultation shall be requested with the Mayor of the Integrated Special City notwithstanding Article 13 (1) of the Environmental Health Act for projects for which consultation with the Mayor is required under Article 172 (1).
② When reviewing or evaluating impacts on public health following a request for consultation under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall hear the opinions of the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the head of the relevant local environmental agency and reflect those opinions to the greatest extent possible.
③ The authority of the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment or the heads of local environmental agencies under Article 13 (1) and (2) of the Environmental Health Act regarding consultation under paragraph ① shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.

CHAPTER III AGRICULTURE, FORESTRY AND FISHERIES

Article 272 (Establishment of master plans for the food technology industry)
① When establishing a master plan for fostering the food technology industry under Article 5 of the Act on Fostering the Food Technology Industry, the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs may reflect the following matters:
1. Objectives and basic policy directions for fostering the food technology industry in the Integrated Special City;
2. Domestic and international trends and development prospects for the food technology industry in the Integrated Special City;
3. Compilation and management of food technology statistics in the Integrated Special City;
4. Support for research and development to advance the food technology industry in the Integrated Special City;
5. Training of specialized personnel necessary for the food technology industry in the Integrated Special City;
6. Support for startups and overseas market entry to develop the food technology industry in the Integrated Special City;
7. Other matters necessary to foster the food technology industry in the Integrated Special City.
② The Mayor shall formulate and implement an annual implementation plan under the master plan for fostering the food technology industry.
③ Other matters necessary for the formulation and implementation of implementation plans shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 273 (Designation of food technology innovation clusters)
The State may designate food technology innovation clusters under Articles 5 (2) 8 and 14 of the Act on Fostering the Food Technology Industry within the Integrated Special City.

Article 274 (Surveys and compilation of statistics concerning the food technology industry)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may conduct fact-finding surveys and compile and manage statistics on the food technology sector to formulate and efficiently implement policies concerning food technology.
② The scope and methods of fact-finding surveys, compilation and management of statistics under paragraph ① and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 275 (Special support for fostering the food technology industry)
The powers of the Government under Articles 9 through 12 of the Act on Fostering the Food Technology Industry shall be vested in the Integrated Special City.

Article 276 (Special provisions concerning regulatory improvement in the food technology industry)
Notwithstanding Article 15 (1) through (4) of the Act on Fostering the Food Technology Industry, where the Mayor deems regulatory improvement necessary, the Mayor may request the Regulatory Rationalization Committee under Article 23 of the Framework Act on Administrative Regulations to abolish or improve regulations or submit opinions pursuant to Articles 17 and 17-2 of the same Act.

Article 277 (Designation of rural vitality promotion special zones)
① To generate rural vitality and promote related private investment, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City may designate a rural vitality promotion special zone (hereinafter referred to as a "promotion special zone") following consultation on strategic environmental impact assessment under Article 16 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act and consideration of the following matters:
1. Whether the area requires rural revitalization and spatial regeneration in response to population decline and for balanced regional development;
2. Whether the area requires improved access to transportation, including roads and railways, or has potential to attract private investment;
3. Whether it serves the public interest by contributing to regional development, including regional economic revitalization and development of underdeveloped areas;
4. Whether other requirements prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance are satisfied.
② Before designating a promotion special zone, the Mayor shall hear the opinions of the heads of Sis, Guns and Gus having jurisdiction and local residents, consult with the heads of relevant administrative agencies and undergo deliberation by the Basic Plan Deliberation Council.
③ Upon designating a promotion special zone, the Mayor shall publicly notify the details in the public bulletin as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance and notify the heads of relevant Sis, Guns and Gus and relevant administrative agencies.
④ Paragraphs ② and ③ shall also apply where the location, boundaries or area of a promotion special zone is altered: Provided, That this shall not apply to minor changes prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑤ Where the Mayor deems that the purpose of designation has been achieved, etc., the Mayor may cancel designation of a promotion special zone following deliberation by the Basic Plan Deliberation Council.
⑥ Procedures, methods and management concerning designation, alteration or cancellation of promotion special zones and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑦ The State and the Integrated Special City may provide financial support necessary for areas designated as promotion special zones under paragraph ①.
⑧ Notwithstanding Articles 30 (1) and 31 (2) of the Farmland Act, the Mayor may designate, alter or cancel designation of agricultural promotion areas within promotion special zones without approval from the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs.
⑨ The authority of the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs concerning permission or consultation (including permission or consultation on changes) for conversion of farmland within promotion special zones under Article 34 of the Farmland Act shall be vested in the Mayor.

Article 278 (Special provisions concerning an increase in the age limit for young farmers and fishers)
① Notwithstanding Article 2, subparagraph 2 of the Act on Fostering and Supporting Successor Farmers and Fishers and Young Farmers and Fishers, the age of young farmers and fishers may be differently prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② The Mayor may provide support for all or part of the expenses incurred as a result of adjusting the age of young farmers and fishers in the Integrated Special City.

Article 279 (Special provisions concerning designation and support of smart agriculture promotion districts)
① Notwithstanding Article 15 (1) of the Act on Fostering and Supporting Smart Agriculture, where the Mayor intends to designate a smart agriculture promotion district (hereinafter referred to as a "promotion district" in this Article) to modernize agriculture and strengthen competitiveness within the Integrated Special City, the Mayor may establish a promotion district development plan under paragraph (3) of the same Article and publicly notify the designation following consultation with the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs.
② Where a promotion district is designated or its development plan is established or amended under paragraph ①, "Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs" in Article 15 (2), (5), (6) and (8) of the Act on Fostering and Supporting Smart Agriculture shall be construed as "Mayor of the Integrated Special City", and "Mayor/Do Governor" as "head of a Si/Gun/Gu".
③ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under Article 15 (9) of the Act on Fostering and Supporting Smart Agriculture may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
④ Where the Mayor designates a promotion district under paragraph ①, the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs may provide administrative and financial support for establishing and improving agricultural infrastructure, research and development related to smart agriculture, smart agriculture education, etc.

Article 280 (Special provisions concerning application of the Mountainous Districts Management Act)
① The powers of the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service under Article 6 (limited to promotion districts), Articles 14 (1) through (3) (excluding national forests managed by the Korea Forest Service), 15-2 (excluding national forests managed by the Korea Forest Service), 17 (1) and (2) (limited to matters relating to transferred powers), 20 (1), 21 (1) (limited to transferred powers), 37 (1) through (4) (limited to transferred powers), 38 (1) through (4) (limited to transferred powers), 39 (2) and (3) (limited to transferred powers), 40 (1) through (3) (limited to transferred powers), 41 (limited to transferred powers), 42 (1) and (2) (limited to transferred powers), 43 (1) and (2) (limited to transferred powers), 44 (1) and (2) (limited to transferred powers), 47 (1) (limited to investigations concerning transferred powers), 48 (1) through (3) (limited to compensation for losses caused by acts relating to transferred powers), 49 (limited to hearings concerning transferred powers), 50 (limited to fees relating to transferred powers), and 57 (3) (limited to imposition and collection of administrative fines concerning transferred powers) of the Mountainous Districts Management Act shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
② Notwithstanding Article 22 (1) 1 of the Mountainous Districts Management Act, to handle affairs transferred to the Mayor under Article 383, the following matters shall undergo deliberation by the Local Mountainous District Management Committee under Article 22 (2) 1 of that Act:
1. Alteration or cancellation of designation of conservation mountainous districts under Article 6 (4) of the Mountainous Districts Management Act;
2. Permission for temporary use of mountainous districts including at least 500,000 square meters of conservation mountainous districts under Article 15-2 (1) of that Act.

Article 281 (Special provisions concerning development of fishery resources)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may formulate and implement support policies necessary to promote exports of fishery products under Article 45 of the Framework Act on Fisheries and Fishing Villages Development and facilitate overseas market entry of seafood products under Article 10 of the Act on Fostering and Supporting the Seafood Industry.
② Notwithstanding Article 4 (3) of the Fisheries Act and Article 9 (2) of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act, the Mayor may exercise authority to formulate fishing ground use and development plans and licensed aquaculture ground use and development plans for sea areas under the Integrated Special City's jurisdiction as prescribed by Presidential Decree.
③ The Mayor shall directly carry out the following matters in accordance with the procedures for approval of fishing ground use and development plans and licensed aquaculture ground use and development plans and for disposition of licenses:
1. Receipt and examination of applications for development plans;
2. Approval of development plans;
3. Determination of priorities for license dispositions and notification of final permission.
④ The following matters shall be excluded from application of the special provisions under this Article:
1. Implementation of international conventions or fishery resource agreements between countries;
2. National-level regulations necessary for conserving the marine environment and ensuring the safety of fishing vessels.
⑤ The authority of the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries under Article 41 (1) 7 and (2) of the Fishery Resources Management Act shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
⑥ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries under Article 62 (2) 5 and (4) of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act, the former part of Article 37-12 (3), Articles 37-13 (2) and 37-15 (3) of the Aquatic Life Disease Control Act, the latter part of Article 44 (4), Article 44 (5), and Article 49 (7) 5 of the Fishery Resources Management Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑦ The authority of the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries under Articles 40 (1), 60 (1) and 81 (3) and (5) of the Fisheries Act shall be vested in the Mayor.
⑧ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries under the proviso to Article 21 (4), Article 21 (6), the proviso to Article 23 (1), and Article 23 (3) of the Fishery Seed Industry Promotion Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑨ Notwithstanding the latter part of Article 46 (2) of the Fisheries Act, the Mayor may conduct experimental fishing (excluding offshore fishing) without approval from the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries. In such cases, the Mayor shall consult in advance with the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
⑩ Matters required to be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries under Article 46 (4) of the Fisheries Act (limited to experimental fishing) may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑪ The approval authority of the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries under the latter part of Article 53 (2) of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act shall be vested in the Mayor. In such cases, the Mayor shall hear the opinion of the President of the National Institute of Fisheries Science.
⑫ Matters required to be prescribed by Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries under Article 53 (4) of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act (limited to experimental aquaculture) may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑬ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries under the former and latter parts of Article 25 (1), Article 25 (4), Article 38 (3), and Article 55 (3) of the Fishing Management and Promotion Act (limited, in the case of Article 55 (3), to imposition and collection of administrative fines concerning transferred powers) may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑭ To promote marine leisure activities, where a person licensed for village fishing or cooperative aquaculture under Article 8 (1) of the Fisheries Act or Article 10 (1) 5 of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act applies for designation of a recreational fishing ground under Article 62 of the Fisheries Act or Article 55 of the Aquaculture Industry Development Act, the Mayor may designate part of the fishing ground as a recreational fishing ground to the extent that the licensed fishing or aquaculture is not hindered. In such cases, the Fisheries Act and the Aquaculture Industry Development Act shall not apply to methods of catching or collecting aquatic animals and plants within the recreational fishing ground.
⑮ Matters necessary for designation criteria, recreational fishing activities, methods and quantities of catching or collecting aquatic animals and plants, and management and operation of recreational fishing grounds under paragraph ⑭ may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
<16> Where a person designated to operate a recreational fishing ground under paragraph ⑭ fails to operate it in accordance with paragraph ⑮, the Mayor may cancel the designation.

Article 282 (Operation of direct payment schemes promoting public interest functions of fisheries and fishing villages)
① Notwithstanding Article 6 of the Act on the Operation of Direct Payment Schemes to Promote Public Interest Functions of Fisheries and Fishing Villages, the Mayor may pay direct payments for disadvantaged areas to fishers engaging in fishing businesses designated by the Mayor.
② The Mayor may provide administrative and financial support necessary to pay direct payments under paragraph ①.

Article 283 (Special provisions concerning management and utilization of marine healing resources)
① The Mayor may survey marine healing resources for the designation or alteration of marine healing districts under Article 9 of the Act on the Management and Utilization of Marine Healing Resources and may propose such designation or alteration to the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries.
② When making a designation or alteration under paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may, where deemed necessary for metropolitan linkages and efficient promotion of the marine healing industry, integrate and designate areas extending across two or more Sis, Guns or Gus or multiple separate areas as one marine healing district.
③ Where multiple areas are designated as one district under paragraph ②, the Mayor shall establish and implement a plan for allocation of functions and linked development considering the characteristics of resources in each area.

Article 284 (Special provisions concerning certification of rural convergence industry operators)
① To revitalize rural convergence industries, notwithstanding Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Act on Fostering and Supporting Rural Convergence Industries, the Mayor may recommend to the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs a person falling under subparagraph 2 of the same Article for certification as a rural convergence industry operator even if the person does not reside in a rural area.
② The Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs may receive a certification application under Article 8 (1) of the Act on Fostering and Supporting Rural Convergence Industries from a person recommended by the Mayor under paragraph ① and certify the person as a rural convergence industry operator.

Article 285 (Special provisions concerning promotion of and support for distribution of agricultural and fishery products)
① To stabilize supply and demand and improve the efficiency of distribution systems for agricultural and fishery products, the Mayor shall formulate and implement measures to modernize wholesale markets for agricultural and fishery products (hereinafter referred to as "wholesale markets"), agricultural and fishery product auction markets (hereinafter referred to as "auction markets"), and comprehensive agricultural and fishery product distribution centers (hereinafter referred to as "comprehensive distribution centers") under Article 2, subparagraphs 2, 5 and 12 of the Act on Distribution and Price Stabilization of Agricultural and Fishery Products and to promote balanced development of distribution networks among regions.
② The Integrated Special City may establish a special fund for financing and operating facilities necessary for wholesale markets within its jurisdiction under paragraph ①, financed by:
1. Contributions from the general account of the Integrated Special City;
2. Usage fees under Article 42 of the Act on Distribution and Price Stabilization of Agricultural and Fishery Products;
3. Other donations and sponsorships, etc.
③ The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for wholesale markets, auction markets and comprehensive distribution centers in the Integrated Special City to perform central distribution functions through organic linkages.
④ The Mayor shall establish an operating committee including producer and consumer organizations to make decisions on major policies and support matters.

Article 286 (Special provisions concerning roles of livestock quarantine officers and duties of public veterinarians)
① Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under Article 7 of the Act on the Prevention of Contagious Animal Diseases (limited to qualification, appointment and commissioning of livestock quarantine officers) may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Notwithstanding Article 21 (1) of the Veterinarians Act, the Mayor may commission veterinarians who do not operate or work at an animal hospital to perform the duties under subparagraphs 2, 3 and 5 of the same paragraph, as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ The Mayor may appoint or commission veterinarians commissioned as public veterinarians under paragraph ② as inspectors under Article 13 (1) of the Livestock Products Sanitary Control Act.

Article 287 (Special provisions concerning support for animal welfare livestock farms)
Notwithstanding Article 64 (1) of the Animal Protection Act, the Mayor may provide the following support to animal welfare livestock farms certified under Article 59 of the same Act (hereinafter referred to as "certified farms" in this Article):
1. Expenses necessary to improve livestock housing to protect animals and enhance their welfare;
2. Guidance, consultation and education on environmental improvement and management of certified farms;
3. Consultation, advice and promotional activities to develop markets for livestock products produced on certified farms;
4. Information, publicity and investment attraction to enter and expand overseas markets for livestock products produced on certified farms;
5. Other matters necessary for management stability of certified farms.

Article 288 (Special provisions concerning supply of locally produced agricultural products for school and public meals)
① Heads of central administrative agencies, local governments and public institutions providing school meals, public meals, etc. in the Integrated Special City may give priority to purchasing agricultural products produced in the Integrated Special City (including simply processed products).
② The State or public institutions may purchase agricultural, livestock and fishery products produced in the Integrated Special City by negotiated contract.
③ Where a negotiated contract is concluded under paragraph ②, it may be concluded with an Integrated Food Support Center under Article 23-6 (3) of the Framework Act on Agriculture, Rural Community and Food Industry.
④ Methods and procedures for negotiated contracts under paragraph ② shall be governed by relevant statutes, including the Act on Contracts to Which the State Is a Party.
⑤ The State and local governments shall endeavor to ensure that high-quality agricultural, livestock and fishery products are supplied to the State or public institutions under paragraphs ① through ④, giving priority to improving the quality of meals.

Article 289 (Special provisions concerning promotion of return to farming, fishing and rural areas)
To help young people returning to farming, fishing and rural areas settle stably, the Mayor may provide support necessary for rural settlement for the following projects as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance:
1. Support for employment and startups of young people returning to farming, fishing and rural areas;
2. Support for settlement conditions for such young people;
3. Support for capability development and livelihood stability for such young people.

Article 290 (Special provisions concerning restrictions on permission for conversion of farmland)
Facilities required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under the subparagraphs of Article 37 (1) of the Farmland Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance: Provided, That the standards shall not be made less restrictive than the limitations under the Farmland Act.

Article 291 (Special provisions concerning establishment and operation of farmland management committees)
① Notwithstanding Article 37-3 of the Farmland Act, the Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall establish a Farmland Management Committee in the Integrated Special City to provide advice on the following matters:
1. Formulation of policies concerning the utilization and preservation of farmland in the Integrated Special City;
2. Agricultural promotion areas and permission for conversion of farmland, etc. in promotion special zones designated within the Integrated Special City;
3. Other matters submitted to the Farmland Management Committee by the Mayor as deemed necessary.
