② Article 37-3 (2) through (4) of the Farmland Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the members, chairperson and terms of office of the Farmland Management Committee under paragraph ①. In such cases, "Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs" shall be construed as "Mayor of the Integrated Special City".
③ Other matters necessary for the composition and operation of the Farmland Management Committee under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 292 (Special provisions concerning establishment of advanced agricultural food export complexes)
① The Mayor may designate and establish advanced agricultural food export complexes to promote agricultural food exports from the Integrated Special City.
② The Mayor may establish an institution responsible for overall operation and support to efficiently operate advanced agricultural food export complexes under paragraph ①.
③ The State may provide administrative and financial support for projects under paragraphs ① and ②.

Article 293 (Special provisions on support from the fisheries development fund)
When establishing master plans and annual implementation plans through the Fishery Product Distribution Development Council under Article 9 (1) of the Act on Management of and Support for Distribution of Fishery Products and plans for operation of the Fisheries Development Fund under Article 46 of the Framework Act on Fisheries and Fishing Villages Development, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may provide the following support for sustainable fisheries within the Integrated Special City and stabilization of fishery product prices:
1. Funding for government stockpiling and purchasing of fishery products to alleviate accumulated supplies in production areas and stabilize prices;
2. Distribution funding in production and consumption areas to promote consumption of fishery products;
3. Other matters necessary for compensating fishers' income and stabilizing their operations.

Article 294 (Special provisions concerning designation and support of leading smart fisheries districts)
① To foster smart fisheries based on information and communication technologies within the Integrated Special City, the Mayor may designate leading smart fisheries districts (hereinafter referred to as "leading districts"), establish development plans for such districts and publicly notify them in the public bulletin. The Mayor shall consult in advance with the heads of Sis, Guns and Gus when designating leading districts and establishing their development plans. Procedures and methods of designation and other necessary matters shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Where the Mayor designates a leading district under paragraph ①, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may provide administrative and financial support within budgetary limits for the establishment and improvement of fisheries infrastructure, smart fisheries research and development, smart fisheries education, etc.

Article 295 (Special provisions concerning fishery resource protection zones)
① The authority of Mayors/Do Governors to designate or change fishery resource protection zones under Articles 29 (2) and 40 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City within its jurisdiction.
② When designating or changing a fishery resource protection zone under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall undergo deliberation by the local urban planning committee under Article 113 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act.
③ Matters necessary for designation or alteration of fishery resource protection zones shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 296 (Special provisions concerning marine spatial management plans and management)
The authority of the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries under Article 12 of the Act on Marine Spatial Planning and Management to designate and change marine use zones shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, limited to sea areas under its jurisdiction.

Article 297 (Special provisions concerning coastal management)
① The authority of the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries under the main sentence of Article 24 (1), the proviso to the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 24 (2), Article 24 (3), Article 24 (4) 1, Article 25, Article 26 (1) and (2), Article 27, Article 28 (3), Article 34 (1) and (3), Articles 35 and 36, and Article 39 (2) of the Coastal Management Act (limited, for Article 39 (2), to imposition and collection of administrative fines concerning transferred powers) shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City. In such cases, deliberation by the Central Coastal Management Deliberation Council under Article 21 (2) of the same Act shall not be required.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Oceans and Fisheries under Article 5 (6), the proviso to Article 24 (1), the main sentence of the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 24 (2), Article 24 (2) 1 and 4, Article 24 (5), Article 25 (1), the proviso to Article 25 (3), Article 33 (2), Article 34 (4), Article 36 (3) and the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 39 (1) of the Coastal Management Act (limited, for Article 39 (1), to imposition and collection of administrative fines concerning transferred powers) may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 298 (Special provisions concerning designation and development of national fishing ports)
Where the Mayor of the Integrated Special City requests the new designation of a national fishing port under Article 17 of the Fishing Villages and Fishery Harbors Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may review the feasibility of the request and designate and develop the port.

Article 299 (Special provisions concerning support for local fishing ports)
Where it is deemed necessary to implement development linked to national marine and fisheries policies, etc. in local fishing ports designated and managed by the Mayor under Article 17 of the Fishing Villages and Fishery Harbors Act, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may provide financial support for the target fishing ports.

Article 300 (Special provisions concerning logistics support for island residents)
The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary to stabilize the lives and improve settlement conditions of residents of islands within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City under Article 2 of the Islands Development Promotion Act.

Article 301 (Special provisions concerning fostering and support of fishing village associations)
Matters concerning the operation of fishing village associations and their officers, etc. in the Integrated Special City shall be governed by the articles of incorporation of the relevant fishing village association.

Article 302 (Special provisions concerning dividends to residents from marine ecosystem carbon sinks and marine energy profits)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may establish and promote resident-participatory profit-sharing models that link carbon sink projects in marine ecosystems, including tidal flats and seaweed, with new and renewable marine energy projects, such as offshore wind power, so that profits are returned to local residents.
② Notwithstanding the Act on the Promotion of the Development, Use and Diffusion of New and Renewable Energy and the Local Finance Act, the Mayor may pay periodic profit dividends to local residents (hereinafter referred to as "sea pensions" in this Article), financed by electricity sales revenues, carbon emission allowance trading revenues, etc. generated from projects under paragraph ①.
③ To establish stable financing for sea pensions under paragraph ②, the Mayor may establish a fund involving power generation business operators, certified carbon sink project operators, resident cooperatives, etc.; matters necessary for raising and operating the fund shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
④ Detailed matters concerning recipients of sea pensions, payment criteria, payment amounts and rates of resident participation under paragraph ② shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 303 (Special provisions concerning introduction and operation of agricultural disaster index insurance)
① To protect farms within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City from typhoons and other weather disasters, the Mayor may implement pilot agricultural disaster index insurance projects (hereinafter referred to as "index insurance") paying insurance proceeds based on indices calculated from meteorological and climate data, including wind speed, precipitation and temperature.
② To operate index insurance under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall establish and implement a plan including:
1. Designation of crops and weather indices subject to index insurance;
2. Acquisition of meteorological and climate data and methods for objectively validating weather indices;
3. Insurance payment standards and calculation of premium rates for each index interval;
4. Support for insurance premiums and operation of reinsurance.
③ To facilitate operation of index insurance, the Mayor may establish a Jeonnam-Gwangju Agricultural Disaster Insurance Fund as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance, and local governments may support part of insurance premiums within budgetary limits.
④ Where the Mayor implements an index insurance pilot project under paragraph ①, authority to deliberate on and approve insurance products shall be deemed vested in the Mayor.
⑤ The State may provide the Mayor with meteorological and climate data from the Korea Meteorological Administration and relevant infrastructure of the National Institute of Agricultural Sciences necessary for operating index insurance.

Article 304 (Special provisions concerning promotion of industries related to smart agriculture)
① Notwithstanding Article 19 (1) of the Act on Fostering and Supporting Smart Agriculture, the Mayor may formulate policies to foster service industries related to smart agriculture that use smart agriculture data, etc. to support crop or livestock growth and disease management.
② Policies under paragraph ① shall include:
1. Support for startups of enterprises related to smart agriculture;
2. Support for research and development by such enterprises;
3. Support for developing domestic and overseas markets by such enterprises;
4. Other projects necessary to foster enterprises related to smart agriculture.
③ Before implementing projects under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall consult in advance with the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs to ensure consistency with national smart agriculture policies.
④ The Minister may provide necessary administrative and financial support within budgetary limits for policies prepared or promoted by the Mayor under paragraph ①.

Article 305 (Special provisions concerning utilization of green biotechnology industry data)
① Notwithstanding Article 13 of the Act on Fostering the Green Biotechnology Industry, the Mayor may perform duties concerning the creation, management and utilization of data generated in the research, demonstration and industrialization of the green biotechnology industry.
② Duties concerning green biotechnology industry data that the Integrated Special City may perform under paragraph ① shall include:
1. Standardization of data related to the green biotechnology industry;
2. Generation, collection, preservation and transmission of such data;
3. Sharing, joint utilization and trading of such data;
4. Establishment of a foundation for joint utilization of green biotechnology industry data platforms;
5. Other matters necessary for digital transformation of the green biotechnology industry.
③ In managing and utilizing data under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall ensure consistency with national green biotechnology industry policies, data policies, standards, security systems and policies of relevant central administrative agencies, and shall consult in advance with the Minister of Agriculture, Food and Rural Affairs.
④ Where the Minister deems that duties performed by the Integrated Special City under paragraph ② contribute to implementing national policies for fostering the green biotechnology industry, the Minister may provide necessary administrative and financial support within budgetary limits.

Article 306 (Special provisions concerning promotion of the seafood industry and establishment of advanced fishery product export complexes and clusters)
① An integrated industrial system linking the production, processing, distribution and export of seafood products may be established to strengthen the competitiveness of the seafood industry in the Integrated Special City.
② To foster the seafood industry and promote exports of fishery products under paragraph ①, the Mayor may designate and establish advanced fishery product export complexes and seafood industry clusters (hereinafter referred to as "specialized complexes, etc.").
③ To establish specialized complexes, etc. under paragraph ②, the State may reflect the establishment of industrial complexes combining seafood processing, research and development, distribution and startup functions in national or sectoral plans under relevant statutes.
④ The State may provide administrative and financial support for securing sites, obtaining authorization and permission, simplifying project procedures and establishing infrastructure necessary for specialized complexes, etc. under paragraphs ② and ③.

Article 307 (Special provisions concerning designation of wintering and summering zones)
① Notwithstanding restrictions on acts in marine national parks under Articles 18 and 23 of the Natural Parks Act, where the Mayor deems it necessary to reduce damage to aquaculture products caused by climate change and maintain stable production, the Mayor may designate certain water surfaces within a marine national park as wintering or summering zones following consultation with the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment.
② Standards and procedures for conserving marine ecosystems and minimizing landscape damage in wintering or summering zones under paragraph ① may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance following consultation with the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment.

Article 308 (Special provisions concerning support for residents of remote outermost islands)
To stabilize the lives and improve the quality of life of residents of remote outermost islands of the Integrated Special City, the Mayor may, notwithstanding Article 5 of the Special Act on Support for Remote Outermost Islands such as Ulleungdo and Heuksando, establish a comprehensive development plan for remote outermost islands within the Integrated Special City and support the following projects. The State may provide administrative and financial support:
1. Support for transportation and logistics costs;
2. Support for medical, educational and care services;
3. Support for expanding basic living infrastructure, including water supply, electricity and telecommunications;
4. Housing and relocation support to improve residential environments and promote relocation to rural and fishing communities;
5. Other matters necessary to guarantee basic living rights of residents of remote outermost islands.

Article 309 (Special provisions concerning development of inhabited islands)
① Within the guidelines established by the Minister of the Interior and Safety under Article 6 (2) of the Islands Development Promotion Act, the Mayor may designate inhabited islands within the Integrated Special City as islands subject to development under Article 4 of the same Act. Designation and alteration shall undergo deliberation by the Integrated Special City Islands Development Deliberation Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Islands Development Deliberation Committee") established as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② The authority of the Minister of the Interior and Safety under Article 5 of the Islands Development Promotion Act shall be vested in the Mayor. Upon designating an island for development, the Mayor shall publicly notify:
1. Development objectives;
2. The islands subject to development and the scope of development projects;
3. An outline of development projects;
4. Project implementation periods.

Article 310 (Special provisions concerning designation of tidal flat management zones and conservation of marine ecosystems)
① To strengthen autonomous management of marine spaces, promote sustainable utilization of tidal flats and surrounding areas and develop the Integrated Special City as a hub for tidal flat ecotourism, the Mayor may, notwithstanding Article 10 (1) of the Act on Sustainable Management and Restoration of Tidal Flats and Surrounding Areas, designate an area of tidal flats, etc. falling under either of the following as a Jeonnam-Gwangju Tidal Flat Management Zone (hereinafter referred to as a "management zone"):
1. An area having a landscape or ecosystem representative of the tidal flats of the Integrated Special City;
2. An area where maintaining clean and healthy tidal flats is necessary.
② Before designating or changing a management zone, the Mayor shall prepare a designation plan including the following particulars, hear the opinions of the head of the relevant local government and local residents, consult with the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries and undergo deliberation by the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Tidal Flat Management Committee under paragraph ④:
1. Grounds and objectives for designation or alteration;
2. Present conditions and characteristics of major tidal flat ecosystems;
3. Use districts and current uses of land within the proposed area and adjoining land;
4. Present status of fishing rights, mining rights and other uses;
5. Current status of areas subject to statutory regulations.
③ Where the Mayor designates a management zone under paragraph ①, the Mayor may take necessary measures, including designation of management zones, establishment of management plans and designation of clean tidal flats, as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance in accordance with Articles 10 through 15 of the Act on Sustainable Management and Restoration of Tidal Flats and Surrounding Areas.
④ Notwithstanding Article 7 of the Act on Sustainable Management and Restoration of Tidal Flats and Surrounding Areas, a Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Tidal Flat Management Committee (hereinafter referred to as the "Committee" in this Article) shall be established within the Integrated Special City to deliberate on:
1. Designation and alteration of management zones;
2. Establishment of management plans for each zone;
3. Designation of clean tidal flats;
4. Other matters deemed necessary by the chairperson.
⑤ The Committee shall consist of not more than 20 members, including a chairperson. The Mayor shall serve as chairperson, and the members shall be persons prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance from among public officials of relevant central administrative agencies and persons with extensive expertise or experience in marine environments and marine and fishery industries commissioned by the Mayor. Other matters necessary for operating the Committee shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑥ Where the Mayor designates a management zone to conserve and utilize tidal flat ecosystems, the State may provide financial support for:
1. Projects to raise awareness of tidal flats, etc. under Article 6 of the Act on Sustainable Management and Restoration of Tidal Flats and Surrounding Areas;
2. Biodiversity conservation measures for tidal flats, etc. under Article 9 of the same Act;
3. Duties concerning management zones under Article 13 of the same Act.
⑦ At the request of the Mayor, the Minister of Oceans and Fisheries may designate a national marine ecosystem park in the Integrated Special City under Article 43-2 (1) of the Marine Ecosystems Conservation and Management Act to systematically conserve and manage marine resources of the Integrated Special City.

Article 311 (Establishment and operation of the agricultural and rural development fund)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall establish and operate an agricultural and rural development fund under this Act to eliminate disparities among regions and develop agriculture and rural communities.
② The sources, uses and other operational matters of the agricultural and rural development fund shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance and shall include projects for compensating, adjusting and supporting disparities among Sis, Guns and Gus.

CHAPTER IV HUMAN RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT AND WELFARE

Article 312 (Establishment of childcare centers or kindergartens exclusively for children of foreigners)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City or a social welfare corporation under Article 16 of the Social Welfare Services Act may establish and operate childcare centers exclusively for children of foreigners to provide effective childcare for such children, and the Mayor may provide support to the relevant social welfare corporation. Matters necessary for establishing and operating such childcare centers shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② The Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may establish and operate kindergartens exclusively for children of foreigners to provide effective education for such children. Matters necessary for establishing and operating such kindergartens shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ Where necessary, the Mayor and the Superintendent of Education may subsidize childcare and education expenses for children using childcare centers or kindergartens under paragraphs ① and ②; detailed standards concerning beneficiaries and payment procedures shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 313 (Special provisions concerning university-led lifelong and vocational education)
To foster talent tailored to regional characteristics, the Mayor and the Superintendent of Education may establish a cooperative system involving specialized high schools, industry-tailored high schools, universities, industries and relevant administrative agencies, and operate lifelong and vocational education policies in a linked and integrated manner.

Article 314 (Special provisions concerning selection of local talent for regional strategic industries)
① The head of a university situated in the Integrated Special City may conduct special admissions for departments specialized in regional strategic industries within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree under Article 15 (1) of the Act on the Development of Local Universities and Colleges and Regional Human Resources: Provided, That prior consent from the Minister of Education shall be required for medical, Korean medical, dental, pharmacy and nursing colleges under Article 15 (2) of the same Act.
② The region eligible for special admission of local talent under paragraph ① shall be the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City.
③ Criteria for designation of specialized departments under paragraph ①, requirements for linkage to regional strategic industries, and matters concerning cooperation and support from local governments shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 315 (Support for integrated universities within the Integrated Special City)
Where universities within the Integrated Special City pursue integration to enhance educational and research capacities or international competitiveness, the State may provide necessary administrative and financial support.

Article 316 (Special provisions concerning introduction of pension schemes for elderly retired farmers)
① The Integrated Special City may introduce a pension scheme for elderly farmers retiring from agriculture.
② Beneficiaries, eligibility conditions, payment amounts, and other matters necessary for operating the pension scheme shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary to introduce a pension scheme in the Integrated Special City.

Article 317 (Special provisions concerning realization of a basic society)
① The Mayor may give priority to policies relating to a basic society in response to changes in social, economic and demographic structures in order to foster the Integrated Special City as a leading region for guaranteeing people's basic living standards and realizing a basic society.
② The Mayor may formulate and implement pilot projects and specialized policies concerning a basic society that reflect regional conditions and characteristics in fields directly relating to basic living, including care, housing, healthcare, education, transportation, energy and income security.
③ The scope, beneficiaries, procedures, financing, delivery systems and other matters necessary for pilot projects and specialized policies under paragraph ② shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
④ The State may provide administrative and financial support for the smooth implementation of pilot projects and specialized policies under paragraphs ② and ③, and their performance may be used as reference and reflected in future national policies and institutional design concerning a basic society.

Article 318 (Special provisions concerning consultations on establishment or amendment of social security schemes)
Where the Mayor undertakes projects concerning childbirth promotion, population support, care, etc., the Mayor may request the Minister of Health and Welfare to simplify consultation procedures concerning establishment or amendment of social security schemes notwithstanding Article 26 (2) of the Framework Act on Social Security.

Article 319 (Special provisions concerning funds to address low birthrates)
① The Mayor may establish a low-birthrate response fund as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance to raise financial resources necessary to address low birthrates in the Integrated Special City.
② The low-birthrate response fund shall be financed by:
1. Support payments and subsidies from local governments;
2. Contributions from the general account of the Integrated Special City;
3. Donations and sponsorships;
4. Other amounts received pursuant to statutes.
③ The fund shall support projects undertaken by the Integrated Special City to address low birthrates.
④ Matters necessary for establishing and operating the fund shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 320 (Designation of special care zones of the Integrated Special City)
① The Mayor may designate and operate special care zones of the Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as "special care zones") to provide care for infants, children, persons with disabilities and older persons.
② The Mayor shall consult in advance with the Superintendent of Education concerning linkage and cooperation between care projects implemented in special care zones and care provided to children by kindergartens under Article 2 of the Early Childhood Education Act and schools under Article 2 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.
③ The Mayor shall establish a special account for special care zones to ensure their stable operation.
④ The Mayor may provide support for existing care projects as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑤ The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary to operate special care zones.

Article 321 (Special provisions concerning establishment of youth jobs tailored to the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City)
① The State and the Mayor may prepare and operate projects and policies to create specialized jobs suited to regional circumstances and culture in the Integrated Special City under Article 17 of the Framework Act on Youth.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support for operating job support policies under paragraph ①.
③ Specific beneficiaries, methods and procedures of support projects shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 322 (Special support for residents' basic living to promote regional vitality)
① To improve residents' quality of life, the Mayor may provide allowances and other necessary financial support within budgetary limits to residents falling under any of the following:
1. Farmers striving to maintain the public interest functions of agriculture and promote sustainable rural development;
2. Artists and citizens engaged in activities to inherit and develop regional culture and arts and expand opportunities for citizens to enjoy culture;
3. Participants in lifelong learning seeking to contribute to developing regional human resources by strengthening capabilities throughout the life cycle and guaranteeing lifelong learning rights.
② When implementing support projects under paragraph ①, the Mayor may give priority to linked use of the Local Extinction Response Fund under the Framework Act on Local Government Fund Management or relevant national subsidies for efficient financial management.
③ Specific beneficiaries, requirements, amounts and methods of payment under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 323 (Protection and education of persons vulnerable to artificial intelligence)
① For digitally vulnerable groups, including older persons and persons with disabilities, the State may distribute barrier-free artificial intelligence interfaces operable by voice, gestures, brainwaves, etc.
② Artificial intelligence-based real-time sign language interpretation and visual assistance services may be provided at all public facilities and on public transportation within the Integrated Special City.

Article 324 (Special provisions concerning expansion of public medical infrastructure)
① In this Article, "public medical infrastructure, etc." means facilities, personnel or projects falling under any of the following:
1. Public health and medical service institutions and responsible medical institutions under the Public Health and Medical Services Act, and facilities, equipment, personnel and systems of cooperation necessary for them to perform their functions;
2. Projects to construct, expand or relocate public health and medical institutions, renovate aging facilities, and improve medical environments under the Public Health and Medical Services Act, the Act on the Establishment and Operation of Local Medical Centers, etc.;
3. Regional specialized medical systems and cooperative networks for providing essential medical care, including treatment of severe conditions, emergencies, childbirth, pediatrics and mental health, under the Framework Act on Health and Medical Services, the Emergency Medical Service Act, etc.;
4. Public hospitals and related infrastructure deemed necessary by the State or the Integrated Special City for disaster and emergency medicine, provision of essential medical services, responses to infectious diseases, etc. under the Emergency Medical Service Act, the Infectious Disease Control and Prevention Act, etc.;
5. Projects to stabilize the operation of emergency medical institutions in medically underserved areas under the Emergency Medical Service Act and expand their equipment and personnel;
6. Projects to improve settlement conditions and provide educational, research and living infrastructure, etc. to train regional doctors and encourage their long-term service under the Act on the Training and Support of Regional Doctors, etc.;
7. Public health doctors enlisted and assigned to medically underserved areas under the Military Service Act and the Act on Special Measures for Health and Medical Services in Agricultural and Fishing Villages, etc.;
8. Projects to install or expand facilities and equipment, undertake extensions, renovations or remodeling, etc. of regional cancer centers situated in the Integrated Special City and designated under Article 19 of the Cancer Control Act.
② The State and the Integrated Special City may support all or part of the costs and personnel required to expand and operate public medical infrastructure, etc. to establish a comprehensive regional essential medical care system within the Integrated Special City.
③ Except as otherwise specially prescribed by another Act, in providing support under paragraph ②, the State and the Integrated Special City shall give priority to strengthening the functions of responsible medical institutions, eliminating regional healthcare disparities and improving medical access in medically underserved areas.
④ The State and the Integrated Special City shall endeavor to ensure that State financial and policy support for emergency, essential and public medical services provided to the respective regions before establishment of the Integrated Special City is not reduced or discontinued.
⑤ The State may give priority to support for expenses under paragraphs ② and ③, taking into account fiscal conditions, etc.
⑥ The Mayor may use the Local Extinction Response Fund under the Framework Act on Local Government Fund Management to support operating expenses of hospitals in medically underserved areas and projects to improve settlement conditions for regional doctors and essential medical personnel.
⑦ Where a person intends to establish a general hospital under Article 3 (2) 3 (f) of the Medical Service Act within the Integrated Special City, the Mayor shall provide support so that a public implementer may establish a corporation with investors other than public implementers under Article 11-2 (1) of the Urban Development Act and promote urban development projects linked to the establishment of that general hospital under a healthcare facility installation plan.

Article 325 (Special financial support for youth support policies)
① The Mayor shall formulate and implement the following policies to provide locally specialized jobs, housing and cultural opportunities so that young people can settle in the region:
1. Expansion of employment opportunities for young people;
2. Support for youth housing;
3. Expansion of basic living infrastructure and cultural and assembly facilities.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support to prevent the outflow of young people from the Integrated Special City and promote their inflow and settlement.

Article 326 (Special provisions concerning operation of local medical centers)
Among local medical centers within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City, the State may give priority to support for operating expenses of local medical centers in medically underserved areas in the field of emergency medicine designated and publicly notified by the Ministry of Health and Welfare under Article 12 (2) and (3) of the Public Health and Medical Services Act, taking into account the financial circumstances of the relevant Si, Gun or Gu.

Article 327 (Special provisions concerning improving settlement conditions and support for foreign workers)
① The Mayor shall formulate and implement every five years a foreign worker support plan linked to the master plan and annual implementation plans for foreigner policies under Articles 5 and 6 of the Framework Act on Treatment of Foreigners Residing in the Republic of Korea to promote stable residence and settlement of foreign workers in agriculture, fisheries and manufacturing within the Integrated Special City. The plan shall include:
1. Fact-finding surveys of foreign workers' working and housing conditions;
2. Establishment of systems to protect human rights and promote rights and interests;
3. Operation of Korean language education and Korean cultural adaptation programs;
4. Measures to provide medical assistance and childcare and education support for their children.
② To improve housing welfare for foreign workers, the Mayor may, notwithstanding relevant statutes, support all or part of expenses necessary to construct, improve or repair dormitories or communal accommodations exclusively for foreign workers in rural areas within budgetary limits.
③ Where deemed necessary to resolve labor shortages within the Integrated Special City, the Minister of Justice may apply the following special provisions at the Mayor's request:
1. Relaxation of requirements for visa issuance and changes to status of stay under the Immigration Act;
2. Extension of periods of stay and simplification of reentry procedures for seasonal workers in agriculture and fisheries;
3. Expansion of quotas for region-specific visas permitting employment in specified areas or industrial sectors within the Integrated Special City.
④ The Mayor may establish and operate a Foreign Worker Support Center to facilitate linguistic communication and conflict resolution between foreign workers and employers, and the State may support its operating expenses.
⑤ The Mayor shall promote projects to increase exchanges between foreign workers and local residents and promote multicultural understanding so that foreign workers can integrate as members of regional communities.

Article 328 (Special provisions on creation and support of youth-specialized zones)
① The Mayor may formulate and implement policies necessary to create and support youth-specialized zones to generate youth employment and revitalize the regional economy within the Integrated Special City.
② The Mayor may comprehensively provide administrative and financial support and implement related policies to revitalize youth-specialized zones.

Article 329 (Establishment of the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Youth Development Fund)
① The Mayor may establish and operate the Jeonnam-Gwangju Integrated Special City Youth Development Fund (hereinafter referred to as the "Fund" in this Article) to promote employment, housing stability, welfare and local settlement of young people within the Integrated Special City.
② The Mayor may provide necessary support within budgetary limits to ensure stable financing of the Fund.
③ The Fund shall be used for:
1. Projects supporting entrepreneurship and employment skills among young people;
2. Projects supporting youth housing stability and living expenses;
3. Projects supporting youth cultural and artistic activities and expanding welfare facilities;
4. Projects promoting youth participation in regional communities and exchanges;
5. Other projects prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance to promote young people's rights, interests and development.
④ The Mayor shall be responsible for management and operation of the Fund; other matters necessary for raising, operating and managing the Fund shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 330 (Special provisions concerning scope of ancillary businesses of medical corporations)
A medical corporation operating a medical institution in the Integrated Special City may engage in ancillary businesses prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance in addition to those specified in the subparagraphs of Article 49 (1) of the Medical Service Act.

Article 331 (Establishment and operation of a public medical foundation)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City may establish and operate a public medical foundation within the Integrated Special City to expand metropolitan medical systems, including improving residents' health and healthcare conditions, substantially improving access to medical care in rural and underserved areas, and establishing a stable and continuous supply system for essential and public healthcare personnel.
② The Mayor shall provide administrative and financial support for establishing and operating the public medical foundation under paragraph ①.
③ Detailed matters necessary for establishment, organization and operation of the foundation and establishment of systems of cooperation with relevant private institutions shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 332 (Establishment and support of public postnatal care centers)
① The Mayor may establish and operate public postnatal care centers to increase birthrates and build care systems, taking account of demand and supply of postnatal care centers in the former jurisdictions of Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City.
② The Mayor shall give priority to administrative and financial support necessary for operation and expansion of facilities of public postnatal care centers.
③ Detailed matters necessary for establishment and entrusted operation of public postnatal care centers shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 333 (Special provisions concerning establishment and operation of violence and abuse reporting response centers)
① The Mayor and heads of Sis, Guns and Gus may establish and operate violence and abuse reporting response centers in cooperation with relevant administrative agencies, police agencies, educational institutions and relevant private institutions to efficiently prevent abuse of socially vulnerable persons, including children, older persons and persons with disabilities, and protect victims.
② The Mayor and heads of Sis, Guns and Gus shall provide administrative and financial support necessary for the smooth operation of centers under paragraph ①.
③ Detailed matters concerning organization, personnel management and systems of cooperation among relevant institutions shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 334 (Special support for medically underserved areas in emergency medicine)
The State may provide the following support to areas within the Integrated Special City designated and publicly notified as medically underserved areas in emergency medicine under Article 12 of the Public Health and Medical Services Act:
1. Support for establishing and operating emergency medical institutions;
2. Support for securing and training emergency medical personnel;
3. Support for modernizing emergency medical equipment and facilities;
4. Support for establishing and operating emergency patient transport systems.

Article 335 (Responsibilities of the State for higher education and development of local talent)
① The State may strategically support systems for higher education and local talent development centered on universities within the Integrated Special City to enable the Integrated Special City to function as a key hub for balanced national development and supra-regional growth strategies.
② The State may give priority to administrative and financial support for talent development, research and development, commercialization of technology, startups, job creation, shared equipment utilization and regional innovation projects undertaken in connection with universities and local industries and research institutions within the Integrated Special City.

Article 336 (Special support for joint growth of universities and regions)
① The State may provide institutional and financial support necessary to link and expand the education, research and industry-academia cooperation functions of universities with regional development following establishment of the Integrated Special City.
② The Mayor may cooperate with universities within the jurisdiction to formulate and implement higher education innovation plans linked to regional strategic industries, supra-regional cooperative projects and national policy projects.

Article 337 (Exclusion of disadvantages in participation in supra-regional cooperation and interministerial projects)
① Establishment of the Integrated Special City shall not cause disadvantages to universities, research institutions or the Integrated Special City when participating in supra-regional cooperative projects, interministerial projects, competitive funding projects, etc. promoted by the State or central administrative agencies.
② In selecting, evaluating and supporting such projects, the State shall endeavor to ensure that the scale of financial support, opportunities to participate and institutional status are not reduced compared with the period before establishment of the Integrated Special City.

Article 338 (Guarantee of existing levels of higher education and talent development support)
The State shall endeavor to maintain or guarantee higher levels of financial and institutional support for higher education and talent development previously received under relevant statutes by universities in the former jurisdictions of Jeollanam-do and Gwangju Metropolitan City following establishment of the Integrated Special City.

Article 339 (Designation of specialized universities)
① To train specialized personnel needed to foster future emerging industries, the Mayor may designate and support universities within the Integrated Special City as specialized universities or specialized graduate schools following consultation with the Minister of Education.
② The State may give priority to budgetary support necessary for such universities to serve as hubs for technology development and training personnel in future emerging industries.

Article 340 (Special provisions concerning promotion of employment of high school graduates in local public enterprises and regional strategic industries)
① In this Article, "high school graduate" means a person falling under any of the following subparagraphs who has not advanced to a school under Article 2 of the Higher Education Act:
1. A graduate or prospective graduate of a high school under Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
2. A graduate or prospective graduate of an industry-tailored high school under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
3. A graduate or prospective graduate of a specialized high school under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
4. A graduate or prospective graduate of an advanced technical school under Article 2, subparagraph 5 of the Elementary and Secondary Education Act;
5. A person recognized as having an educational qualification equivalent to high school graduation under the Elementary and Secondary Education Act.
② To promote job creation and foster a social climate that values skills over educational qualifications by supporting employment of high school graduates from underserved areas in local public enterprises and regional strategic industries receiving administrative or financial support, the Mayor may formulate and implement the following policies:
1. Expansion of jobs for high school graduates in local public enterprises and regional strategic industries;
2. Customized employment support and increased recruitment of high school graduates;
3. Awareness-raising projects promoting skill-based recruitment;
4. Support for career development after employment for high school graduates.
③ The following institutions or enterprises with at least 20 regular employees shall endeavor to recruit high school graduates for not less than 20 percent of their new regular positions each year:
1. Local public enterprises established by the Integrated Special City under the Local Public Enterprises Act;
2. Regional strategic industry enterprises receiving administrative and financial support from the Integrated Special City;
3. Enterprises designated by the Mayor among those located in industrial complexes within the Integrated Special City established under the Industrial Sites and Development Act;
4. Other institutions or enterprises prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
④ The Mayor may provide the following support to institutions or enterprises faithfully fulfilling the employment efforts under paragraph ③:
1. Support for part of personnel expenses arising from new employment of high school graduates;
2. Support for vocational training and qualification acquisition expenses;
3. Tax benefits, including reductions of local taxes;
4. Additional points when bidding for public procurement contracts of the Integrated Special City;
5. Other support prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑤ The Mayor may annually review employment status under paragraph ③ and reward institutions or enterprises with outstanding employment records.
⑥ The Mayor may implement the following projects to strengthen employment capabilities and support workplace adaptation of high school graduates:
1. Operation of on-site customized vocational education programs suited to regional industrial demand;
2. Support for continuing education and degree acquisition after employment;
3. Support for workplace mentoring programs;
4. Support for conclusion of employment-linked agreements between high schools and enterprises.
⑦ Matters necessary for formulating and implementing policies under paragraphs ① through ⑥ shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 341 (Special provisions linking regional hub campuses of national universities to strategic industries)
① To strengthen linkages with regional strategic and emerging industries, the State and the Integrated Special City may provide special provisions concerning research, demonstration and industry-academia cooperation at regional hub campuses of national universities as prescribed by Presidential Decree, notwithstanding the Higher Education Act, the National Research and Development Innovation Act and other relevant statutes.
② The State and the Integrated Special City may support the integrated operation of field practice, testing, demonstration and retraining courses linked to fishing grounds, aquaculture farms, ports, coastal areas and marine protected areas for education, research and industry linkages in fisheries and marine-related fields at regional hub campuses of national universities. In such cases, special provisions necessary for use for educational and research purposes may be provided within the scope prescribed by Presidential Decree, notwithstanding the Fisheries Act, the Fishing Villages and Fishery Harbors Act, the Marine Environment Management Act and other relevant statutes.

Article 342 (Support for attracting global talent to departments linked to regional strategic industries)
① The State shall actively implement the following matters to attract international students for fostering regional strategic industries in the Integrated Special City:
1. Holding international events jointly organized by the Government, local governments and enterprises to attract international students;
2. Operating delegations for overseas job fairs and intergovernmental cooperation;
3. Securing budgets and personnel to attract international students;
4. Other government-wide cooperative support activities necessary to attract international students.
② The Integrated Special City may implement the following projects to support international students in settling stably in the region, and the State shall endeavor to support such projects:
1. Payment of various subsidies, including education and training subsidies linked to local employment;
2. Support for establishing and operating local residential and living facilities;
3. Other projects to improve local settlement conditions for international students.

Article 343 (Support for and promotion of talent employment)
① To attract talent to future emerging industries and stabilize employment, the Mayor may implement the following projects or support all or part of the expenses necessary therefor:
1. Operation of employment-linked internship and field practice programs involving local universities, research institutes and enterprises;
2. Establishment of customized vocational training, career development consulting and job matching systems for persons seeking employment in future emerging industries;
3. Employment promotion incentives, wage subsidies or social insurance premium support for enterprises newly recruiting local talent;
4. Other matters prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance to promote employment and long-term retention of talent.
② When local public enterprises or invested or contributed institutions, etc. conduct procurement bids for projects, construction or goods, the Mayor may give preferential treatment to enterprises employing at least a prescribed percentage of talent in future emerging industries within the region.
③ Matters necessary for the support criteria under paragraphs ① and ② shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 344 (Housing and settlement support for outstanding talent)
① To enable outstanding talent in future emerging industries to settle stably, the Mayor may provide special allocations of housing as prescribed by Presidential Decree notwithstanding Article 54 of the Housing Act: Provided, That the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport may restrict the methods of housing supply in areas at risk of speculation prescribed by Presidential Decree.
② The Mayor may implement housing expense support policies, including free rental of rental housing for a specified period to key talent meeting criteria prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance, or give priority to supplying rental housing in accordance with criteria and procedures separately determined following consultation with the Minister of Land, Infrastructure and Transport.
③ The State may support part of the financial resources necessary for housing support policies under paragraphs ① and ②.

Article 345 (Support for improvements to educational environments to retain outstanding talent)
The Mayor and the Superintendent of Education may attract outstanding schools or provide special support payments for improving educational environments in areas near future emerging industry complexes or research and development special zones.

Article 346 (Special provisions concerning promotion of democratic citizenship education)
① The Superintendent of Education shall systematically conduct democratic citizenship education so that students inherit the righteous historical identity and constitutional spirit of Honam, characterized by the resistance of righteous armies during the Imjin and Jeongyu invasions, the Donghak Peasant Revolution, resistance armies in the late Korean Empire, the Student Independence Movement, the Yeosu-Suncheon October 19 Incident, the April 19 Revolution and the May 18 Democratization Movement, which constitute the historical distinctiveness of the Jeonnam-Gwangju region, and develop into citizens who respect the fundamental principles and values of democracy and practice peace and human rights.
② The Superintendent of Education shall establish a basic plan for democratic citizenship education in schools of the Integrated Special City every four years, including the following matters, and prepare a detailed annual implementation plan:
1. Development of educational materials linked to the history of democracy in Jeonnam-Gwangju (including the Yeosu-Suncheon October 19 Incident and May 18 Democratization Movement);
2. Operation and support of experiential and participatory educational programs appropriate to developmental stages at each school level;
3. Support for training and research to strengthen teachers' capacity to teach democratic citizenship;
4. Establishment of networks for democratic citizenship education and entrusted projects, etc. through cooperation with relevant local organizations and civil society.
③ To establish plans and deliberate on policies under paragraph ②, a Democratic Citizenship Education Committee for Schools of the Integrated Special City may be established under the Superintendent of Education. The Superintendent may appoint or commission members from among persons with extensive knowledge and experience, including educational experts and persons affiliated with local democratization movement organizations.
④ Heads of schools at each level within the Integrated Special City shall formulate and implement annual school-specific democratic citizenship education plans based on autonomy in the operation of curricula, and the Superintendent of Education may provide necessary administrative and financial support.

CHAPTER V OTHER MATTERS

Article 347 (Special provisions for fostering traditional markets and shopping districts)
① The Mayor may establish a basic plan for revitalizing traditional markets and shopping districts in the Integrated Special City and support the following projects. The State may provide administrative and financial support:
1. Support for revitalizing shopping districts;
2. Support for revitalizing neighborhood-type shopping districts;
3. Support for weekend markets;
4. Designation, fostering and cancellation of culture and tourism-oriented markets;
5. Support for establishing stores directly operated by farmers and fishers;
6. Fostering young merchants;
7. Promoting utilization of vacant stores;
8. Support for revitalizing commercial districts;
9. Support for projects modernizing commercial infrastructure;
10. Promotion of market improvement projects.
② To establish the basic plan under paragraph ①, the Mayor may request necessary data from the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and local governments.
③ Upon establishing the basic plan under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall notify the Sis, Guns and Gus within the Integrated Special City.
④ Matters necessary for establishing and implementing the basic plan under paragraph ①, other than those prescribed in paragraphs ① through ③, shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 348 (Special provisions concerning reduction or exemption of charges for use of State and public land)
The Government and the Mayor may reduce or exempt for ten years charges for the use of State or public land for common facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree within markets and projects modernizing facilities, as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 349 (Promotion of culture and the arts)
① To eliminate cultural disparities among regions and develop distinctive local cultures, the Mayor shall establish and implement a culture and arts promotion plan (hereinafter referred to as a "promotion plan") every five years.
② A promotion plan shall include:
1. Basic policies and plans concerning promotion of culture and the arts;
2. Support for cultural and artistic activities and fostering of cultural industries;
3. Expansion and improvement of cultural and artistic facilities;
4. Transmission and development of traditional culture and the arts;
5. Discovery and promotion of local culture and the arts;
6. Promotion of cultural and artistic exchanges and globalization;
7. Matters required to be reflected in implementation plans under Article 6 (4) of the Regional Culture Promotion Act;
8. Other matters necessary for promotion of culture and the arts.
③ To establish a promotion plan, the Mayor may request relevant data from the heads of central administrative agencies and local governments.
④ A promotion plan shall undergo deliberation by the City/Do Regional Culture Cooperation Committee under Article 6-2 of the Regional Culture Promotion Act.
⑤ Where necessary to promote culture in the Integrated Special City, the State may provide budgetary support to persons implementing cultural promotion projects.
⑥ The portions of a promotion plan reflecting matters under paragraph ② 7 shall be deemed an implementation plan for regional culture promotion under Article 6 (4) of the Regional Culture Promotion Act.

Article 350 (Establishment of regional culture promotion hubs)
Notwithstanding Articles 13-3 (1) and 13-4 (1) of the Regional Culture Promotion Act, the Mayor may designate and revoke designation of institutions dedicated to regional culture promotion to expand opportunities to enjoy culture and ensure balanced cultural development within the Integrated Special City. In such cases, the Mayor shall consult with the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism in advance.

Article 351 (Special provisions concerning designation of cultural districts)
① Notwithstanding the Regional Culture Promotion Act, the Mayor may designate the following areas as cultural districts to promote culture and the arts and revitalize tourism:
1. Areas with a concentration of cultural facilities under the Culture and Arts Promotion Act;
2. Sites where relocation of military facilities has been confirmed and surrounding areas;
3. Areas with educational and cultural facilities installed in urban parks under the Act on Urban Parks and Green Areas.
② The State may provide administrative and financial support for successfully establishing cultural districts designated under paragraph ①.

Article 352 (Special provisions concerning designation of cultural industry promotion districts)
① Notwithstanding Article 28-2 (2) and (5) of the Framework Act on the Promotion of Cultural Industries, the Mayor may designate or cancel cultural industry promotion districts without obtaining approval from the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism. In such cases, the Mayor shall consult with the Minister in advance.
② To promote cultural industries within the Integrated Special City, the Mayor may establish and operate a dedicated institution undertaking:
1. Collection and provision of information necessary to promote cultural industries, attract enterprises and support occupancy;
2. Various forms of support for enterprises located within cultural industry promotion districts;
3. Promotion of projects combining cultural industries with new technologies;
4. Training of professionals in cultural industry promotion;
5. Other projects necessary to promote cultural industries.
③ The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary following designation of cultural industry promotion districts.

Article 353 (Special provisions concerning designation of cultural industry promotion facilities)
① Notwithstanding Articles 21 (1) and 22 of the Framework Act on the Promotion of Cultural Industries, the Mayor may designate or cancel designation of cultural industry promotion facilities. The Mayor shall consult in advance with the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism.
② Notwithstanding paragraph ①, approval from the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism shall be required for designation or cancellation of cultural industry promotion facilities by the Mayor in any of the following cases:
1. Where national funding is or is expected to be invested;
2. Where a public institution or an institution financed or invested in by the State participates.
③ The Mayor shall notify the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism without delay of the results of designation or cancellation under paragraph ①.
④ The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary for designation of cultural industry promotion facilities under paragraph ①.

Article 354 (Special provisions concerning international art transactions)
① To foster the Integrated Special City as a global art market hub, the Mayor may designate part of its jurisdiction as a free international art trading zone.
② The Ministry of Finance and Economy may take special financial measures, including relaxation or exemption of reporting obligations for foreign exchange transactions relating to art trading within a free zone under paragraph ①.

Article 355 (Special provisions concerning feasibility assessment for establishment of public museums and art galleries)
① Where the Mayor intends to establish a public museum or public art gallery under Article 3 (1) 2 and Article 3 (2) of the Museum and Art Gallery Support Act, the Mayor shall, notwithstanding Article 12-2 of the same Act, establish an establishment and operation plan and conduct a preliminary review of feasibility for establishment (hereinafter referred to as a "preliminary review").
② Matters necessary for procedures and methods of preliminary reviews shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 356 (Special provisions concerning sports facilities and support for international sports events)
① The authority of the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism under Article 10-2 (2) of the Installation and Utilization of Sports Facilities Act shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism under Articles 7 (2) and 8 (3) of the Installation and Utilization of Sports Facilities Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 357 (Fostering and promotion of the tourism industry)
① The State shall pursue improvements to relevant statutes so that the Integrated Special City can implement tourism policies autonomously and shall consider promotion of tourism in the Integrated Special City when formulating tourism promotion plans and implementing projects.
② The Integrated Special City shall contribute to national tourism promotion by establishing tourism conditions, developing tourism resources and fostering tourism industries in the region autonomously and responsibly.
③ Where necessary in formulating nationwide tourism policies and in connection with tourist safety, consumer protection and tourism standards, the State may request cooperation from the Integrated Special City.

Article 358 (Special provisions concerning designation of tourist destinations)
Notwithstanding Article 52 of the Tourism Promotion Act, the Mayor may designate tourist destinations, etc. without prior consultation with the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism.

Article 359 (Special provisions concerning development plans for tourist destinations)
Notwithstanding Articles 55, 56 and 58 of the Tourism Promotion Act, Articles 156 through 158 of this Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to implementation and loss of effect of development plans for tourist destinations and tourist complexes not implemented as development projects under Article 150 (2) 18 and to authorization and permission, etc. where approval or approval of changes has been obtained.

Article 360 (Special provisions concerning fostering tourism in population-declining areas)
① The Mayor shall endeavor to revitalize population-declining areas by giving priority to fostering tourism industries in areas with outstanding specialized tourism resources, including rural and marine tourism resources, within population-declining areas under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Special Act on Support for Areas with Declining Populations.
② To foster tourism under paragraph ①, the Mayor may give priority to implementing projects to establish integrated resort complexes, including cultural, sports and recreation facilities, within population-declining areas.
③ The State may provide administrative and financial support for fostering tourism in population-declining areas and areas of concern for population decline.
④ Where necessary for development projects under paragraph ②, the Mayor may provide necessary support, including tax reductions or exemptions, as prescribed by local tax statutes.
⑤ Matters concerning eligible recipients and scope of support under paragraph ③ shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 361 (Special provisions concerning registration of news agencies)
① The authority of the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism under Articles 8 (1) and (2), 9 (5), 9-3 (1), (2), (5) and (7), 9-5 (1) and (2), and 37 (2) (limited to imposition and collection of administrative fines concerning transferred powers) of the News Agency Promotion Act shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City. Notwithstanding Article 9-4 (1) of the same Act, a Registration Cancellation Deliberation Committee shall be established under the Mayor.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under the former part of the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 8 (1) (limited to Presidential Decrees concerning registration of news agencies), Article 8 (1) 6, Article 9-4 (2), Article 9-5 (1), and Article 37 (2) of the News Agency Promotion Act (limited to imposition and collection of administrative fines concerning transferred powers) may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 362 (Special provisions concerning registration of newspapers, etc.)
① The authority of the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism under Article 28 (1), the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 28 (2), and Article 39 (3) of the Act on the Promotion of Newspapers, etc. (limited to imposition and collection of administrative fines concerning transferred powers) shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under the main sentence and proviso to the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 9 (1), Article 24 (2), Article 28 (1) and Article 39 (3) of the Act on the Promotion of Newspapers, etc. (limited to imposition and collection of administrative fines concerning transferred powers) may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 363 (Special provisions concerning foreign artists and employees of tourism businesses)
Notwithstanding Articles 8 and 10-2 of the Immigration Act, at the request of the Mayor of the Integrated Special City, the Minister of Justice may separately prescribe visa issuance procedures and maximum periods of stay granted on each occasion by status of stay for artists operating within districts or special zones prescribed by Presidential Decree and foreigners working for tourism businesses under the Tourism Promotion Act.

Article 364 (Special provisions concerning the Tourism Promotion Act)
① The authority of the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism under Articles 8 (4), 35 through 40 (excluding Article 35 (1) 9-2), 47 (1), and 77 of the Tourism Promotion Act (excluding authority concerning casino businesses) shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City.
② Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree or Ordinance of the Ministry of Culture, Sports and Tourism under Article 3 (1) 3 (b), Article 3 (2) (excluding campgrounds), Article 4 (3) through (5), Article 5 (2) and (4), Article 6 (1) and (2), Article 9, Article 10 (1) and (4), Article 12, Article 13 (1) and (5), Article 15 (1) through (3), the proviso to the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 16 (5), Article 16 (5) 2, Article 17 (1), the proviso to Article 17 (4), Article 17 (6), Article 20 (1), Article 20 (2) 1, the proviso to Article 20 (2) 2, Article 20 (4), the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 20 (5), Article 20 (5) 7, the main sentence of Article 31 (1), the former part of Article 33 (1), Article 33 (5) (excluding the content, duration and methods of safety education), Article 34 (1), Article 35 (1) 8, the main sentence of Article 38 (1), the main sentence and proviso to Article 38 (2), the main sentence of the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 40, Article 48 (2), the main sentence of Article 52 (1), the latter part of Article 52 (5), and the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 79 of the Tourism Promotion Act (excluding matters concerning casino businesses) may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 365 (Special provisions concerning the Integrated Special City Tourism Promotion and Development Fund)
① Notwithstanding Article 2 (1) of the Tourism Promotion and Development Fund Act, the Mayor shall establish the Integrated Special City Tourism Promotion and Development Fund to efficiently develop tourism businesses and contribute to increasing foreign currency revenues from tourism.
② The Fund under paragraph ① shall be financed by contributions from the Integrated Special City.

Article 366 (Management and operation of the Integrated Special City Tourism Promotion and Development Fund)
① The Integrated Special City Tourism Promotion and Development Fund shall be managed by the Mayor.
② Matters necessary for management of the Fund, including employment of private-sector experts, shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ The Mayor shall annually establish and implement a fund operation plan in accordance with the Framework Act on Local Government Fund Management.

Article 367 (Application mutatis mutandis of the Tourism Promotion and Development Fund Act)
Except as provided in this Act or Integrated Special City ordinances, the Tourism Promotion and Development Fund Act shall apply mutatis mutandis to the Integrated Special City Tourism Promotion and Development Fund. In such cases, "Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism" shall be construed as "Mayor of the Integrated Special City", and "Presidential Decree" as "Integrated Special City ordinance".

Article 368 (Special provisions concerning special tourist zones)
Notwithstanding Article 70 of the Tourism Promotion Act, the Mayor may designate, cancel or alter special tourist zones without prior consultation with the Minister of Culture, Sports and Tourism.

Article 369 (Designation and operation of outstanding tourism business operators)
① The Mayor may operate a system for designating outstanding tourism business operators to improve the quality of tourism businesses and their services.
② Matters necessary for designation and operation of outstanding tourism business operators under paragraph ① may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 370 (Establishment of special accounts for cultural regeneration)
① The Mayor shall establish an Integrated Special City Special Account for Cultural Regeneration to regenerate idle spaces, facilities, etc. for which regeneration is deemed necessary into integrated cultural and artistic spaces.
② The State may support part of the expenses incurred in implementing projects under paragraph ①.

Article 371 (Special provisions concerning establishment of cultural promotion funds)
① To support the flourishing of culture and the arts, expansion of cultural infrastructure and development of content, the Mayor may establish and operate the Integrated Special City Cultural Promotion Fund (hereinafter referred to as the "Fund" in this Article).
② The Fund shall be financed by:
1. Transfers from the general account of the Integrated Special City;
2. Donations from individuals or corporations under Article 22 (3) of the Regional Culture Promotion Act;
3. Income from operation of the Fund.
③ The Fund shall be used for:
1. Support for region-specific arts festivals and global marketing;
2. Support for creation and production by local artists;
3. Culture and arts education projects for citizens of the Integrated Special City;
4. Other cultural promotion projects deemed necessary by the Mayor.
④ The duration of the Fund shall be 20 years; where continued implementation of projects is necessary, it may be extended as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑤ Where a culture and arts promotion fund established under relevant statutes or ordinances existed before this Act entered into force, that fund may be separately managed and operated while maintaining its former purposes and operational system, without being integrated into the new Fund established under this Act.

Article 372 (Designation of local culture and tourism districts)
① Where necessary to discover, maintain, preserve, inherit and develop local culture and promote tourism, the Mayor may designate and foster local culture and tourism districts as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② A person seeking designation as a local culture and tourism district under paragraph ① shall prepare a development plan and obtain approval from the Mayor as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. The same shall apply to amendments.
③ The Mayor may provide support for infrastructure needed to establish local culture and tourism districts, including roads, water supply, sewage, communications and energy supply facilities.

Article 373 (Establishment of tourism development plans)
① To efficiently develop and manage tourism resources, the Mayor shall establish a tourism development plan for the Integrated Special City (hereinafter referred to as a "tourism development plan" in this Article) as part of a comprehensive plan, including:
1. Tourism conditions and trends;
2. Demand for and supply of tourism;
3. Protection, development, utilization and management of tourism resources;
4. Development, improvement and supplementation of tourist destinations and complexes;
5. Linkages among tourist destinations;
6. Promotion of tourism businesses;
7. Environmental conservation;
8. Other matters necessary for development and management of tourism resources.
② Matters necessary for implementing tourism development plans may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 374 (Special provisions concerning establishment of the Integrated Special City Climate Response Fund)
① The Mayor shall establish the Integrated Special City Climate Response Fund to respond to climate change and promote the transition to carbon neutrality.
② The Fund under paragraph ① shall be financed by:
1. Transfers from the general account of the Integrated Special City;
2. Grants for collection expenses of environmental improvement charges under the Environmental Improvement Cost Allocation Act;
3. Grants for collection expenses of emission charges under the Clean Air Conservation Act and the Water Environment Conservation Act;
4. Grants for collection expenses of groundwater usage charges under the Groundwater Act;
5. Income from operating the Integrated Special City Climate Response Fund;
6. Other income.

Article 375 (Special provisions concerning cancellation or reduction of designation of provincial parks)
Notwithstanding Article 4-3 (2) of the Natural Parks Act, the Mayor may cancel designation of a provincial park or reduce its area following consultation with the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment.

Article 376 (Special provisions concerning designation and management of conservation resources)
① The Mayor may designate and manage resources deemed rare or of high conservation value as conservation resources, as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② When designating conservation resources under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall publicly notify the designation without delay as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ Where necessary to protect conservation resources, the Mayor may prohibit their capture, cutting, collection or damage, require reporting, prohibit disclosure or relocation, order removal of obstacles, or take other necessary measures as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
④ Where necessary to protect conservation resources, the Mayor may bear or subsidize expenses necessary for their management or protection.
⑤ A person wishing to sell or purchase conservation resources within the Integrated Special City or transport them outside its jurisdiction shall obtain permission from the Mayor as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑥ The Mayor shall compensate persons suffering losses due to dispositions under paragraph ③.
⑦ Other detailed matters concerning management of conservation resources shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 377 (Establishment of environmental conservation cooperation funds)
① To raise financial resources necessary for proactive conservation and management of environmental and ecological resources in the Integrated Special City, the Mayor shall establish an environmental conservation cooperation fund as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② The Fund under paragraph ① shall be financed by the following sources, limited, for subparagraphs 1 through 5, to amounts accruing to the Integrated Special City:
1. Penalty surcharges and administrative fines under the Sewerage Act;
