2. Grants for collection expenses of environmental improvement charges under the Environmental Improvement Cost Allocation Act;
3. Grants for collection expenses of emission charges under the Clean Air Conservation Act;
4. Grants for collection expenses of emission charges under the Water Environment Conservation Act;
5. Administrative fines imposed on persons violating environmental statutes, including the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, Clean Air Conservation Act and Water Environment Conservation Act;
6. Transfers from the general account and other special accounts of the Integrated Special City.
③ The State may provide financial support to the environmental conservation cooperation fund under paragraph ①.

Article 378 (Special provisions concerning forest culture, recreation and welfare)
① The authority of the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service under Articles 13 (2) through (4), 14 (3), 16 (2) through (4), 19 (1) and (2), 20 (4) and 21 (2) through (4) of the Forest Culture and Recreation Act (limited to public or private forests designated as natural recreation forests) shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City: Provided, That the Mayor shall notify the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service at least once each year of the status of designation of natural recreation forests and approval of development plans for the relevant year.
② The authority of the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service under Articles 27 (1) through (4), 29 (1) and (2), 33 (1), 35 (1), (2), (4) and (5), 36, 37 (2), 47 (1) and (2), and 48 (1) through (5) of the Forest Welfare Promotion Act (limited to public or private forests) shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City: Provided, That the Mayor shall notify the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service at least once each year of the status of designation of forest welfare districts, development of forest welfare complexes, approval of implementation plans, etc. for the relevant year. <Amended on 2026.5.12>
③ To process affairs transferred to the Mayor under paragraph ②, a Forest Welfare Deliberation Committee shall be established under the Mayor to deliberate on:
1. Designation and cancellation of forest welfare districts;
2. Approval of development plans and implementation plans for forest welfare complexes.
The composition and operation of the Forest Welfare Deliberation Committee shall be governed by the Forest Welfare Promotion Act.
④ Deliberation by the Forest Welfare Deliberation Committee under paragraph ③ shall be deemed deliberation by the Forest Welfare Deliberation Committee under Article 8 of the Forest Welfare Promotion Act for affairs transferred to the Mayor under paragraph ②.

Article 379 (Special provisions concerning designation of mountain village revitalization support centers)
Notwithstanding Article 27-3 of the Forestry and Mountain Villages Development Promotion Act, the authority of the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service shall be vested in the Mayor of the Integrated Special City. In such cases, the Mayor shall independently provide administrative and financial support comparable to the level of nationally designated centers.

Article 380 (Designation of forest use promotion districts)
① To promote forest utilization and encourage related private investment, the Mayor may designate an area satisfying all of the following requirements as a forest use promotion district (hereinafter referred to as a "promotion district"):
1. The area is at least 30,000 square meters and suitable for the purpose of designation, utilization plan and surrounding conditions;
2. Forest resources and landscapes in the area have sufficient potential as resources for promoting forest use;
3. The area serves the public interest by contributing to regional development, such as regional economic revitalization and development of underdeveloped areas;
4. Projects can be implemented in an environmentally and ecologically sustainable manner;
5. Projects do not pose a risk of disasters, including landslides and soil runoff;
6. Investment plans for forest use promotion projects are feasible;
7. Other requirements prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance are satisfied.
② To designate a promotion district, the Mayor shall establish a development plan for the promotion district under Article 381, consult with the heads of relevant administrative agencies (including the Administrator of the Korea Forest Service; hereinafter the same shall apply in paragraph ③), including consultation on strategic environmental impact assessment under Article 16 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act, and obtain deliberation by the Basic Plan Deliberation Council.
③ Upon designating a promotion district, the Mayor shall publicly notify the details as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance and notify the heads of relevant administrative agencies. Public notification of topographical maps shall be governed by Article 8 of the Framework Act on the Regulation of Land Use.
④ The Mayor shall make the details notified under paragraph ③ available for public inspection for at least 14 days.
⑤ Paragraphs ② through ④ shall apply to alterations of the location, boundaries, area, etc. of a promotion district: Provided, That they shall not apply to minor alterations prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
⑥ The State, Integrated Special City and Sis, Guns and Gus shall minimize uncontrolled development within promotion districts and ensure harmony and balance between the conservation and use of mountainous districts and forests, and shall formulate policies necessary to achieve the purposes of designation.
⑦ Where necessary to investigate whether a project is implemented in accordance with details publicly notified under paragraph ③, the Mayor may require an implementer of forest use promotion projects designated under Article 383 to submit relevant materials.
⑧ The Mayor may request the heads of relevant central administrative agencies, government-funded institutions and government-invested institutions to provide data and statistics necessary to analyze efficient management of promotion districts and impacts on the regional economy.
⑨ Where a promotion district ceases to meet requirements under any subparagraph of paragraph ①, the Mayor may cancel its designation following deliberation by the Basic Plan Deliberation Council.
⑩ Procedures, methods and management concerning designation, alteration or cancellation of promotion districts shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 381 (Development plans for promotion districts)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City shall establish a development plan for a promotion district (hereinafter referred to as a "promotion district development plan") before designating the district.
② A promotion district development plan shall include:
1. Name, location and area of the promotion district;
2. Methods and period of implementation of forest use promotion projects;
3. Purpose of designation and development direction of the district;
4. Land use and traffic management plans;
5. Plans for installing major infrastructure, including roads, water supply, sewerage and electricity, including plans for sharing costs;
6. Ecological, landscape and environmental conservation plans and pollution prevention plans;
7. Safety and disaster measures and rescue and emergency response plans;
8. Plans for sharing costs of arterial facilities, etc. installed outside the promotion district;
9. Matters concerning use, supply and disposal of developed land, etc.;
10. Compensation plans, including relocation measures;
11. Detailed lists of land, etc. subject to expropriation or use;
12. Financing and annual investment plans;
13. Other matters prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ When establishing a promotion district development plan, the Mayor shall hear the opinions of heads of Sis, Guns and Gus, local residents and experts in advance as prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 382 (Deemed authorization and permission following designation of promotion districts)
① When a promotion district is designated and publicly notified, designation, establishment, alteration or determination under the following subparagraphs shall be deemed made on the date of public notification in accordance with the details publicly notified under Article 383 (3), limited to matters consulted on in advance with the heads of the administrative agencies responsible for authorization and permission (including completion of deliberation or opinion-hearing procedures under relevant statutes):
1. Designation of urban development zones under Article 3 of the Urban Development Act and establishment of urban development project plans under Article 4 of that Act;
2. Designation of housing site development districts under Article 3 of the Housing Site Development Promotion Act and establishment of housing site development plans under Article 8 of that Act;
3. Designation of national industrial complexes, general industrial complexes and urban high-tech industrial complexes under Articles 6, 7 and 7-2 of the Industrial Sites and Development Act (limited to designation for fostering environmentally friendly and high-tech industries);
4. Designation of tourist destinations and tourism complexes under Article 52 of the Tourism Promotion Act;
5. Amendment of master plans for reclamation under Articles 22 and 27 of the Public Waters Management and Reclamation Act;
6. Determination of river zones under Article 10 of the River Act and amendment of river master plans under Article 25 of that Act (limited to local rivers under the River Act);
7. Amendment of waterworks improvement plans under Article 5 of the Water Supply and Waterworks Installation Act;
8. Amendment of master plans for sewerage improvement under Articles 5 and 6 of the Sewerage Act (limited to changes other than important matters prescribed by the Minister of Climate, Energy and Environment under Article 6 (1) of the Sewerage Act).
② Except as provided in paragraph ①, Articles 24 through 26 of the Framework Act on Administration shall apply mutatis mutandis to criteria and effects of deemed designations, etc.

Article 383 (Designation of implementers of forest use promotion projects)
① The Mayor shall designate implementers of forest use promotion projects from among the following persons in accordance with criteria and procedures prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance:
1. Local governments;
2. Public institutions prescribed by Presidential Decree among public institutions under Article 4 of the Act on the Management of Public Institutions;
3. Local public corporations established under the Local Public Enterprises Act;
4. Private investors meeting qualification requirements, including capital, prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance;
5. Corporations established through investment by at least two persons falling under subparagraphs 1 through 4 for the purpose of implementing forest use promotion projects and meeting requirements prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance;
6. Associations established by landowners within promotion districts for the purpose of implementing forest use promotion projects.
② When intending to designate an implementer under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall consider:
1. Financial soundness and ability to raise funds;
2. Experience in implementing development projects similar to forest use promotion projects;
3. Other matters deemed necessary by the Mayor for smooth implementation of forest use promotion projects and publicly notified.
③ Upon designating an implementer under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall publicly notify the designation in the public bulletin.

Article 384 (Revocation and replacement of designation of forest use promotion project implementers)
① Where an implementer of forest use promotion projects falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Mayor may revoke its designation under Article 383: Provided, That the Mayor shall revoke the designation where subparagraph 1 applies:
1. Where designation or approval under this Act was obtained by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where construction or a project has not commenced within one year after approval of an implementation plan under Article 385 (1);
3. Where approval of an implementation plan under Article 385 (1) has been revoked;
4. Where an application for approval of an implementation plan has not been made by the deadline under Article 385 (5);
5. Where the purposes of a forest use promotion project are deemed difficult to achieve due to a natural disaster, bankruptcy of the implementer or other grounds prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Upon revoking designation under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall publicly notify the revocation.
③ Where designation is revoked under paragraph ①, the Mayor may designate a new implementer in place of the former implementer. Article 383 shall apply mutatis mutandis to the replacement designation.
④ An implementer designated as a replacement under paragraph ③ shall succeed to the status of the former implementer regarding approval of implementation plans.

Article 385 (Establishment and approval of implementation plans for promotion districts)
① An implementer of forest use promotion projects shall prepare an implementation plan and obtain approval from the Mayor as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance. The same shall apply to amendments to an approved plan, except amendments to minor matters prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② An implementation plan shall include:
1. Name, location and area of the forest use promotion project;
2. Objectives and direction of implementation;
3. Plans for securing and using land;
4. Matters concerning district-unit plans prepared under Article 52 of the National Land Planning and Utilization Act;
5. Planned layout drawings and outline design documents;
6. Phased development plans, limited to projects requiring phased development due to project conditions;
7. Other matters prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
③ When intending to approve an implementation plan or amendments thereto (excluding minor amendments prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance), the Mayor shall consult with the heads of relevant administrative agencies and hear residents' opinions as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
④ Upon approving or approving amendments to an implementation plan, the Mayor shall publicly notify the approval as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance and send copies of the relevant documents to the heads of Sis, Guns and Gus. The heads receiving copies shall make the contents available for public inspection for at least 14 days.
⑤ An application for approval under the main sentence of paragraph ① shall be made within two years after the date of designation as an implementer of forest use promotion projects.

Article 386 (Special provisions concerning application of the Mountainous Districts Management Act within promotion districts)
① Notwithstanding Articles 12 and 18 of the Mountainous Districts Management Act, standards for restrictions on acts in conservation mountainous districts and permission to convert mountainous districts concerning gradients and elevation may be prescribed differently by Presidential Decree for forest use promotion projects.
② Notwithstanding Article 7 (2) of the Baekdudaegan Protection Act, a project implementer may undertake any of the following acts necessary to implement a forest use promotion project within the buffer zone of a promotion district:
1. Installing and improving hiking or trekking trails (including shelters, ecological bridges and observation facilities) under Article 7 (1) 4-2 of the Baekdudaegan Protection Act;
2. Establishing arboretums, natural recreation forests, healing forests and other public-interest forest facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree under Article 7 (2) 2 of the Baekdudaegan Protection Act;
3. Installing the minimum park facilities and implementing park projects permitted in park nature conservation districts under Article 18 (2) 1 (b) of the Natural Parks Act;
4. Constructing tracks under Article 2, subparagraph 1 of the Track Transportation Act.
③ Matters required to be prescribed by Presidential Decree under the proviso to the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 18 (2), the main sentence and proviso to the portion other than the subparagraphs of Article 23 (1), and the former and latter parts of Article 23 (4) of the Natural Parks Act may be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance: Provided, That the scope of such ordinances shall be limited to provincial and county parks within promotion districts.
④ Notwithstanding Article 11 (1) 1 of the Forest Protection Act, where the Mayor intends to use a forest protection area within a promotion district as a site for any of the following facilities, the Mayor may cancel all or part of its designation:
1. Facilities necessary for natural recreation forests under Article 14 (2) and (3) of the Forest Culture and Recreation Act;
2. Facilities necessary for forest bathing sites, healing forests, forest campsites and forest sports facilities under Article 20 of the Forest Culture and Recreation Act;
3. Facilities necessary for arboretums under Article 7 of the Arboretums and Gardens Act.
⑤ Forest protection areas whose designation may be canceled by the Mayor under paragraph ④ shall be limited to forests other than national forests managed by the Korea Forest Service that constitute living environment protection areas, landscape protection areas, water source cultivation protection areas and disaster prevention protection areas under Article 7 (1) 1 through 4 of the Forest Protection Act.

Article 387 (Support for installation of infrastructure)
① The State and the Integrated Special City may directly install roads and other facilities prescribed by Presidential Decree or support installation costs to facilitate forest use promotion projects and attract investment.
② Matters concerning beneficiaries and scope of support by the Integrated Special City under paragraph ① shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 388 (Completion inspections)
① Where a project implementer completes all or part of a forest use promotion project (limited, for partial completion, to where the approved implementation plan includes phased development plans under Article 385 (2) 6), the implementer shall prepare a project completion report and undergo a completion inspection by the Mayor as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
② Upon receipt of a project completion report under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall conduct a completion inspection without delay. Where necessary for efficiency, the Mayor may entrust the inspection to a relevant administrative agency, public institution, research institution or other specialized institution.
③ The designating authority may request the head of a state agency, local government or public institution that will take over or manage public facilities included in the project completion report under paragraph ① to participate in the completion inspection, and a person receiving such a request shall comply unless there is a special reason not to do so.
④ Where the Mayor determines from the completion inspection under paragraph ② that a forest use promotion project has been completed, the Mayor shall issue a certificate of completion inspection to the implementer and publicly announce completion of the project. Where the project has not been completed in accordance with the implementation plan, the Mayor shall order necessary measures, including supplementary construction, without delay.
⑤ When conducting a completion inspection under paragraph ②, where the Mayor has consulted with the heads of relevant administrative agencies under paragraph ⑦ concerning completion inspections, completion authorizations, etc. under authorization and permission deemed granted pursuant to Article 382, such completion inspections and authorizations shall be deemed obtained.
⑥ To obtain deemed completion inspection or authorization under paragraph ⑤, an implementer (excluding the Mayor where the Mayor is the implementer) shall submit the relevant documents required by the applicable Acts together with the application for completion inspection under paragraph ①.
⑦ When conducting a completion inspection under paragraph ②, the Mayor shall consult with the heads of relevant administrative agencies in advance where matters falling under completion inspections or authorizations under authorization and permission deemed granted pursuant to Article 382 are included.
⑧ Developed land or installed facilities shall not be used before completion inspection under paragraph ①.

Article 389 (Special provisions concerning development of underdeveloped areas within the Integrated Special City)
① The Mayor shall formulate and give priority to supporting policies to eliminate disparities and promote balanced development of underdeveloped areas within the Integrated Special City.
② Where the Mayor implements policies for balanced development of underdeveloped areas, the State may provide necessary administrative and financial support for those policies.

Article 390 (Support for cultural and tourism infrastructure)
① The Mayor shall facilitate priority installation or attraction of cultural facilities, including convention facilities, libraries, museums, art galleries, culture and arts centers and large performance venues, tourism, accommodation and entertainment facilities and sports facilities (hereinafter referred to as "cultural and tourism facilities") to promote culture and tourism.
② The Mayor may grant authorization or permission, etc. or provide administrative and financial support to persons intending to establish or relocate cultural and tourism facilities within the Integrated Special City under paragraph ①.

Article 391 (Establishment of a historical and cultural hub city)
① The Integrated Special City shall formulate and implement necessary policies and actively endeavor to develop into a center of the history and culture of Mahan, Later Baekje and Gaya.
② The Integrated Special City may provide administrative and financial support for historical and cultural surveys and research concerning Mahan, Later Baekje and Gaya, fostering performance, history, tradition, culture, the arts and tourism projects, and establishing facilities and spaces for people to enjoy history and culture.

Article 392 (Designation of special historical and cultural zones)
① To inherit and develop historical identity, the Mayor may designate certain areas within the jurisdiction of the Integrated Special City as special historical and cultural zones (hereinafter referred to as "special zones") serving as historical and cultural hubs.
② When designating a special zone, the Mayor shall consult with the heads of central administrative agencies responsible for the Act on the Conservation and Utilization of Cultural Heritage, the Act on the Safeguarding and Promotion of Intangible Heritage, and other relevant statutes.
③ The following projects may be promoted with priority within special zones:
1. Systematic conservation and transmission of national heritage and traditional culture;
2. Protection and utilization of historical and cultural assets and their spiritual values;
3. Concentration and revitalization of intangible heritage, traditional arts and folk culture;
4. Strengthening tourism, education and research functions based on history and culture.
④ A consultative body involving relevant central administrative agencies may be established and operated for the efficient operation of special zones.

Article 393 (Special provisions concerning special zones)
① Notwithstanding the Act on the Conservation and Utilization of Cultural Heritage, the Act on the Safeguarding and Promotion of Intangible Heritage and other relevant statutes, the Integrated Special City may apply special provisions for conservation and utilization of national heritage and historical and cultural assets within special zones.
② Where necessary for establishing and operating special zones, the Integrated Special City may, notwithstanding the State Property Act and the Public Property and Commodity Management Act, permit persons prescribed by Presidential Decree to use or profit from State or public property through negotiated contracts, or reduce or exempt usage fees as prescribed by relevant statutes.
③ The scope and procedures of special provisions applicable to special zones shall be prescribed by Presidential Decree.

Article 394 (Special provisions concerning creation of national industrial complexes for convergence of artificial intelligence and cultural content)
① The State may provide administrative and financial support necessary to perform research and development of convergence technologies for the development of cultural industries based on exchanges and convergence among scientific, technological, design, cultural, artistic, humanities and social science disciplines within the Integrated Special City.
② The Minister of Science and ICT may support all or part of the expenses necessary to establish next-generation digital infrastructure within national industrial complexes, including next-generation mobile communications networks, high-performance computing centers and data centers dedicated to artificial intelligence-based creation.
③ Enterprises engaging in immersive content, generative artificial intelligence creation, games, video, webtoons, animation and future cultural technologies may be attracted to national industrial complexes, and local taxes, etc. may be reduced or exempted as prescribed by the Restriction of Special Local Taxation Act.
④ To promote demonstration and commercialization of artificial intelligence convergence content services developed by enterprises located in national industrial complexes, the Mayor may designate and operate a culture industry regulation-free special zone in which regulations are suspended or exempted for a specified period as prescribed by relevant statutes: Provided, That this shall apply only where procedures under Articles 72 through 75 of the Act on Special Cases concerning Regulation of Regulation-Free Special Zones and Special Economic Zones for Specialized Regional Development are applied mutatis mutandis.

Article 395 (Special provisions concerning designation and development of global content tourism complexes)
① To foster the content industry and create an international tourism hub, the Mayor may designate a global content tourism complex following consultation on strategic environmental impact assessment under Article 16 of the Environmental Impact Assessment Act.
② For a tourism complex designated under paragraph ①, changes to use districts and relaxation of restrictions on building coverage ratios and floor-area ratios may apply as prescribed by the National Land Planning and Utilization Act, Building Act and other relevant statutes.
③ The Mayor may construct cultural facilities under the Culture and Arts Promotion Act, including integrated performance facilities for Korean Wave content, and the State may support part of the costs of their construction as prescribed by relevant statutes.
④ The Mayor may construct facilities related to cultural industries, including permanent esports stadiums and video production facilities, and the State may support their construction costs.
⑤ A tourism complex designated under paragraph ① shall be deemed a unit development project district within a free economic zone under the Special Act on Designation and Management of Free Economic Zones pursuant to its development plan (limited to cases where procedures under Article 4 (2) through (4) of that Act have been completed), and acquisition taxes of the project implementer shall be reduced or exempted as prescribed by the Restriction of Special Local Taxation Act.

Article 396 (Support for hosting international events)
The Government may designate the Integrated Special City as the venue for international events, including the G20 Summit and the 33rd Conference of the Parties to the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change (COP33).

Article 397 (Special provisions concerning designation of regional global medical tourism special zones)
① The Mayor may designate and foster the following global medical tourism special zones according to the characteristics of medical resources in each region:
1. Advanced medical zone: Artificial intelligence-based precision medicine, treatment of severe diseases, beauty and cosmetic surgery;
2. Wellness medical zone: Marine healing, rehabilitation medicine and integrated Korean medicine treatment;
3. Forest healing zone: Forest healing as prescribed by the Forest Culture and Recreation Act.
② The Mayor shall establish an international medical support center within global medical tourism special zones to provide integrated support throughout the process from entry into the Republic of Korea through medical treatment, recuperation, tourism and departure for foreign patients, and shall provide administrative convenience for issuing long-term residence visas to patients and guardians.

Article 398 (Special environmental regulatory provisions for island and coastal tourism development)
① The Mayor may designate environmentally friendly tourism promotion districts to develop tourism using the unique ecology and culture of islands and coastal areas.
② To expedite environmental reviews and prior impact consultations on national heritage for development projects within environmentally friendly tourism promotion districts, the Mayor shall establish and operate an Integrated Deliberation Committee involving public officials from the Ministry of Climate, Energy and Environment and other relevant agencies and private-sector experts. Deliberation by the Committee shall be deemed consultation with the relevant central administrative agencies.
③ To minimize environmental damage arising from development, the Mayor shall allocate a certain proportion of development profits to environmental restoration and ecosystem conservation funds.

Article 399 (Special provisions concerning designation and support of special island culture conservation zones)
① To conserve and transmit the unique historical and cultural values of islands and enhance sustainable competitiveness of island areas based on those values, the Mayor may designate certain areas as special island culture conservation zones (hereinafter referred to as "island special zones").
② The Mayor may give priority to the following projects within island special zones:
1. Recording and supporting transmission of distinctive island folk culture, intangible heritage and traditional ways of life;
2. Developing content based on island cultural assets and fostering island-specific tourism brands;
3. Improving island residents' settlement conditions and establishing infrastructure for sustainable ecotourism;
4. Expanding and operating cultural infrastructure, including island culture transmission centers and museums.
③ Where necessary to designate island special zones, the Mayor shall consult with the heads of relevant central administrative agencies and establish a comprehensive plan for operating such zones.
④ The Mayor may provide financial support necessary for smooth implementation of projects.

Article 400 (Promotion of and support for water circulation)
① Where the Integrated Special City requests support for projects including facilities specified in the items of Article 2, subparagraph 3 of the Act on the Promotion of and Support for Water Circulation and other facilities deemed necessary by the Mayor to promote water circulation, the State may give priority to designating an area as a water circulation promotion zone under Article 6 of that Act.
② The State may support expenses necessary for projects implemented within a water circulation promotion zone designated under paragraph ①.

PART IV SUPPLEMENTARY PROVISIONS

Article 401 (Cooperation of public institutions)
① The Mayor of the Integrated Special City and the Superintendent of Education of the Integrated Special City may request cooperation in administrative affairs from public institutions under the Act on the Management of Public Institutions, etc. (limited to institutions located in the Integrated Special City; hereinafter referred to as "public institutions"). Public institutions shall cooperate unless there is a special reason not to do so.
② The Mayor and the Superintendent of Education may establish and operate development councils for individual sectors to facilitate cooperation with public institutions.
③ Matters concerning the scope of public institutions, cooperation under paragraphs ① and ②, and composition and operation of sectoral development councils shall be prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 402 (Supervision)
① Where a project implementer or business operator under this Act falls under any of the following subparagraphs, the Mayor may revoke authorization, approval, permission, registration or designation under this Act; suspend its effect; order suspension of construction; order rebuilding, alteration, relocation or demolition of buildings or artificial structures; or order other necessary measures: Provided, That where subparagraph 1 applies, the Mayor shall revoke the relevant authorization, approval, permission, registration or designation:
1. Where authorization, approval, permission, registration or designation under this Act was obtained by fraud or other improper means;
2. Where continuing implementation of a development project under this Act becomes impossible or is deemed likely to seriously harm the public interest due to changed circumstances.
② Where the Mayor orders a measure under paragraph ①, the Mayor shall publicly announce it as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.

Article 403 (Prevention of disadvantages to the status of public officials)
Public officials whose status changes under this Act shall be appointed to positions corresponding to their career experience, assigned duties and former positions and shall not otherwise suffer disadvantages in personnel matters.

Article 404 (Collection of administrative fines, etc. following transfers of authority)
Where the authority to impose or collect administrative fines, penalty surcharges, development charges and additional charges thereon, etc. (hereinafter referred to as "administrative fines, etc." in this Article) formerly vested in the heads of central administrative agencies is vested in the Mayor under this Act, delinquent administrative fines, etc. shall be collected pursuant to the Act on the Collection of Local Administrative Penalty Charges and Other Charges.

Article 405 (Deemed status as public officials for application of penal provisions)
Members of the Support Committee, Audit Committee, Integrated Special City Personnel Committee and Integrated Special City Office of Education Personnel Committee who are not public officials shall be deemed public officials for the purposes of applying penal provisions of the Criminal Act and other Acts to acts performed in connection with their duties.

PART V PENALTY PROVISIONS

Article 406 (Penalties concerning foreign educational institutions)
A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than three years or by a fine not exceeding 30 million won:
1. A person who, without obtaining approval for establishment under Article 73 (2), uses the name of a foreign educational institution or recruits students and actually operates facilities in the form of a foreign educational institution;
2. A person who obtains approval for establishment under Article 73 (2) by fraud or other improper means.

Article 407 (Penalties concerning the Audit Committee)
A person falling under any of the following subparagraphs shall be punished by imprisonment for not more than one year or by a fine not exceeding ten million won:
1. A person subject to an audit by the Audit Committee who refuses the audit or fails to comply with a request for submission of materials without justifiable grounds;
2. A person who obstructs auditing activities of an audit organization without justifiable grounds;
3. A person who violates the duty to maintain confidentiality under Article 94 (1).

Article 408 (Administrative fines)
① A person who fails to comply with a disposition or order issued by the Mayor under Article 402 (1) shall be subject to an administrative fine not exceeding ten million won.
② Administrative fines under paragraph ① shall be imposed and collected by the Mayor as prescribed by Integrated Special City ordinance.
